docs.title: Inferences Table
docs.text: # Claim Type What the Bible actually says Why this is an inference Criteria I1 The dead are in a conscious intermediate state between death and resurrection I-B E43 (2 Cor 5:8): Paul willing to be absent from body and present with Lord. E44 (Phil 1:23): Paul desires to depart and be with Christ. E45 (Luke 23:43): Jesus promises paradise to thief. AGAINST: E1-E13 (9+ OT texts: dead know nothing, thoughts perish, no praise, silence, darkness). E14 (David not ascended). E16 (without resurrection, dead perished). E27 (being with the Lord follows resurrection). Must choose between two readings of 2 Cor 5:8 / Phil 1:23 (immediate vs. subjective-instant-at-resurrection). Must override the plain meaning of E1-E13 and E16. Must import temporal immediacy not specified by the Greek aorist. I022 I2 The "under the sun" qualifier limits Ecclesiastes death-state statements to earthly perspective only, not absolute reality I-D E2 (Ecc 9:5): "the dead know not any thing." The phrase "under the sun" appears in Ecc 9:6 after the death-state statement. Requires adding a theological framework (earthly vs. heavenly perspective) that the text itself does not establish. The negation in v.5 is absolute: einam yodim meumah (they do not know anything). The qualifier "under the sun" in v.6 applies to "portion in anything done under the sun" -- what they have no portion IN, not a limitation on the scope of their unknowing. I003 I3 Death is merely "separation of soul from body," with the soul continuing consciously I-D E21 (Gen 2:7): man became a living soul. E17 (Ezek 18:4): the soul that sins shall die. E18 (Matt 10:28): soul can be destroyed. E19 (1 Tim 6:16): God alone has immortality. E22 (Ecc 12:7): spirit returns to God. The definition "separation of soul from body" does not appear in any biblical text. Must override E17 (soul dies), E18 (soul destroyed), E19 (God alone has immortality). Requires importing the concept of an inherently immortal, conscious soul -- a concept the text does not contain and multiple texts contradict. I002 I4 Paul's "desire to depart and be with Christ" (Phil 1:23) and "absent from body, present with Lord" (2 Cor 5:8) teach immediate conscious presence with Christ at death I-B FOR: E43 (2 Cor 5:8), E44 (Phil 1:23) -- Paul expresses preference for being with Christ over earthly life. AGAINST: E16 (1 Cor 15:18, same author: dead perished without resurrection). E26 (1 Cor 15:53-54, same author: immortality put on at resurrection). E37 (2 Tim 4:8, same author: crown at "that day," the appearing). Phil 3:11 (same letter: attaining resurrection). Phil 3:20-21 (same letter: future bodily transformation). Must choose between "immediate at death" and "subjective instant at resurrection." Must reconcile with E16 (dead perished without resurrection -- same author). The Greek grammar (aorist infinitives connected by kai) does not specify temporal relationship. I004 I5 The rich man and Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31) teaches literal afterlife geography I-D E41 (Luke 16:23): parabolic character in hades, in torments. Passage is within a parabolic discourse (Luke 15:3). Opening formula matches labeled parables (Luke 12:16, 16:1). "Abraham's bosom" appears only here. Stated point: "they have Moses and the prophets" (vv.29,31). Must override the genre identification (parable within parabolic discourse). Must treat unique vocabulary ("Abraham's bosom") as literal geography despite appearing nowhere else. Must ignore the stated teaching point. Must override same-author statements: David not ascended (Acts 2:34), Stephen fell asleep (Acts 7:60). I023 I6 Revelation 6:9-11 proves the dead are conscious because the souls "cry out" I-D E42 (Rev 6:9-11): souls under altar in apocalyptic vision. Gen 4:10: Abel's blood "cries" from ground. Rev 16:7: the altar itself speaks. Rev 20:4-5: same souls "lived" at first resurrection. Must override the genre (apocalyptic vision with symbolic elements throughout). Must treat "crying out" as literal consciousness while ignoring that Abel's blood also "cries" (Gen 4:10) and the altar speaks (Rev 16:7). Must ignore Rev 20:4-5 (same souls "lived" = came to life at resurrection, meaning they were not alive before). I024 I7 The OT and NT present a unified doctrine of unconscious death (soul sleep) as the state of all dead until resurrection I-A E1-E20, N1-N6: 20 Cond. E-items across 8+ OT authors and NT apostolic teaching. Death = sleep (7+ authors). Resurrection = the hope. Dead know nothing. Thoughts perish. No praise. Silence. David not ascended. Dead perished without resurrection. Systematizes 20+ E-items and 6 N-items into a comprehensive doctrinal statement. All components come from E/N tables. Only criterion #5 (systematizing) applies. I020 I8 The witch of Endor incident (1 Sam 28) proves the dead can communicate I-D 1 Sam 28:3-20: Saul consults a medium. Only the woman saw (vv.12-14). No new information beyond 1 Sam 15:28. God condemned the act (1 Chr 10:13). Comprehensive law against necromancy (Exo 22:18; Lev 19:31; 20:6,27; Deu 18:9-14). Must override the divine prohibition (God forbade and condemned the act). Must accept the medium's claim at face value despite Saul seeing nothing. Must override E1-E13 (dead unconscious). I025

docs.title: I-B Resolution: I1 -- The dead are in a conscious intermediate state
docs.text:
Step 1 -- Tension: - FOR: E43 (2 Cor 5:8), E44 (Phil 1:23), E45 (Luke 23:43) - AGAINST: E1-E13 (9+ OT texts), E14 (Acts 2:34), E15 (Heb 11:39-40), E16 (1 Cor 15:18), E19 (1 Tim 6:16), E27 (1 Thess 4:16-17), E28 (John 6:39-40), N1-N2, N4-N6

Step 2 -- Clarity Assessment:

Item Level Rationale E1 (Psa 146:4) Plain Directly addresses death: thoughts perish. No interpretation needed. E2 (Ecc 9:5) Plain Directly states: the dead know nothing. Absolute negation. E4 (Ecc 9:10) Plain Directly states: no knowledge in sheol. Names the location. E5 (Psa 6:5) Plain Directly states: no remembrance in death/sheol. E6 (Psa 115:17) Plain Directly states: dead praise not, go to silence. E9 (Job 14:21) Plain Directly states: dead know not whether sons prosper. E14 (Acts 2:34) Plain Directly states: David is NOT ascended. Unambiguous negation. E16 (1 Cor 15:18) Plain Directly states: without resurrection, dead have perished. Reductio argument. E19 (1 Tim 6:16) Plain Directly states: God ALONE has immortality. E27 (1 Thess 4:16-17) Plain Directly states: dead rise, THEN ever with the Lord. Chronological sequence. E43 (2 Cor 5:8) Ambiguous Two aorist infinitives; temporal relationship unspecified by grammar. Requires choosing between immediate and non-immediate readings. E44 (Phil 1:23) Ambiguous Same grammatical pattern as E43. Same-letter context (Phil 3:11,20-21) favors resurrection reading. E45 (Luke 23:43) Ambiguous Depends on editorial punctuation absent from original Greek. Contradicted by John 20:17 if read traditionally.

Step 3 -- Weight: The FOR side has 3 items, all classified Ambiguous -- each involves grammatical alternatives, editorial punctuation, or unspecified temporal relationships. The AGAINST side has 10+ Plain statements directly addressing the death-state with unambiguous negation of consciousness. The Plain statements vastly outweigh the Ambiguous ones in both quantity and clarity.

Step 4 -- SIS Application: The Plain statements (E1-E6, E9, E14, E16, E19, E27) determine the reading of the Ambiguous ones (E43-E45). The "absent from body, present with Lord" (E43) and "depart and be with Christ" (E44) are read as expressing Paul's confidence that death leads to being with Christ -- subjectively instantaneous from the dead person's perspective because there is no conscious interval. Luke 23:43 (E45) is read with "today" modifying "I say" (the Syriac Peshitta reading), consistent with Jesus not being in paradise on that day (John 20:17).

Step 5 -- Resolution: Strong Plain statements on one side (20 E-items + 5 N-items establishing unconscious death, resurrection as the hope, God alone having immortality). Only Ambiguous statements on the other side (3 items, each with documented grammatical or textual alternatives). The resolution is Strong in the conditionalist direction. The dead are unconscious between death and resurrection.

docs.title: I-B Resolution: I4 -- Paul teaches immediate conscious presence at death
docs.text:
Step 1 -- Tension: - FOR: E43 (2 Cor 5:8), E44 (Phil 1:23) - AGAINST: E16 (1 Cor 15:18), E26 (1 Cor 15:53-54), E37 (2 Tim 4:8), Phil 3:11, Phil 3:20-21

Step 2 -- Clarity Assessment:

Item Level Rationale E16 (1 Cor 15:18) Plain Same author states: without resurrection, dead perished. Logically incompatible with conscious bliss at death. E26 (1 Cor 15:53-54) Plain Same author states: immortality put on at resurrection, not at death. E37 (2 Tim 4:8) Contextually Clear Same author states: crown given "at that day" (the appearing), not at death. E43 (2 Cor 5:8) Ambiguous Aorist infinitives without temporal specification. E44 (Phil 1:23) Ambiguous Aorist infinitive + present infinitive via kai. Same letter contains resurrection as hope.

Step 3 -- Weight: Paul's own clearer statements (1 Cor 15:18,53-54; 2 Tim 4:8) outweigh the ambiguous ones (2 Cor 5:8; Phil 1:23).

Step 4 -- SIS: The same author's plain statements interpret his ambiguous ones. Paul's "absent/present" and "depart/be with Christ" are read as expressing confidence in resurrection, not temporal immediacy.

Step 5 -- Resolution: Strong Same-author Plain statements on one side, only Ambiguous statements on the other.

docs.title: Word Studies
docs.text:
Key findings that affect interpretation:

  • Sheol (H7585, 68 occ.): Every sheol characterization describes unconsciousness, silence, darkness, and cessation. Receives both righteous and wicked.
  • Hades (G86, 11 occ.): Semantically equivalent to sheol (LXX maps sheol to hades 58 times; Acts 2:27,31 confirms). Temporary -- cast into lake of fire (Rev 20:14).
  • Koimao (G2837, 19 occ.): The standard NT death-as-sleep word. Used by Jesus, Luke, Paul, and Peter. LXX translates shakab (H7901) as koimao 141 times.
  • Nephesh (H5315, 788 occ.) / Psyche (G5590, 105 occ.): "Life/being/self," not "immortal soul." Can die (Ezek 18:4), be destroyed (Matt 10:28), refer to corpses (Lev 21:11).
  • Athanasia (G110, 3 occ.): God alone has it (1 Tim 6:16). Mortals put it on at resurrection (1 Cor 15:53-54). The phrase "immortal soul" does not appear in Scripture.
  • Paradeisos (G3857, 3 occ.): One use involves editorial punctuation issues (Luke 23:43), one is a living person's vision (2 Cor 12:4), one is eschatological (Rev 2:7).

docs.title: Difficult Passages
docs.text:
2 Cor 5:8, Phil 1:23: These are the most commonly cited passages for conscious intermediate state. Analysis shows that (a) the Greek grammar does not specify temporal immediacy between death and being with Christ, (b) the same author explicitly states that without resurrection the dead have "perished" (1 Cor 15:18), and (c) Paul's hope in both letters is resurrection and bodily transformation. The passages express Paul's confidence that death leads to being with Christ -- a confidence fully satisfied by resurrection.

Luke 23:43: The traditional reading depends entirely on editorial comma placement. The Greek has no punctuation. Jesus was not in paradise on crucifixion day (John 20:17). The Syriac Peshitta reading ("I say unto thee today, thou shalt be with me in paradise") resolves the contradiction.

Luke 16:19-31: The passage is situated within a parabolic discourse, uses the same opening formula as labeled parables, and its stated teaching point is about heeding Scripture, not afterlife geography. One parable cannot override 9+ clear OT death-state passages and Jesus's own teachings about death as sleep and resurrection as the hope.

Matt 22:32 / Luke 20:38: Jesus explicitly introduces this as proof of RESURRECTION (not intermediate state). "All live unto him" (Luke 20:38) is proleptic -- God counts the dead as living because their resurrection is certain (cf. Rom 4:17). The Sadducees denied resurrection, not intermediate state, and Jesus's argument addresses their denial.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The biblical evidence on the state of the dead divides into two tiers: (1) twenty explicit statements across 8+ OT authors and NT apostolic teaching consistently describe the dead as unconscious -- thoughts perish, know nothing, no praise, silence, darkness, forgetfulness; and (2) ten passages alleged to teach conscious intermediate state, each of which involves genre complications (parable, apocalyptic vision), grammatical ambiguity (aorist infinitives without temporal specification, editorial punctuation absent from the original), or contextual qualifications (same-author resurrection hope, condemned necromancy, Jesus calling an event "the vision") that prevent ECT classification at the E-tier.

Resurrection is the consistent biblical hope for the dead. Jesus places it "at the last day" (John 6:39,40,44,54). Paul places being "with the Lord" after the resurrection event (1 Thess 4:16-17). Daniel is told to "rest" and then "stand" at the end of days (Dan 12:13). David, "a man after God's own heart," has not ascended to heaven (Acts 2:34). The OT heroes of faith "received not the promise" (Heb 11:39-40).

Paul's argument in 1 Cor 15:18 provides the decisive logical test: if there is no resurrection, those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished. This argument works only if the dead are NOT already in conscious bliss with Christ. The fact that Paul considers "no resurrection" equivalent to "perished" proves that resurrection -- not death -- is the mechanism by which the dead receive life.

Evidence items tracked in etc6-master-evidence.md.

docs.title: What CAN Be Said (Scripture explicitly states or necessarily implies)
docs.text:
• The dead know nothing (Ecc 9:5)
  • Thoughts perish at death (Psa 146:4)
  • There is no work, knowledge, or wisdom in sheol (Ecc 9:10)
  • The dead do not praise God (Psa 6:5, 115:17, 88:10-12, 30:9, Isa 38:18-19)
  • The dead go down into silence (Psa 115:17)
  • Death is described as sleep by God, Jesus, and 7+ biblical authors
  • David has not ascended into the heavens (Acts 2:34)
  • The OT heroes of faith have not received the promise (Heb 11:39-40)
  • Without resurrection, dead believers have perished (1 Cor 15:18)
  • God alone has immortality; humans must put it on at resurrection (1 Tim 6:16, 1 Cor 15:53-54)
  • The soul can die (Ezek 18:4) and be destroyed (Matt 10:28)
  • Resurrection at the last day is the biblical hope (John 6:39-40, 1 Thess 4:16-17, Dan 12:2)
  • Being "ever with the Lord" follows resurrection, not death (1 Thess 4:17)
  • Death reverses creation: dust returns, spirit returns to God, thoughts perish (Gen 3:19, Ecc 12:7, Psa 146:4)
  • Hades is temporary storage for the dead, not the final state (Rev 20:13-14)

docs.title: What CANNOT Be Said (not explicitly stated or necessarily implied by Scripture)
docs.text:
• That the dead are conscious between death and resurrection (no didactic text says this; all alleged passages involve genre, grammar, or context qualifications)
  • That "absent from body, present with Lord" means temporal immediacy at death (the Greek grammar does not specify temporal relationship)
  • That the "immortal soul" survives death in conscious awareness (the phrase does not appear in Scripture; the soul can die and be destroyed)
  • That the rich man and Lazarus describes literal afterlife geography (the passage is parabolic; "Abraham's bosom" appears only there)
  • That Luke 23:43 teaches immediate paradise at death (depends on editorial punctuation; Jesus was not in paradise that day)
  • That the souls under the altar prove consciousness (apocalyptic vision; Abel's blood also "cries"; the altar also speaks)
  • That death is "separation of soul from body" (no verse defines death this way; Gen 3:19 defines it as return to dust)
  • That the dead can communicate with the living (God prohibits and condemns the attempt; 1 Chr 10:13)

docs.title: Primary Verses (32 — full analysis required)
docs.text:
OT Death-State: Unconsciousness and Silence: Old Testament passages explicitly describing the dead as unconscious, silent, unknowing, or inactive - Psa 146:4 — His breath goeth forth, he returns to earth; in that very day his thoughts perish - Eccl 9:5-6 — The dead know not any thing; no more reward; memory forgotten; love, hatred, envy perished - Eccl 9:10 — No work, device, knowledge, or wisdom in sheol whither thou goest - Psa 6:5 — In death there is no remembrance of thee; in sheol who shall give thee thanks? - Psa 115:17 — The dead praise not the LORD, neither any that go down into silence - Psa 88:10-12 — Wonders to the dead? Shall dead arise and praise? Lovingkindness in the grave? Faithfulness in destruction? Wonders in the dark? Righteousness in forgetfulness? - Job 14:10-14 — Man dies, wastes away; where is he? Lies down, rises not till heavens be no more; thou shalt call and I will answer - Job 14:21 — Dead know not whether sons come to honour or brought low — explicit unconsciousness - Isa 38:18-19 — Sheol cannot praise thee; death cannot celebrate thee; they that go down into the pit cannot hope for thy truth; the living shall praise thee

OT and NT Sleep Vocabulary: Passages using shakab, yashen, koimao, or katheudo as metaphor for death - Dan 12:2 — Many that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake — resurrection from sleep-state - John 11:11-14 — Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; I go to awake him; then Jesus said plainly, Lazarus is dead - 1 Cor 15:18 — If no resurrection, then they which are fallen asleep in Christ are PERISHED — impossible if consciously in heaven

Sheol/Hades Characterization: Passages describing the nature and character of sheol and hades - Eccl 9:10 — No work, device, knowledge, or wisdom in sheol whither thou goest - Psa 6:5 — In death there is no remembrance of thee; in sheol who shall give thee thanks? - Psa 115:17 — The dead praise not the LORD, neither any that go down into silence - Psa 88:10-12 — Wonders to the dead? Shall dead arise and praise? Lovingkindness in the grave? Faithfulness in destruction? Wonders in the dark? Righteousness in forgetfulness?

Alleged Conscious Intermediate State Passages: Each requires detailed grammatical and contextual analysis; these are the counter-evidence to evaluate - 2 Cor 5:1-9 — Alleged conscious intermediate state — absent from body, present with Lord; earthly house dissolved - Phil 1:21-24 — Alleged conscious intermediate state — to depart and be with Christ which is far better; same letter: resurrection at 3:11,20-21 - Luke 23:43 — Alleged conscious intermediate state — 'today shalt thou be with me in paradise'; comma placement issue - Luke 16:19-31 — Alleged conscious intermediate state — rich man and Lazarus parable; Abraham's bosom - Rev 6:9-11 — Alleged conscious intermediate state — souls under the altar crying out - 1 Sam 28:3-20 — Alleged conscious intermediate state — witch of Endor; Saul and Samuel - Matt 17:1-9 — Alleged conscious intermediate state — transfiguration with Moses and Elijah; Jesus calls it 'the vision' (horama) - 1 Pet 3:18-20 — Alleged conscious intermediate state — preaching to spirits in prison

Resurrection as the Biblical Hope: Passages presenting resurrection, not death, as the moment of receiving eternal life and being with the Lord - John 6:39-40 — I will raise him up at the last day — repeated 4x; resurrection is the hope, not immediate heaven - Dan 12:2 — Many that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake — resurrection from sleep-state - 1 Cor 15:51-54 — We shall not all sleep; mortal must put on immortality; corruptible must put on incorruption — immortality acquired at resurrection - Acts 2:29-34 — David is NOT ascended into the heavens — explicit denial of David's conscious heavenly state despite being 'a man after God's own heart' - Heb 11:39-40 — These all, having obtained a good report through faith, received NOT the promise — OT saints not yet in heaven

Creation Anthropology and Death Reversal: The Gen 2:7 creation formula and its reversal at death - Gen 2:7 — Formation of living soul — dust + neshamah = nephesh chayyah; foundational for what 'dies' at death - Gen 3:19 — Death sentence — dust to dust; defines death as reversal of creation - Eccl 12:7 — Dust returns to earth; spirit returns to God who gave it — reversal of Gen 2:7 - Psa 146:4 — His breath goeth forth, he returns to earth; in that very day his thoughts perish

Immortality Conditional, Not Inherent: Passages establishing that immortality belongs to God alone and is acquired at resurrection - 1 Tim 6:15-16 — God alone (monos) hath immortality — foundational for conditional immortality

Key Cross-References for Alleged Conscious State Passages: Verses that resolve or contextualize the alleged conscious state passages - John 20:17 — I am not yet ascended to my Father — Jesus not in paradise on crucifixion day; critical for Luke 23:43 - 1 Cor 15:18 — If no resurrection, then they which are fallen asleep in Christ are PERISHED — impossible if consciously in heaven

Additional Primary Verses: - Matt 22:31-32 — God of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob — God of the living; Jesus used to prove RESURRECTION, not present consciousness - Acts 7:59-60 — Stephen: Lord Jesus receive my spirit; he fell ASLEEP — spirit commended + sleep language combined - 1 Thess 4:13-17 — Them which are asleep; dead in Christ shall rise first; then we which are alive shall be caught up; so shall we ever be with the Lord

docs.title: Focus Areas
docs.text:
1. OT Death-State Passages: Silence, Unconsciousness, and Cessation: The OT consistently describes the dead as unconscious across at least 6 books and 8+ authors. READ the following passages with full chapter context: Psa 146:4 (thoughts PERISH — eshtonah H6250), Eccl 9:5-6,10 (know NOTHING — meumah), Psa 6:5 (no remembrance — zeker H2143), Psa 115:17 (dead praise NOT), Psa 88:10-12 (series of rhetorical questions expecting 'no'), Job 14:10-14,21 (dead know nothing of sons), Isa 38:18-19 (Hezekiah: dead cannot praise). Run hebrew_parser.py on each key verse to document the vocabulary of negation (lo, ayin, ein) combined with cognitive/volitional terms. The research agent should also retrieve Job 3:13-19 (rest/quiet/sleep), Job 10:21-22 (darkness), Job 17:13-16 (sheol as house). Cross-reference with Psa 30:9 and Psa 143:3. This focus area establishes the E-item foundation. Verses: Psa 146:4, Eccl 9:5-6, Eccl 9:10, Psa 6:5, Psa 115:17, Psa 88:10-12, Job 14:10-14, Job 14:21, Isa 38:18-19, Psa 30:9, Psa 143:3, Job 3:13-19, Job 10:21-22, Isa 26:14 Strong's: H6250, H2143, H7585, H4194, H2822

  2. Death as 'Sleep' — OT and NT Vocabulary Chain: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/H3462-yâshên.md and D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G2837-koimao.md for existing canonical studies. H7901 (shakab) and G2518 (katheudo) DO NOT have library entries and need generation. Trace the death-sleep formula: OT uses shakab ('sleep with fathers' — Deut 31:16, 2 Sam 7:12, 1 Ki 2:10, 11:43, 14:31 etc.) and yashen (Ps 13:3, Jer 51:39, Dan 12:2). NT uses koimao (John 11:11, Acts 7:60, 13:36, 1 Cor 15:6,18,20,51, 1 Thess 4:13-15) and katheudo (Matt 9:24, Mark 5:39, 1 Thess 5:10). Run hebrew_parser.py on Deut 31:16, Dan 12:2, and Jer 51:39 to verify shakab/yashen death uses. Run greek_parser.py on John 11:11-14, 1 Cor 15:51, 1 Thess 4:13-14 for koimao. Also check H7290 (radam — deep sleep/stupor, Jon 1:5-6, Ps 76:6) and H8639 (tardemah — deep sleep, Gen 2:21, Gen 15:12). Count authors: Moses, Job/poet, Jeremiah, Daniel, Jesus, Luke, Paul — at minimum 7. Verses: Deut 31:16, Dan 12:2, Jer 51:39, Psa 13:3, John 11:11-14, Acts 7:60, Acts 13:36, 1 Cor 15:6, 1 Cor 15:18, 1 Cor 15:51, 1 Thess 4:13-15, 1 Thess 5:10, Matt 9:24, Mark 5:39 Strong's: H7901, H3462, G2837, G2518, H7290, H8639

  3. Sheol (H7585) and Hades (G86) as the Abode of the Dead: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/H7585-showl.md and D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G86-háidēs.md for existing canonical studies. Sheol (H7585, 68 OT occurrences) is characterized by: silence (Ps 115:17), no work/knowledge/wisdom (Eccl 9:10), darkness (Job 10:21-22, Ps 143:3), no praise (Ps 6:5, Isa 38:18-19), forgetfulness (Ps 88:12). LXX translates sheol as hades 58 times, confirmed by Acts 2:27,31 (Ps 16:10 quoted). Hades (G86, 11 NT occurrences): Matt 11:23, 16:18, Luke 10:15, 16:23, Acts 2:27,31, Rev 1:18, 6:8, 20:13,14. Sheol receives both righteous AND wicked — Jacob (Gen 37:35), Korah (Num 16:30-33), David (Ps 16:10), Hezekiah (Isa 38:10). Hades is TEMPORARY — delivered up dead, cast into lake of fire (Rev 20:13-14). Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py on Ps 16:10 to trace the sheol→hades chain. Also examine Isa 14:9-11, Isa 5:14, Prov 15:24, Prov 27:20, Jon 2:2 for sheol characterization. Verses: Ps 16:10, Acts 2:27, Acts 2:31, Eccl 9:10, Job 10:21-22, Isa 5:14, Isa 14:9-11, Prov 15:24, Jon 2:2, Rev 20:13-14, Matt 11:23, Matt 16:18, Gen 37:35, Num 16:30-33 Strong's: H7585, G86, H6757, H2822

  4. 2 Corinthians 5:1-9 — Absent from Body, Present with Lord: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/2-corinthians-5-unclothed-intermediate-state/CONCLUSION.md for the prior dedicated study. Key grammatical points: (1) Paul uses clothing metaphor — he wants to be 'clothed upon' (ependysasthai, aorist middle infinitive) NOT 'unclothed' (ekdysasthai). He explicitly does NOT want to be naked/disembodied (v.4). (2) 'Absent from body, present with Lord' (v.8) — two aorist infinitives (ekdemesai, endemesai) connected by kai. The aorist does not specify temporal relationship or duration between the two events. (3) The PURPOSE stated is 'that mortality might be swallowed up of life' (v.4) — direct language from 1 Cor 15:54. (4) 1 Cor 15:18 is the decisive cross-reference: if no resurrection, dead in Christ have 'perished' (apollymi) — impossible if they are already in conscious bliss. Run greek_parser.py --verse on 2 Cor 5:1, 5:4, 5:6, 5:8. Also read the skenoma (G4638) and endyo (G1746) word studies. Compare with Phil 3:20-21 (transformation of body at coming). Verses: 2 Cor 5:1-9, 2 Cor 5:4, 2 Cor 5:8, 1 Cor 15:54, 1 Cor 15:18, Phil 3:20-21, Rom 8:22-23 Strong's: G4638, G1746, G1553, G1736, G1927

  5. Philippians 1:21-24 — To Depart and Be with Christ: The critical interpretive move is reading Phil 1:23 in the context of the SAME LETTER. Phil 3:10-11: 'if by any means I might attain unto the resurrection of the dead' — why seek resurrection if already with Christ at death? Phil 3:20-21: 'we look for the Saviour...who shall change our vile body' — future transformation, not present bliss. The word 'depart' (analysai, G360) is an aorist active infinitive; 'to be with Christ' (syn Christo einai) follows immediately without specifying temporal gap. From the dead person's subjective perspective (no conscious interval), the next conscious moment after death IS being with Christ at resurrection. Compare with 2 Tim 4:6-8 where Paul anticipates the 'crown of righteousness' given 'at that day' (the appearing of Christ), NOT at death. Run greek_parser.py --verse on Phil 1:23 and 2 Tim 4:8. Verses: Phil 1:21-24, Phil 1:23, Phil 3:10-11, Phil 3:20-21, 2 Tim 4:6-8 Strong's: G360, G4862

  6. Luke 23:43 — 'Today Shalt Thou Be with Me in Paradise': Three key issues: (1) PUNCTUATION: Greek manuscripts have no punctuation. The comma placement — 'I say unto thee, Today shalt thou...' vs. 'I say unto thee today, Thou shalt...' — is entirely editorial. The word 'today' (semeron G4594) can modify either verb. The Syriac Peshitta and the Curetonian manuscript place 'today' with 'I say.' (2) JESUS WAS NOT IN PARADISE THAT DAY: John 20:17 — three days later, Jesus told Mary 'I am not yet ascended to my Father.' If paradise = God's presence (2 Cor 12:4, Rev 2:7), Jesus was not there on Friday. (3) PARADEISOS (G3857): Only 3 NT occurrences — Luke 23:43, 2 Cor 12:4, Rev 2:7. LXX uses it for Eden (Gen 2:8). Rev 2:7 links it to the tree of life. Run greek_parser.py --verse on Luke 23:43 and John 20:17. READ any existing library entry for G3857 (not found in library — missing). Also check Acts 2:31 — Christ's soul was not left in hades. Verses: Luke 23:43, John 20:17, 2 Cor 12:4, Rev 2:7, Acts 2:31 Strong's: G3857, G4594

  7. Luke 16:19-31 — Rich Man and Lazarus: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/etc6-09-rich-man-lazarus/CONCLUSION.md for the prior dedicated study (17 evidence items). Key points: (1) GENRE: Situated in Luke 15-16, a continuous parabolic discourse. Luke 15:3 provides a single parabole label for three stories. The opening formula 'a certain rich man' (anthropos tis plousios) matches Luke 12:16 (labeled parabole) and 16:1 (universally accepted as parabolic). (2) STATED TEACHING POINT: 'They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them' (vv.29,31) — the lesson is about listening to Scripture, not about afterlife geography. (3) SAME AUTHOR: Luke records 'David is not ascended' (Acts 2:34) and Stephen 'fell asleep' (Acts 7:60). (4) ABRAHAM'S BOSOM: Appears ONLY in this passage in all Scripture. (5) Tree 3 classification: Fails Gate 1 (parabolic character) and Gate 3 (parabolic genre). Prior classification: Neutral. Run greek_parser.py on Luke 16:23-24 to document the vocabulary (odunao/basanos vs. basanizo/basanismos). Verses: Luke 16:19-31, Luke 15:3, Luke 12:16, Luke 16:1, Acts 2:34 Strong's: G3860, G3852

  8. Revelation 6:9-11 — Souls Under the Altar: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/etc6-10-souls-under-altar/CONCLUSION.md for the prior dedicated study (20 evidence items). Key points: (1) APOCALYPTIC GENRE: Every surrounding element in Revelation's visions is symbolic — seals, horsemen, stars falling, sky rolling up. Psychas (souls) under the altar = OT sacrificial imagery where blood is poured at altar base (Lev 4:7,18,25,30). (2) ABEL PARALLEL: Gen 4:10 — Abel's blood 'cries' from the ground. This is forensic personification, not literal voice. The word 'cry' (krazo G2896) used of blood/creation elsewhere. (3) ALTAR SPEAKS: Rev 16:7 — the altar itself speaks. If souls speaking proves consciousness, the altar is also conscious. (4) ANAPAUOMAI link: Rev 6:11 'rest' (anapauomai) connects to Rev 14:13 'rest from labours.' (5) Rev 20:4-5: These same souls 'LIVED' at the first resurrection — they were not alive before. Tree 3: Gate 1 FAIL (symbolic vision-figure), Gate 3 FAIL (apocalyptic genre). Prior classification: Neutral. Verses: Rev 6:9-11, Gen 4:10, Lev 4:7, Rev 16:7, Rev 14:13, Rev 20:4-5 Strong's: G5590, G2896, G373

  9. 1 Samuel 28:3-20 — Witch of Endor and Matt 17:1-9 — Transfiguration: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/saul-witch-endor-necromancy/CONCLUSION.md for the prior 1 Sam 28 study. For the witch of Endor: (1) Comprehensive OT prohibition against necromancy (Exo 22:18, Lev 19:31, 20:6,27, Deut 18:9-14). (2) Saul did NOT see anything — only the woman saw (vv.12-14). She described 'elohim ascending.' (3) No new information was given beyond what Samuel had prophesied while alive (1 Sam 15:28). (4) God CONDEMNED Saul for this act (1 Chr 10:13). (5) If the dead are actually unconscious, this was demonic impersonation. For the transfiguration: (1) Moses was RESURRECTED — Jude 9 records Michael's dispute with the devil about the BODY of Moses. (2) Elijah was TRANSLATED — never died (2 Ki 2:11). (3) Jesus calls it 'the vision' (horama, G3705) in Matt 17:9. Neither passage requires conscious intermediate state. Run greek_parser.py on Matt 17:3 and Matt 17:9 to document horama usage. Verses: 1 Sam 28:3-20, 1 Chr 10:13, Exo 22:18, Lev 19:31, Deut 18:9-14, Matt 17:1-9, Matt 17:9, Jude 1:9, 2 Ki 2:11 Strong's: G3705, H178

  10. 1 Peter 3:18-20 and 4:6 — Preaching to Spirits in Prison: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/1-peter-3-spirits-in-prison/CONCLUSION.md for the prior dedicated study. Key interpretive framework: (1) 'By the Spirit' (en ho, v.19) = the Spirit of Christ who was in OT prophets (1 Pet 1:10-11). (2) The preaching occurred 'in the days of Noah' (v.20) through Noah, 'a preacher of righteousness' (2 Pet 2:5). (3) The 'spirits' are those who were disobedient during Noah's time and are NOW in 'prison' (death/sheol). (4) 1 Pet 4:6: 'was the gospel preached' (euaggelisthe, aorist passive) to those who ARE dead — past action to present dead = preached while alive. (5) Alternative: 'spirits' = fallen angels (Gen 6:1-4, 2 Pet 2:4, Jude 6), with 'prison' = tartaroo. Run greek_parser.py --verse on 1 Pet 3:19 and 1 Pet 4:6 to document the aorist passive and en ho construction. Verses: 1 Pet 3:18-20, 1 Pet 4:6, 1 Pet 1:10-11, 2 Pet 2:5, 2 Pet 2:4, Jude 1:6, Gen 6:1-4 Strong's: G4151, G5438, G2782

  11. Resurrection as the Biblical Hope — Not Immediate Heaven: The resurrection is presented as the moment when believers receive their reward and are 'with the Lord' — not death. Key passages: (1) John 6:39,40,44,54 — 'I will raise him up at the LAST DAY' repeated 4 times. (2) 1 Thess 4:16-17 — dead in Christ rise first, THEN 'so shall we ever be with the Lord.' Being with the Lord follows resurrection, not death. (3) 1 Cor 15:18 — the devastating logical argument: if no resurrection, dead believers have PERISHED. If they are already in heaven, Paul's argument makes no sense. (4) Dan 12:2 — they SLEEP in dust until they AWAKE. (5) Acts 2:29,34 — David, the man after God's heart, is NOT ascended to heaven. (6) Heb 11:39-40 — the OT heroes 'received NOT the promise' and await perfection 'with us.' (7) Rev 20:4-5 — martyrs 'lived' at the first resurrection. (8) John 5:28-29 — ALL in graves shall come forth. Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py on 1 Thess 4:16 and John 6:40. Verses: John 6:39-40, John 6:44, John 6:54, 1 Thess 4:16-17, 1 Cor 15:18, Dan 12:2, Acts 2:29-34, Heb 11:39-40, Rev 20:4-5, John 5:28-29 Strong's: G386, G1453, G2227

  12. Anthropological Foundation: What Dies and What Returns to God: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/H5315-nephesh.md, D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/H7307-ruach.md, D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/H5397-nshamah.md, D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G5590-psyche.md, D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G4151-pneuma.md, and the translation relationships D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/TR-nephesh-psyche.md and D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/TR-ruach-pneuma.md (listed in D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/TR-nephesh-psyche.md and D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/TR-ruach-pneuma.md). Also READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/WG-soul.md and D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/WG-spirit.md. Creation formula (Gen 2:7): dust (aphar H6083) + breath (neshamah H5397) = living soul (nephesh chayyah). Death reversal: dust returns to earth (Gen 3:19, Eccl 3:20), spirit (ruach) returns to God (Eccl 12:7), thoughts PERISH (Ps 146:4). Man BECAME a soul, not received one. Same term (nephesh chayyah) for animals (Gen 1:24). Nephesh can DIE (Ezek 18:4), be DESTROYED (Matt 10:28), refer to CORPSES (Lev 21:11, Num 6:6). Ruach = the animating principle — never used for corpses. When ruach departs, cessation is total. Animals share the same ruach (Eccl 3:19). Verses: Gen 2:7, Gen 3:19, Eccl 12:7, Eccl 3:19-21, Psa 146:4, Ezek 18:4, Matt 10:28, Lev 21:11 Strong's: H5315, H7307, H5397, G5590, G4151, H6083

  13. The Matt 22:31-32 / Luke 20:34-38 Problem: 'God of the Living': In all three synoptic accounts (Matt 22:23-32, Mark 12:18-27, Luke 20:27-38), the Sadducees challenge RESURRECTION. Jesus responds with God's self-identification as 'God of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob' to prove that these patriarchs WILL RISE — not that they are currently conscious. Luke 20:37-38 adds 'for all live unto him' — a proleptic statement: they are counted as living because their resurrection is certain (cf. Rom 4:17 'calleth those things which be not as though they were'). The passage proves the CERTAINTY of resurrection, which the Sadducees denied (Acts 23:8). If the patriarchs were already alive in heaven, Jesus's argument proves too little — the Sadducees would have no reason to deny it. Run greek_parser.py on Matt 22:32 and Luke 20:38. Verses: Matt 22:31-32, Luke 20:37-38, Mark 12:26-27, Rom 4:17, Acts 23:8 Strong's: G2198, G3498

docs.title: Critical Methodological Notes
docs.text:
1. Investigator, not advocate: Report what the text says. Every passage must be analyzed on its own terms before comparing with other passages.

  2. Evidence Classification Trees apply: All evidence items will be classified using Trees 1-5 from the etc6-series-methodology. Position labels: Cond., ECT, ECT-direction, Neutral. Master Evidence IDs left blank.

  3. Genre gates are critical: For Luke 16:19-31, Rev 6:9-11, 1 Sam 28, and Matt 17:1-9, the genre classification (Tree 3 Gates 1 and 3) determines whether these passages can produce E-items or are classified as Neutral.

  4. The 1 Cor 15:18 test: Apply this logic test to every alleged conscious intermediate state passage: if believers are already in conscious bliss with Christ, Paul's argument that without resurrection they have 'perished' makes no sense. This is not an argument from silence — it is a reductio ad absurdum from Paul himself.

  5. Prior studies to READ: The research agent should read CONCLUSION.md from: etc6-04-state-of-the-dead, etc6-05-four-hell-words, etc6-09-rich-man-lazarus, etc6-10-souls-under-altar, 2-corinthians-5-unclothed-intermediate-state, 1-peter-3-spirits-in-prison, saul-witch-endor-necromancy, stephens-prayer-receive-spirit, spirits-of-just-men-made-perfect, objections-to-soul-sleep.

  6. Count authors: Document which biblical authors use sleep/unconsciousness language for death. The breadth of authorial witness is evidentially significant.

  7. Full chapter context mandatory for all alleged conscious state passages. Isolated verse readings are methodologically invalid for determining genre and context.

docs.title: The Short Answer
docs.text: The Bible teaches that the dead are unconscious -- resting in a dreamless sleep -- until the resurrection. They do not go immediately to heaven or hell. Resurrection, not death, is the moment when believers receive their reward and are reunited with Christ.

docs.title: What the Old Testament Says
docs.text:
Across multiple authors and centuries, the Old Testament paints a consistent picture: death is the end of all conscious activity until God intervenes.

  • Thoughts stop. "His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish" (Psalm 146:4).
  • The dead know nothing. "The dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward" (Ecclesiastes 9:5).
  • No activity in the grave. "There is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave" (Ecclesiastes 9:10).
  • No praise, only silence. "The dead praise not the LORD, neither any that go down into silence" (Psalm 115:17).

Job, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and Daniel all agree: the dead are asleep, unaware, and waiting.

docs.title: Death as Sleep
docs.text: The Bible repeatedly calls death "sleep." God uses this language (Deuteronomy 31:16). Jesus uses it -- "Our friend Lazarus sleepeth" (John 11:11). Paul and the other apostles use it throughout the New Testament. Sleep is a state without awareness, and that is precisely the point.

docs.title: Only God Has Immortality
docs.text: Scripture is clear that humans do not possess an immortal soul by nature. "God alone hath immortality" (1 Timothy 6:16). Immortality is something believers must "put on" at the resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:53-54). The soul can die (Ezekiel 18:4) and be destroyed (Matthew 10:28). The phrase "immortal soul" never appears in the Bible.

docs.title: Resurrection Is the Hope
docs.text:
Every passage that tells us when believers are rewarded points to the resurrection, not to the moment of death:

  • Jesus: "I will raise him up at the last day" (John 6:40) -- repeated four times.
  • Paul: "The dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them ... and so shall we ever be with the Lord" (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17).
  • Peter at Pentecost: "David is not ascended into the heavens" (Acts 2:34).

Paul makes the point inescapable in 1 Corinthians 15:18 -- if there is no resurrection, then believers who have died "are perished." That argument only works if the dead are not already alive in heaven. Resurrection is not a bonus; it is the sole means by which the dead receive life.

docs.title: What About the Passages That Seem to Say Otherwise?
docs.text: A handful of texts are commonly cited in favor of consciousness after death -- the rich man and Lazarus, the thief on the cross, Paul's "absent from the body, present with the Lord." In each case, closer examination reveals genre considerations (parable, apocalyptic vision), grammatical ambiguity (the Greek does not specify when), or editorial punctuation choices that are not present in the original manuscripts. None of them, on careful reading, overturns the clear, repeated teaching found throughout both Testaments.

docs.title: The Bottom Line
docs.text: The Bible's testimony is consistent from Genesis to Revelation: death is an unconscious rest. The dead are not suffering, not rejoicing, not watching from above. They are asleep, held safely by God, waiting for the resurrection morning when Christ calls them from the grave and gives them life that will never end.

docs.title: Cross-Testament Parallels
docs.text:
• 1 Thess 4:16 → Rev 11:15 (nt, vocabulary — trumpet, voice, heaven, Christ)
  • 1 Thess 4:16 → 1 Cor 15:52 (nt, vocabulary + theological — dead, trumpet; resurrection at last trump)
  • 1 Thess 4:16 → Rev 14:13 (nt, vocabulary + theological — dead, heaven, voice; dead rest then live)
  • John 6:40 → John 3:16 (nt, vocabulary + theological — everlasting life, believe, everyone; eternal life through faith)
  • John 6:40 → John 11:26 (nt, vocabulary + theological — everlasting, believe, everyone; life through faith)
  • John 6:40 → John 6:54 (nt, vocabulary + structural — everlasting life, last day; 'I will raise him up at the last day' repeated)
  • Rev 6:9 → Rev 5:6 (nt, vocabulary — slain (sphazo); Lamb slain, martyrs slain)
  • Rev 6:9 → Gen 4:10 (ot, theological + structural — blood crying out; Abel's blood cries from ground, martyrs' blood cries under altar; forensic personification)
  • Rev 6:9 → Lev 4:7 (ot, structural — blood poured at base of altar; sacrificial blood at altar base, souls/lives under altar)
  • Acts 2:27 → Psa 16:10 (ot, direct quotation — sheol→hades; 'thou wilt not leave my soul in sheol/hades')

Also called TOPHETH. A place in the valley of the sons of Hinnom 2KI 23:10. Jewish children passed through the fire to the god Molech in 2KI 23:10; JER 7:31,32; 19:6,11-14; 32:35. See also 2CH 28:3; 33:6. Destroyed by Josiah 2KI 23:10. Horror of ISA 30:33.

docs.title: Jacob expects to go to sheol mourning
docs.text:
And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.

Context: Jacob believes Joseph is dead. A righteous patriarch expects sheol.

Notes: First sheol occurrence. Jacob is righteous, yet expects sheol. KJV: 'grave.'

docs.title: Korah swallowed alive into sheol
docs.text:
Numbers 16:30: But if the LORD make a new thing, and the earth open her mouth, and swallow them up, with all that [appertain] unto them, and they go down quick into the pit; then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the LORD. [...] Numbers 16:33: They, and all that [appertained] to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation.

Context: Judgment on Korah for rebellion. KJV: 'pit' for sheol.

Notes: Sheol receives the judged. 'Perished from among the congregation' — cessation language.

docs.title: Fire burns to lowest sheol
docs.text:
For a fire is kindled in mine anger, and shall burn unto the lowest hell, and shall consume the earth with her increase, and set on fire the foundations of the mountains.

Context: Song of Moses — divine judgment on unfaithful Israel.

Notes: KJV: 'lowest hell.' Fire metaphor about extent of God's consuming anger. Verb 'consume' (akal) = destruction.

docs.title: The LORD brings down to sheol and raises up
docs.text:
The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.

Context: Hannah's prayer — celebrating God's sovereignty over life and death.

Notes: Kill/make alive = bring down to sheol/bring up. Sheol = death, with resurrection hope. KJV: 'grave.'

docs.title: Hide me in sheol until wrath passes
docs.text:
O that thou wouldest hide me in the grave, that thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!

Context: Job's lament about human mortality.

Notes: Sheol as temporary hiding place. 'Until thy wrath be past' + 'set time' = temporal. KJV: 'grave.'

docs.title: Rephaim tremble; sheol naked before God; Abaddon uncovered
docs.text:
Job 26:5: Dead [things] are formed from under the waters, and the inhabitants thereof. [...] Job 26:6: Hell [is] naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.

Context: Job describes God's power over all creation including the underworld.

Notes: H7496 rephaim + H7585 sheol + H11 abaddon. Sheol-Abaddon pairing.

docs.title: No remembrance in death; no praise in sheol
docs.text:
For in death [there is] no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?

Context: David's prayer in distress — psalm of lament.

Notes: E-tier: sheol characterized by 'no remembrance' and inability to praise. KJV: 'grave.' Didactic psalm.

docs.title: Wicked turned into sheol
docs.text:
The wicked shall be turned into hell, [and] all the nations that forget God.

Context: Psalm of praise for God's justice.

Notes: KJV: 'hell.' Same word (sheol) as Ps 6:5 ('grave'). Wicked go to same place as Jacob/David/Job.

docs.title: God will not leave my soul in sheol
docs.text:
For thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.

Context: Messianic psalm — quoted by Peter in Acts 2:27,31.

Notes: Pivotal: OT sheol (H7585), NT quotation uses hades (G86). Confirms sheol = hades. Also pairs sheol with shachath (H7845). KJV: 'hell.'

docs.title: Sheep laid in sheol; God redeems from sheol
docs.text:
Psalm 49:14: Like sheep they are laid in the grave; death shall feed on them; and the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning; and their beauty shall consume in the grave from their dwelling. [...] Psalm 49:15: But God will redeem my soul from the power of the grave: for he shall receive me. Selah.

Context: Wisdom psalm contrasting foolish rich and righteous.

Notes: Three sheol refs, all 'grave.' Death 'feeds on' wicked (consumption). Righteous hope: God redeems from sheol's power.

docs.title: No wonders, lovingkindness, or praise in sheol
docs.text:
Psalm 88:10: Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? shall the dead arise [and] praise thee? Selah. [...] Psalm 88:11: Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave? [or] thy faithfulness in destruction? [...] Psalm 88:12: Shall thy wonders be known in the dark? and thy righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?

Context: Darkest psalm — lament with no resolution.

Notes: E-tier: Comprehensive negation. Parallels: grave (sheol) = destruction (abaddon) = dark = land of forgetfulness.

docs.title: The dead praise not the LORD
docs.text:
The dead praise not the LORD, neither any that go down into silence.

Context: Psalm contrasting living who praise with dead who cannot.

Notes: Sheol = 'silence.' Consistent with Ps 6:5, 88:10-12, Ecc 9:10.

docs.title: If I make my bed in sheol, thou art there
docs.text:
If I ascend up into heaven, thou [art] there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou [art there].

Context: David on God's omnipresence.

Notes: Heaven-sheol merism. God's omnipresence, not sheol's nature. KJV: 'hell.'

docs.title: Way of life above; depart from sheol beneath
docs.text:
The way of life [is] above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.

Context: Proverb contrasting wise (life) and foolish (sheol/death).

Notes: Life = above; sheol = beneath. Wise avoids premature death. KJV: 'hell.'

docs.title: Sheol and Abaddon never satisfied
docs.text:
Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

Context: Proverbial comparison: insatiability.

Notes: Sheol-Abaddon pairing. KJV: 'Hell and destruction.' Hebrew pairs them as synonyms.

docs.title: The dead know nothing; no work in sheol
docs.text:
Ecclesiastes 9:5: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten. [...] Ecclesiastes 9:6: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any [thing] that is done under the sun. [...] Ecclesiastes 9:10: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do [it] with thy might; for [there is] no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.

Context: Qoheleth's observation about death and the state of the dead.

Notes: Comprehensive negation of consciousness: no knowledge, no reward, no work, no device, no wisdom in sheol. KJV: 'grave.'

docs.title: Sheol enlarges herself without measure
docs.text:
Therefore hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure: and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth, shall descend into it.

Context: Woe oracle against Jerusalem's corruption.

Notes: Personification of sheol as insatiable. Imagery is swallowing/consuming, not torturing. KJV: 'hell.'

docs.title: Sheol stirred up to meet king of Babylon
docs.text:
Isaiah 14:9: Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet [thee] at thy coming: it stirreth up the dead for thee, [even] all the chief ones of the earth; it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations. [...] Isaiah 14:10: All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us? [...] Isaiah 14:11: Thy pomp is brought down to the grave, [and] the noise of thy viols: the worm is spread under thee, and the worms cover thee. [...] Isaiah 14:15: Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.

Context: Mashal (taunt-poem, v.4) against king of Babylon. Genre: satirical prophecy.

Notes: Genre critical: v.4 labels this mashal. Dead 'speaking' = poetic personification. v.10: 'weak as we.' v.11: worms = decomposition. KJV: 'hell/grave.'

docs.title: Sheol cannot praise; death cannot celebrate
docs.text:
For the grave cannot praise thee, death can [not] celebrate thee: they that go down into the pit cannot hope for thy truth.

Context: Hezekiah's thanksgiving for deliverance from death.

Notes: E-tier: sheol = no praise; death = no celebration; pit = no hope. Three parallel terms. KJV: 'grave.'

docs.title: Carcasses — worm not die, fire not quenched
docs.text:
And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.

Context: Final verse of Isaiah. Righteous look upon aftermath of judgment. Quoted in Mark 9:48.

Notes: Subjects are 'carcases' (peger H6297) = dead bodies, NEVER used for living. Worm (tolaath H8438) = decomposition agent. 'Unquenchable fire' = fire completing its work.

docs.title: O sheol, I will be thy destruction
docs.text:
I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction: repentance shall be hid from mine eyes.

Context: God's promise of triumph over death — quoted by Paul in 1 Cor 15:55.

Notes: Sheol-maveth parallelism. God DESTROYS sheol/death, not preserves them. Paul quotes with hades replacing sheol.

docs.title: Out of the belly of sheol cried I
docs.text:
And said, I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD, and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, [and] thou heardest my voice.

Context: Jonah's prayer from inside the fish — near-death experience.

Notes: Sheol used metaphorically for near-death. Jonah was alive. KJV: 'hell.'

docs.title: Capernaum brought down to hades
docs.text:
And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.

Context: Jesus pronounces woe on unrepentant cities.

Notes: Hades (G86) = humiliation/judgment. Heaven-hades merism echoing Isa 14:13-15.

docs.title: Gates of hades shall not prevail
docs.text:
And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.

Context: Peter's confession at Caesarea Philippi.

Notes: Hades as power of death. 'Gates of hades' = power of death won't overcome the church.

docs.title: Capernaum thrust down to hades
docs.text:
And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.

Context: Parallel to Matt 11:23.

Notes: Same hades usage. Humiliation/judgment imagery.

docs.title: Rich man in hades, in torments
docs.text:
And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.

Context: Parable of Rich Man and Lazarus. Genre: parable (series in Luke 15-16).

Notes: Hades (G86) + basanos (G931). Genre = parable — fails Tree 3 Gates 1,3. ONLY passage associating hades with consciousness. Word is basanos (touchstone), not basanizo.

docs.title: Peter quotes Ps 16:10: soul not left in hades
docs.text:
Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell, neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.

Context: Peter's Pentecost sermon quoting Psalm 16:10 (LXX).

Notes: E-tier: Direct quotation with hades (G86) replacing sheol (H7585). Confirms sheol-hades equivalence.

docs.title: Christ's soul not left in hades
docs.text:
He seeing this before spake of the resurrection of Christ, that his soul was not left in hell, neither his flesh did see corruption.

Context: Peter's interpretation of Ps 16:10 as messianic prophecy.

Notes: Second confirmation: hades = sheol. Christ in hades = general abode of ALL dead, not punishment.

docs.title: O death, thy sting; O grave, thy victory
docs.text:
O death, where [is] thy sting? O grave, where [is] thy victory?

Context: Paul's resurrection chapter climax, quoting Hosea 13:14.

Notes: Hades = 'grave' in KJV. Third NT confirmation of sheol-hades equivalence. Hades = defeated enemy.

docs.title: Keys of hades and death
docs.text:
[I am] he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.

Context: Christ's self-identification to John.

Notes: Hades-thanatos pairing (cf. sheol-maveth in OT). Christ holds authority over hades.

docs.title: Death and Hades follow the pale horse
docs.text:
And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.

Context: Fourth seal — apocalyptic vision of death.

Notes: Hades personified alongside Death, as in OT sheol-maveth. Power is 'to kill' — death vocabulary.

docs.title: Death and hades give up dead; cast into lake of fire
docs.text:
Revelation 20:13: And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. [...] Revelation 20:14: And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.

Context: Great White Throne judgment.

Notes: Hades is TEMPORARY — delivers up dead, then destroyed. DISTINCT from lake of fire. Lake of fire = 'second death.'

docs.title: In danger of gehenna of fire
docs.text:
But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.

Context: Sermon on the Mount — intensifying the law on murder/anger.

Notes: First NT gehenna (G1067). 'Gehenna of fire' (tēn geennan tou pyros). Fire = gehenna's defining characteristic.

docs.title: Whole body cast into gehenna
docs.text:
Matthew 5:29: And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast [it] from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not [that] thy whole body should be cast into hell. [...] Matthew 5:30: And if thy right hand offend thee, cut it off, and cast [it] from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not [that] thy whole body should be cast into hell.

Context: Sermon on the Mount — lust and radical self-denial.

Notes: Alternative: member 'perishes' (apollymi G622). Destruction vocabulary. Body 'cast' = disposal.

docs.title: Destroy soul and body in gehenna
docs.text:
And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

Context: Jesus sends out the twelve — instructions about fear.

Notes: Most explicit gehenna verse. God 'destroys' (apolesai = apollymi G622) psyche AND soma in gehenna. Verb = apollymi (destroy), NOT basanizo (torment).

docs.title: Cast into gehenna fire vs. enter life
docs.text:
And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast [it] from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire.

Context: Discourse on stumbling blocks.

Notes: 'Enter into life' vs. 'cast into gehenna fire.' Life vs. gehenna = existence vs. destruction.

docs.title: Child of gehenna
docs.text:
Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.

Context: Seven woes against scribes and Pharisees.

Notes: Gehenna as metaphor for spiritual state. 'Child of gehenna' = Semitic idiom of characterization.

docs.title: How escape damnation of gehenna
docs.text:
[Ye] serpents, [ye] generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?

Context: Final woe — climax of condemnation.

Notes: 'Damnation' = krisis (G2920, judgment). About escaping judgment.

docs.title: Gehenna: worm not die, fire not quenched
docs.text:
Mark 9:43: And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched: [...] Mark 9:44: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched. [...] Mark 9:45: And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched: [...] Mark 9:46: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched. [...] Mark 9:47: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire: [...] Mark 9:48: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

Context: Jesus on stumbling blocks — triple repetition of gehenna warning.

Notes: Gehenna + asbestos (G762) + skolex (G4663). Quotes Isaiah 66:24. Isaiah source: carcasses (peger = dead bodies). Contrast: 'enter life' vs. gehenna.

docs.title: Fear him who can cast into gehenna
docs.text:
But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.

Context: Jesus on fear of God vs. fear of man.

Notes: Sequence: God KILLS first, THEN casts into gehenna. Gehenna follows death.

docs.title: Tongue set on fire of gehenna
docs.text:
And the tongue [is] a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.

Context: James on the tongue's danger.

Notes: Only non-Jesus gehenna use. Metaphorical: destructive power likened to gehenna's fire.

docs.title: Angels cast down to tartaroo, reserved unto judgment
docs.text:
For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast [them] down to hell, and delivered [them] into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;

Context: 2 Peter's chain of three OT judgment examples.

Notes: Only tartaroo (G5020) occurrence. Verb, not noun. Angels ONLY. 'Reserved unto judgment' = temporary imprisonment. Chains of darkness = confinement.

docs.title: Angels in everlasting chains; Sodom suffering eternal fire
docs.text:
Jude 1:6: And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. [...] Jude 1:7: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.

Context: Jude parallels 2 Peter 2:4.

Notes: Aidios (G126) chains. 'Unto judgment of the great day' = temporary holding. Jude 1:7: Sodom's 'eternal fire' — Sodom is NOT still burning. Results eternal, not process.

docs.title: Everlasting fire prepared for devil and angels
docs.text:
Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:

Context: Sheep/goats judgment — left hand sentence.

Notes: Aionios (G166) + pyr (G4442). 'Prepared for the devil and his angels' — originally for supernatural beings. Does NOT use sheol/hades/gehenna/tartaroo.

docs.title: Everlasting punishment vs. eternal life
docs.text:
And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.

Context: Conclusion of sheep/goats parable.

Notes: Kolasis (G2851) + aionios (G166). Key disputed text. Does aionios modify PROCESS (eternal punishing) or RESULT (permanent consequence)? Kolasis etymologically = curtailment.

docs.title: Devil tormented day and night forever
docs.text:
And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet [are], and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.

Context: Final defeat of Satan.

Notes: Basanizo (G928). Subjects: devil, beast, false prophet — supernatural/symbolic. When HUMANS encounter lake of fire, text uses 'second death' not basanizo.

docs.title: Smoke of torment ascends forever
docs.text:
Revelation 14:10: The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: [...] Revelation 14:11: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.

Context: Third angel's message — warning against beast worship.

Notes: Basanizo + basanismos. Alludes to Isa 34:9-10 (Edom's destruction — smoke formula). Subjects: beast-worshippers specifically.

docs.title: Edom: smoke ascending forever
docs.text:
Isaiah 34:9: And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. [...] Isaiah 34:10: It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.

Context: Prophecy against Edom — total destruction.

Notes: OT source for Rev 14:11 and 19:3. 'Smoke goes up forever' — but Edom is not still burning. Establishes OT convention: 'eternal fire/smoke' = finality of destruction.

docs.title: Everlasting destruction from the Lord's presence
docs.text:
Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power;

Context: Paul on the fate of gospel-rejecters at Christ's return.

Notes: Olethros (G3639, destruction) + aionios. Paul uses DESTRUCTION vocabulary, not torment.

docs.title: Not in book of life cast into lake of fire
docs.text:
And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

Context: Great White Throne — human fate.

Notes: When HUMANS encounter lake of fire, no torment vocabulary. Lake of fire = second death (v.14).

docs.title: Lake of fire = second death
docs.text:
But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.

Context: Description of who goes to lake of fire.

Notes: Explicit: lake of fire = 'the second death.' Death vocabulary, not torment. Definitive statement for human fate.

docs.title: Beast and false prophet cast into lake of fire
docs.text:
And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.

Context: Christ's return and defeat of the beast.

Notes: Beast and false prophet = symbolic entities, not individual humans. Cast 'alive' — different from human encounter ('second death').

docs.title: Valley of the son of Hinnom — boundary
docs.text:
And the border went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom unto the south side of the Jebusite; the same [is] Jerusalem: and the border went up to the top of the mountain that [lieth] before the valley of Hinnom westward, which [is] at the end of the valley of the giants northward:

Context: Tribal boundary description for Judah.

Notes: Ge-ben-Hinnom: first mention. Pure geographic reference.

docs.title: Valley of Hinnom — Benjamin boundary
docs.text:
And the border came down to the end of the mountain that [lieth] before the valley of the son of Hinnom, [and] which [is] in the valley of the giants on the north, and descended to the valley of Hinnom, to the side of Jebusi on the south, and descended to Enrogel,

Context: Benjamin's tribal boundary.

Notes: Second geographic reference. Still purely topographical.

docs.title: Josiah defiles Topheth in Valley of Hinnom
docs.text:
And he defiled Topheth, which [is] in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech.

Context: Josiah's religious reform.

Notes: Topheth (H8612) in Valley of Hinnom (H2011). Josiah ends sacrificial use.

docs.title: Ahaz burns children in Valley of Hinnom
docs.text:
Moreover he burnt incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burnt his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen whom the LORD had cast out before the children of Israel.

Context: Ahaz's idolatrous reign.

Notes: Child sacrifice in ge-Hinnom. The abomination that curses the valley.

docs.title: Manasseh passes children through fire
docs.text:
And he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards: he wrought much evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke him to anger.

Context: Manasseh's idolatrous reign.

Notes: Second king, same child sacrifice. Valley associated with death of children, not ongoing torment.

docs.title: Valley of Hinnom cursed — Valley of Slaughter
docs.text:
Jeremiah 7:31: And they have built the high places of Tophet, which [is] in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire; which I commanded [them] not, neither came it into my heart. [...] Jeremiah 7:32: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that it shall no more be called Tophet, nor the valley of the son of Hinnom, but the valley of slaughter: for they shall bury in Tophet, till there be no place.

Context: Jeremiah's temple sermon — pronouncing judgment.

Notes: God did NOT command child sacrifice. Valley renamed 'valley of slaughter.' Slaughter/death vocabulary. They will 'bury' — corpse disposal.

docs.title: Valley of Hinnom renamed Valley of Slaughter
docs.text:
Jeremiah 19:2: And go forth unto the valley of the son of Hinnom, which [is] by the entry of the east gate, and proclaim there the words that I shall tell thee, [...] Jeremiah 19:6: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that this place shall no more be called Tophet, nor The valley of the son of Hinnom, but The valley of slaughter.

Context: Jeremiah's broken potter prophecy.

Notes: Reinforces Jer 7:31-32. Prophetic destiny: slaughter and burial.

docs.title: Molech worship in Valley of Hinnom
docs.text:
And they built the high places of Baal, which [are] in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through [the fire] unto Molech; which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin.

Context: Jeremiah's prophecy during Jerusalem siege.

Notes: Third Jeremiah ref: God condemns burning, calls it 'abomination' He never commanded.

docs.title: Topheth ordained of old — fire and brimstone
docs.text:
For Tophet [is] ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made [it] deep [and] large: the pile thereof [is] fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it.

Context: Prophetic judgment oracle — Assyria's defeat.

Notes: Topheth as judgment imagery. Fire and brimstone. Context: military defeat and death.

docs.title: Valley of Hinnom as post-exilic reference
docs.text:
Zanoah, Adullam, and [in] their villages, at Lachish, and the fields thereof, at Azekah, and [in] the villages thereof. And they dwelt from Beersheba unto the valley of Hinnom.

Context: Post-exilic settlement list.

Notes: Post-exilic: valley still geographic reference, now without sacrificial connotations.

docs.title: Destruction and Death heard wisdom's fame
docs.text:
Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.

Context: Job's poem on wisdom.

Notes: Abaddon (H11) personified alongside maveth (H4194). Sheol-Abaddon-Death conceptual cluster.

docs.title: Fire consumes to Abaddon
docs.text:
For it [is] a fire [that] consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.

Context: Job's oath of innocence.

Notes: Abaddon = destruction as endpoint of consuming fire. Fire + Abaddon = complete consumption.

docs.title: Lovingkindness in sheol? Faithfulness in Abaddon?
docs.text:
Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave? [or] thy faithfulness in destruction?

Context: Darkest psalm — no resolution.

Notes: Sheol ('grave') parallel with Abaddon ('destruction'). Rhetorical question expecting 'no.'

docs.title: Sheol and Abaddon before the LORD
docs.text:
Hell and destruction [are] before the LORD: how much more then the hearts of the children of men?

Context: Proverb about God's omniscience.

Notes: Sheol-Abaddon pairing. KJV: 'Hell and destruction.' Associates sheol with destruction, not torment.

docs.title: Abaddon/Apollyon — king of the abyss
docs.text:
And they had a king over them, [which is] the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in the Hebrew tongue [is] Abaddon, but in the Greek tongue hath [his] name Apollyon.

Context: Fifth trumpet — demonic locusts.

Notes: Abaddon explicitly equated with Apollyon (G623, from apollymi = to destroy). Confirms destruction semantics.

docs.title: Everlasting life vs. everlasting contempt
docs.text:
And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame [and] everlasting contempt.

Context: Final chapter of Daniel — resurrection prophecy.

Notes: Owlam (H5769) for both outcomes. 'Contempt' = deraon (H1860, only here and Isa 66:24). Dead 'sleep in dust' = unconsciousness until resurrection.

docs.title: Perish vs. everlasting life
docs.text:
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

Context: Jesus's discourse with Nicodemus.

Notes: Apollymi (perish) vs. zoe aionios. Contrast: perish vs. live, not torment vs. bliss.

docs.title: Wages of sin is death vs. gift of eternal life
docs.text:
For the wages of sin [is] death; but the gift of God [is] eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Context: Paul's conclusion to Romans 6.

Notes: Thanatos (death) vs. zoe aionios. Wages of sin = death, not eternal life in torment.

docs.title: Day burns as oven; wicked become ashes
docs.text:
Malachi 4:1: For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch. [...] Malachi 4:2: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall. [...] Malachi 4:3: And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do [this], saith the LORD of hosts.

Context: Final OT prophecy about the Day of the LORD.

Notes: Stubble burned up, neither root nor branch. Wicked become ASHES under righteous's feet. OT's last word on wicked's fate.

docs.title: As though they had not been
docs.text:
For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, [so] shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.

Context: Obadiah's prophecy against Edom.

Notes: 'As though they had not been' (kelo hayu) — most explicit cessation statement in OT.

docs.title: Sorrows of sheol compassed me
docs.text:
The sorrows of hell compassed me about; the snares of death prevented me;

Context: David's song of deliverance.

Notes: Sheol-maveth parallelism. KJV: 'hell.' Figurative for mortal danger.

docs.title: Strong speak from midst of sheol
docs.text:
The strong among the mighty shall speak to him out of the midst of hell with them that help him: they are gone down, they lie uncircumcised, slain by the sword.

Context: Lamentation over Egypt — prophetic genre.

Notes: Genre: prophetic lamentation with personification. Dead 'speaking' = literary device. 'Slain' = dead, not tormented.

docs.title: Jealousy cruel as sheol
docs.text:
Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love [is] strong as death; jealousy [is] cruel as the grave: the coals thereof [are] coals of fire, [which hath] a most vehement flame.

Context: Love poetry — power of love.

Notes: Death-sheol parallelism. Sheol = grave's relentless power. KJV: 'grave.'

docs.title: Deceased (rephaim) shall not rise
docs.text:
[They are] dead, they shall not live; [they are] deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.

Context: Isaiah's song of praise.

Notes: Rephaim (H7496). Destroyed, memory perishes. Destruction and cessation language.

docs.title: Jacob: gray hairs to sheol with sorrow
docs.text:
And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in the which ye go, then shall ye bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.

Context: Jacob refuses to let Benjamin go.

Notes: Same sheol, same 'grave.' Sheol = common destination, not punitive. FA9 supporting verse.

docs.title: Covenant with death and sheol
docs.text:
Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves:

Context: Isaiah denounces Jerusalem's false confidence.

Notes: Death-sheol parallelism. People think they can negotiate with death/sheol. KJV: 'hell.'

docs.title: Enlarges desire as sheol
docs.text:
Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine, [he is] a proud man, neither keepeth at home, who enlargeth his desire as hell, and [is] as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all people:

Context: Woe against Babylon.

Notes: Sheol as simile for insatiability. Sheol-death parallelism. KJV: 'hell.'

docs.title: Though they dig into sheol
docs.text:
Though they dig into hell, thence shall mine hand take them; though they climb up to heaven, thence will I bring them down:

Context: God's inescapable judgment.

Notes: Heaven-sheol merism. No one escapes God. Not about sheol's nature. KJV: 'hell.'

docs.title: Korah and company go down into sheol
docs.text:
They, and all that [appertained] to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation.

Context: Continuation of the Korah rebellion narrative. The earth swallows Korah and his followers. KJV translates sheol as 'pit' here. They 'perished' (abad H6) -- destruction vocabulary.

Notes: Paired with Numbers 16:30. KJV uses 'pit' for sheol here. The result is perishing (abad), not ongoing torment. Sheol receives the judged but the narrative verb is destruction.

docs.title: Sheol as permanent from a pre-resurrection perspective
docs.text:
[As] the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no [more].

Context: Job laments his mortality. KJV translates sheol as 'grave.' Job sees death/sheol as final from a pre-resurrection perspective.

Notes: Cloud metaphor: consumed (kalah H3615) and vanishes. Sheol is the grave from which one does not return. KJV: 'grave' for sheol (righteous person speaking).

docs.title: Sheol as depth beyond human reach
docs.text:
[It is] as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know?

Context: Zophar describes God's wisdom as unfathomable. Sheol represents the deepest conceivable place -- paired with heaven as its opposite. KJV translates sheol as 'hell' here.

Notes: Spatial merism: heaven/sheol = highest/deepest = everywhere. Sheol is the spatial opposite of heaven, not a moral opposite. KJV: 'hell' for sheol in a wisdom context.

docs.title: Imprecatory psalm -- echoes Korah narrative
docs.text:
Let death seize upon them, [and] let them go down quick into hell: for wickedness [is] in their dwellings, [and] among them.

Context: David's imprecation against enemies. 'Go down quick (alive) into sheol' echoes Numbers 16:30,33 (Korah). KJV translates sheol as 'hell.'

Notes: Imprecatory genre. David invokes the Korah precedent. 'Quick' = alive (chayyim H2416). Death and sheol paired. KJV: 'hell' for sheol (wicked as subjects).

docs.title: Deliverance from the lowest sheol
docs.text:
For great [is] thy mercy toward me: and thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell.

Context: David's thanksgiving. God delivers from sheol tachtiy (lowest sheol). KJV translates sheol as 'hell.' David -- a righteous person -- speaks of being delivered FROM sheol.

Notes: If sheol = place of punishment for the wicked, why does righteous David need deliverance from it? Sheol here means the grave/death threat. KJV: 'hell' for sheol (righteous person as subject).
