"Same destination = same experience" must be added by the reader; the text does not state it. The text itself applies different vocabulary to the symbolic entities and to the humans. I069 I2 Rev 20:10's torment formula describes the fate of non-human/symbolic entities, not the fate of human beings I-A Cond. E2-E7: Subject identifications (all non-human/symbolic). E9: Formula applied to these three. E37: Formula appears once, only these subjects. N1: Different vocabulary for different subjects. N3: Formula never applied to humans. Systematizes the subject identifications and vocabulary distribution into a conclusion about whom the formula addresses. Uses only E/N vocabulary and concepts. I070 I3 Basanizo is a word family specific to supernatural/apocalyptic contexts for judgment, not a term for human eschatological fate I-A Cond. All 12 basanizo occurrences documented in E23-E27, E9, E25, E26. N2: Distributional observation confirmed. Systematizes the distributional data into a genre-specific conclusion. Uses only E/N components. I071 I4 The beast represents a system of human adherents; therefore the torment of the symbolic beast transfers to the humans within that system I-C ECT E4: The beast is a symbolic system. E12: Rev 19:20-21 uses different vocabulary for the beast (cast alive) and its human followers (slain). E8: Rev 20:9 uses "devoured" for human followers. E11: Rev 21:8 assigns human wicked "the second death." The claim that torment of a symbol transfers to the humans represented requires an external bridging concept (representative torment). The text does not state this transfer. The text explicitly uses different vocabulary for the system and for the humans within it. I072 I5 The "for ever and ever" formula always means genuinely eternal regardless of subject I-B ECT E9: Formula used in Rev 20:10. Rev 4:9-10: Formula applied to God (genuinely eternal). BUT E20: Isa 34:9-10 uses identical "for ever" language for Edom — animals inhabit ruins. E21: Babylon's smoke "for ever and ever" (Rev 19:3) yet "found no more at all" (Rev 18:21-23). The formula is applied to the eternal God (genuinely eternal) and to judgment on non-eternal subjects (Edom, Babylon). Both readings have E-level support. The claim that the formula is univocal requires choosing one meaning over another. I073

docs.title: I-B Resolution: I1 — Same lake = same experience
docs.text:
Step 1 — Tension: - FOR: E9 (all three in lake + tormented), E10 (humans also in lake), E16 (fire prepared for devil and his angels — humans sent there too) - AGAINST: E12 (different vocabulary: cast alive vs. slain in Rev 19:20-21), E8 (devoured for humans in 20:9), E10-E11 (second death for humans in 20:14-15, 21:8), N1 (vocabulary differentiation is a necessary implication)

Step 2 — Clarity Assessment:

Item Level Rationale E12 Plain Rev 19:20-21 uses different verbs in consecutive verses for symbolic entities (cast alive) and humans (slain) — directly addresses the question of whether different subjects receive the same treatment N1 Plain Observable vocabulary fact verified from the Greek text across Rev 19-21 E8 Plain katephagen (devoured) for human nations in Rev 20:9 is unambiguous destruction vocabulary E10-E11 Contextually Clear "Second death" designation for humans requires awareness that this is a death concept per the X=Y formula, but the death vocabulary is clear E9 Contextually Clear The torment formula is stated plainly but applied to non-human/symbolic subjects in apocalyptic genre E16 Ambiguous Matt 25:41 says fire was prepared for the devil and his angels; humans are sent there — but does not state they experience the same thing as the devil

Step 3 — Weight: The AGAINST side has multiple Plain items (E12, N1, E8) plus Contextually Clear items (E10-E11). The FOR side has one Contextually Clear item (E9, but subject is non-human) and one Ambiguous item (E16). The weight favors the AGAINST side.

Step 4 — SIS Application: The Plain items (E12, N1, E8) govern the reading of Ambiguous items. The text's own vocabulary differentiation — humans slain/devoured/second death vs. non-human entities tormented — determines the reading of the "same lake" observation. Being in the same location does not require the same experience when the text explicitly describes different outcomes.

Step 5 — Resolution: Strong Plain statements on the AGAINST side (vocabulary differentiation in same narrative units) with only Ambiguous statements on the FOR side. The text itself distinguishes what happens to different subjects at the same destination.

docs.title: I-B Resolution: I5 — "For ever and ever" always genuinely eternal
docs.text:
Step 1 — Tension: - FOR: Rev 4:9-10 (formula applied to God — genuinely eternal), E9 (formula applied to judgment in Rev 20:10) - AGAINST: E20 (Isa 34:9-10 uses identical "for ever" language for Edom — animals inhabit ruins), E21 (Rev 19:3 + 18:21-23: Babylon's smoke "for ever" yet "found no more at all")

Step 2 — Clarity Assessment:

Item Level Rationale E20 Plain Isa 34:9-10 uses identical formula; Isa 34:11-17 describes animals in ruins — the OT demonstrates the formula does not always mean ongoing process. Observable fact. E21 Plain Rev 18:21-23 explicitly says "found no more at all" five times; Rev 19:3 uses "for ever" for the same entity. Coexistence of cessation and "forever" language in the same literary context is observable. Rev 4:9-10 Plain Applied to God, the formula is genuinely eternal. E9 Contextually Clear The formula in Rev 20:10 requires determining whether it follows the God-usage (genuinely eternal) or the judgment-usage (permanent result).

Step 3 — Weight: Both sides have Plain items. However, the AGAINST side demonstrates from OT and NT evidence that the identical formula is used for entities whose cessation is explicitly described. The FOR side shows the formula is genuinely eternal when applied to God, but this does not prove it is univocal across all subjects.

Step 4 — SIS Application: The OT passage (Isa 34:9-10) provides the interpretive key for the judgment usage of the formula. The OT is the source material; Revelation draws on its imagery. The Edom and Babylon parallels demonstrate the formula can describe permanent results of completed destruction. Applied to God (genuinely eternal being), it is genuinely eternal. Applied to judgment on non-eternal subjects, it describes permanence of result.

Step 5 — Resolution: Strong The Isa 34:9-10 and Babylon evidence (Plain on the AGAINST side) demonstrates the formula is not univocal. The formula's meaning is subject-determined: genuinely eternal for God, permanent result for judgment on non-eternal subjects. The claim that it is always genuinely eternal requires ignoring the OT usage and the Babylon evidence within Revelation itself.

Full Tree 3/4/5 walkthroughs for every E-item classified Cond. or ECT and every N-item are documented in CLASSIFICATIONS.md.

Summary of reclassifications: - E8 (Rev 20:9, devoured): Candidate Cond. → reclassified Neutral (Genre Gate fail — apocalyptic) - E9 (Rev 20:10, tormented): Candidate ECT → reclassified Neutral (Subject Gate fail — all three subjects non-human/symbolic; Genre Gate fail — apocalyptic) - E10 (Rev 20:14-15, second death): Candidate Cond. → reclassified Neutral (Genre Gate fail — apocalyptic) - E11 (Rev 21:8, second death): Candidate Cond. → reclassified Neutral (Genre Gate fail — apocalyptic) - E18 (Ezek 28:18-19, ashes): Candidate Cond. → reclassified Neutral (Subject Gate fail — non-human cherub) - E19 (Dan 7:11, beast destroyed): Candidate Cond. → reclassified Neutral (Subject Gate fail — symbolic beast)

Items whose classification stood after full Tree 3 walkthrough: - E17 (1 John 3:8): Cond. — all gates pass (didactic epistle, destruction vocabulary) - E28 (Rom 6:23): Cond. — all gates pass (didactic epistle, death = wages of sin) - E29 (Luke 17:29): Cond. — all gates pass (Jesus' didactic saying, destruction vocabulary) - E30 (2 Pet 2:6): Cond. — all gates pass (didactic epistle, ashes, "ensample") - E32 (Mal 4:1): Cond. — all gates pass (prophetic eschatology, burn up) - E33 (Obad 1:16): Cond. — all gates pass (prophetic, cessation) - E34 (Psa 37:10): Cond. — all gates pass (wisdom, cessation)

docs.title: Basanizo (G928) — 12 NT occurrences
docs.text: From basanos (G931, touchstone for testing metals). 7 non-judgment uses (illness, waves, rowing, moral distress, childbirth, prophetic witness). 5 judgment uses (all in Revelation's apocalyptic framework or demonic speech). No epistle, Gospel didactic section, or OT passage uses this word for human eschatological fate. The KJV translates it with five different English words.

docs.title: Basanismos (G929) — 6 occurrences
docs.text: All in Revelation. Time-bounded in 4 of 6 (five months, Rev 9:5; one hour for Babylon, Rev 18:7, 10, 15).

docs.title: Therion (G2342) — 46 occurrences
docs.text: 38 of 46 in Revelation, where it is always the apocalyptic beast-entity. A symbolic political-religious system, not a literal individual.

docs.title: Pseudoprophetes (G5578) — 11 occurrences
docs.text: 3 singular in Revelation = one specific apocalyptic entity (= earth beast per Rev 19:20). 7 plural elsewhere = class of human deceivers. 1 singular outside Revelation with personal name (Acts 13:6, Bar-Jesus).

docs.title: Diabolos (G1228) — 38 occurrences
docs.text: Supernatural adversary when articular/singular. Identified as dragon/serpent (Rev 12:9), spirit being (Eph 2:2), pre-human (Gen 3:1), commander of angels (Matt 25:41). Subject of destruction vocabulary (Heb 2:14, katargeo; 1 John 3:8, luo).

docs.title: Katargeo (G2673) — 32 occurrences
docs.text: Applied to the devil (Heb 2:14) and death (1 Cor 15:26). Semantic range includes abolish, render powerless, destroy. Destruction-class vocabulary regardless of exact nuance.

docs.title: Rev 14:10-11 — Torment vocabulary applied to beast-worshippers
docs.text: This passage comes closest to applying torment vocabulary to human subjects. Two factors complicate a straightforward ECT reading: (1) the passage is in Revelation's apocalyptic framework (Genre Gate fails), and (2) the "for ever and ever" formula applies to the smoke (kapnos) of their torment, not directly to the torment itself — and Rev 19:3 shows the identical smoke formula describes Babylon, which is "found no more at all." (Examined in depth in etc7-11-smoke-ascending-forever.)

docs.title: The "same lake" argument
docs.text: The devil, beast, false prophet, death, hades, and unsaved humans all end up in the same lake. The inference that same destination = same experience is resolved I-B Strong against (see I-B Resolution above): the text itself uses different vocabulary for different subjects at the same destination.

docs.title: The "beast-as-representative" argument
docs.text: The beast represents a system that includes human adherents. The inference that the beast's torment transfers to those humans is classified I-C (compatible external) — an interpretive framework not stated in the text. The text applies different vocabulary to the symbol and to the humans within the system (Rev 19:20-21, 20:9, 21:8).

docs.title: Katargeo ambiguity (Heb 2:14)
docs.text: Whether katargeo means "destroy" or "render powerless" is a genuine lexical question. The word study documents the semantic range. Regardless of exact nuance, the verb is destruction-class vocabulary applied to the devil in a didactic epistle. E15 is classified Neutral because of this ambiguity — both sides can accept that the text uses this verb for the devil.

docs.title: What CAN Be Said (Scripture explicitly states or necessarily implies)
docs.text:
• The three subjects of the "tormented for ever and ever" formula in Rev 20:10 are the devil (non-human spirit being), the beast (symbolic entity), and the false prophet (symbolic entity). None is a literal human being.
  • The torment formula (basanisthesontai eis tous aionas ton aionon) appears once in Scripture and is applied only to these three non-human/symbolic entities.
  • Revelation uses different vocabulary for human subjects at the lake: devoured (Rev 20:9), slain (Rev 19:21), the second death (Rev 20:14-15, 21:8). The vocabulary differentiation is a textual fact.
  • The lake of fire is self-interpreted as "the second death" (Rev 20:14).
  • Basanizo in judgment contexts appears only in Revelation's apocalyptic framework or in demonic speech. No epistle, Gospel didactic section, or OT passage applies it to human eschatological fate.
  • The OT describes the Satan-figure with destruction/cessation vocabulary: fire devours, becomes ashes, exists never any more (Ezek 28:18-19).
  • The "for ever" formula is used in the OT for Edom (Isa 34:9-10), which is not still burning.
  • Destruction/death vocabulary for human fate spans all genres (OT prophets, wisdom, Gospels, epistles). Torment vocabulary for judgment is genre-specific to Revelation and demonic speech.
  • The wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23) — the same word as "second death."
  • Jesus interprets fire and brimstone as "destroyed them all" (Luke 17:29). Peter calls Sodom's reduction to ashes "an ensample" (2 Pet 2:6).

docs.title: What CANNOT Be Said (not explicitly stated or necessarily implied by Scripture)
docs.text:
• It cannot be said from the text that the "tormented for ever and ever" formula applies to human beings. No verse applies this formula to any human individual or class.
  • It cannot be said that being in the same lake necessarily means experiencing the same outcome. The text uses different vocabulary for different subjects at the same destination.
  • It cannot be said that the torment of a symbolic entity automatically transfers to the humans represented by that entity. The text applies different vocabulary to the symbol and to the humans within the system.
  • It cannot be said that basanizo is the standard biblical term for the final fate of human wicked. The word appears in judgment contexts only in Revelation's apocalyptic framework and in demonic speech.
  • It cannot be said that the "for ever and ever" formula is univocal across all subjects. The OT uses identical language for Edom (ended fire), and Revelation uses it for Babylon (found no more at all).
  • It cannot be said that the OT teaches ongoing torment for the Satan-figure. Ezekiel 28 describes that entity becoming ashes and existing never any more.

docs.title: Tally Summary
docs.text:
• Explicit statements: 37
  • Cond.: 7 (E17, E28, E29, E30, E32, E33, E34)
  • ECT: 0

  • Neutral: 30 (E1-E16, E18-E27, E31, E35-E37)

  • Necessary implications: 3

  • Cond.: 0
  • ECT: 0

  • Neutral: 3 (N1, N2, N3)

  • Inferences: 5

  • I-A (Evidence-Extending): 2 (I2 Cond., I3 Cond.)
  • I-B (Competing-Evidence): 2 (I1 ECT resolved Strong against, I5 ECT resolved Strong against)
  • I-C (Compatible External): 1 (I4 ECT)
  • I-D (Counter-Evidence External): 0

Position summary: - Conditionalist direction: 7 E + 0 N + 2 I-A = 9 items (all E-items in didactic genre with all gates passing) - ECT direction: 0 E + 0 N + 2 I-B (both resolved Strong against) + 1 I-C = 3 items (all at inference level) - Neutral: 30 E + 3 N = 33 items

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
Rev 20:10 names three subjects for the "tormented day and night for ever and ever" formula: the devil, the beast, and the false prophet. The text identifies all three as non-human or symbolic entities. The devil is a supernatural spirit being identified by a four-fold chain (Rev 12:9, 20:2) and called "the spirit" (Eph 2:2). The beast is a symbolic composite entity with seven heads, ten horns, and a multi-century temporal existence pattern (Rev 13:1-2, 17:8). The false prophet is the earth beast of Rev 13:11-17, identified by matching vocabulary in Rev 19:20.

Tree 3's Subject Gate fails for all three subjects. None is a literal human being. The Genre Gate independently fails because Revelation is an apocalyptic vision (Rev 1:1, semaino). The proposed ECT classification for Rev 20:10 does not survive the mechanical gate process.

The torment formula (basanisthesontai eis tous aionas ton aionon) appears once in Scripture — Rev 20:10 — and is applied only to these three non-human/symbolic entities. It is never applied to any human being anywhere in the Bible. When humans enter the lake of fire, the text consistently uses different vocabulary: devoured (Rev 20:9), slain (Rev 19:21), and the second death (Rev 20:14-15, 21:8).

Basanizo (G928) in judgment contexts appears only in Revelation's apocalyptic framework or in demonic speech. No epistle, Gospel didactic section, or OT passage uses it for the final fate of human wicked. Destruction/death vocabulary for human fate spans all genres and all authors.

The OT describes the Satan-figure (the same entity as Rev 20:10's devil) with destruction/cessation vocabulary: fire devours, becomes ashes, exists never any more (Ezek 28:18-19). The "for ever" formula is used for Edom (Isa 34:9-10), which is not still burning, and for Babylon (Rev 19:3), which is "found no more at all" (Rev 18:21-23).

Seven explicit statements at the conditionalist direction passed all four Tree 3 gates — all from didactic genres (epistles, Jesus' sayings, OT prophets, wisdom). Zero explicit statements at the ECT direction survived the gate process. The two I-B inferences (same lake = same experience; formula always means genuinely eternal) were both resolved Strong against the ECT reading based on the text's own vocabulary differentiation and the OT/NT evidence for subject-determined formula meaning.

The evidence at the E and N tiers is entirely Neutral (33 items documenting textual facts) or Conditionalist (7 items from didactic genres). The ECT case for Rev 20:10 rests entirely at the inference level (3 items: 2 I-B resolved Strong against, 1 I-C).

Study completed: 2026-06-04 Cross-references: etc6-12-tormented-forever (predecessor), etc7-11-smoke-ascending-forever (smoke formula), etc6-13-lake-of-fire-second-death (lake self-interpretation), for-ever-and-ever-revelation (formula analysis)

docs.text:
Rev 20:10 — Crux text and immediate context: The primary passage under investigation with surrounding narrative (Rev 20:7-15) - Rev 20:7-8 — Satan released after 1000 years, deceives nations — narrative context for v.10 - Rev 20:9 — Humans 'devoured' (katephagen) — different vocabulary from v.10 torment - Rev 20:10 — Crux text — devil, beast, false prophet 'tormented day and night for ever and ever' - Rev 20:14 — Death and hades cast into lake of fire — 'this is the second death' (predicate nominative identification) - Rev 20:15 — Humans cast into lake — no torment formula applied, only death

Beast/False Prophet identification passages: Key passages establishing beast and false prophet as symbolic entities - Rev 13:1-2 — Beast rises from sea with seven heads, ten horns — composite of Daniel 7 beasts, symbolic entity - Rev 13:11-17 — Earth beast (= false prophet) — two horns like a lamb, speaks as dragon, symbolic characteristics - Rev 17:8 — Beast 'was, and is not, and shall ascend' — temporal description impossible for literal human - Rev 19:20 — Beast and false prophet cast 'alive' (zontes) into lake — different from human treatment - Rev 19:21 — Human remnant 'slain' (apektanthesan) — destruction vocabulary for humans vs. 'alive' for symbolic entities - Rev 16:13 — Unclean spirits from dragon, beast, false prophet — counterfeit trinity as unit

Devil/Satan identification passages: Passages establishing the devil as non-human supernatural being - Rev 12:9 — Dragon = devil = Satan = serpent — explicit identification chain, non-human spirit being - Rev 20:2 — Dragon = serpent = devil = Satan — restates identification from 12:9 in immediate context - Heb 2:14 — Christ came to 'destroy' (katargeo) the one having the power of death, the devil — destruction language for Satan - 1 John 3:8 — Son of God was manifested to 'destroy' (luo) the works of the devil - Matt 25:41 — Eternal fire 'prepared for the devil and his angels' — primary designation for non-human entities

All 12 basanizo (G928) occurrences: Every NT use of basanizo for complete semantic range analysis - Matt 4:24 — Basanizo for physical illness — 'those which were taken with divers diseases and torments' - Matt 8:29 — Demons ask Jesus 'art thou come hither to torment (basanisai) us before the time?' — demons anticipate basanizo - Matt 14:24 — Basanizo for ship 'tossed' by waves — word does not require consciousness - Mark 5:7 — Demoniac says 'torment me not' using basanizo — demonic speech context - Mark 6:48 — Disciples 'toiling' (basanizo) in rowing — physical exertion, not judgment - Luke 8:28 — Demon begs Jesus 'torment me not' — parallel to Mark 5:7, demonic encounter - 2 Pet 2:8 — Lot 'vexed' (basanizo) his righteous soul — moral distress, not punishment - Rev 9:5 — Basanizo with explicit five-month time limit — word does not inherently mean eternal - Rev 11:10 — Two witnesses 'tormented' (basanizo) earth-dwellers — prophetic ministry, not punishment - Rev 12:2 — Woman 'pained' (basanizo) in childbirth — non-judgment use in Revelation itself - Rev 14:10 — Basanizo for beast-worshippers 'in the presence of the Lamb' — apocalyptic judgment context - Rev 20:10 — Crux text — devil, beast, false prophet 'tormented day and night for ever and ever'

OT background — fate of symbolic/supernatural entities: OT passages describing the judgment/destruction of beings referenced in Rev 20:10 - Isa 14:12-15 — OT: Lucifer/morning star brought down to sheol/pit — OT background for Satan's fate - Isa 34:9-10 — OT: Edom's 'smoke shall go up for ever' — identical language for ended judgment

Human fate vocabulary (non-torment): Passages using destruction/death vocabulary for human wicked - Rev 21:8 — Eight categories of human wicked — lake = second death, no torment formula

Additional Primary Verses: - Ezek 28:18-19 — OT: Satan becomes 'ashes upon the earth' and shall 'never be any more' — destruction language for same entity - Rev 1:1 — Revelation 'signified' (semaino) — genre marker for symbolic/apocalyptic communication

docs.title: Supporting Verses (24 — retrieve for context, no individual analysis)
docs.text:
• Rom 6:23 — Wages of sin is death (thanatos) — same word as 'second death' in Rev 20:14
  • 2 Pet 2:4 — Angels that sinned cast down to tartarus — punishment of supernatural beings
  • Jude 1:6 — Angels kept in everlasting chains under darkness — supernatural entity punishment
  • Gen 19:24-25 — Sodom destroyed by fire and brimstone — OT paradigm for lake of fire imagery
  • 2 Pet 2:6 — Sodom turned to ashes, 'example unto those that after should live ungodly'
  • Jude 1:7 — Sodom suffering 'vengeance of eternal fire' — yet reduced to ashes
  • Luke 17:29 — Fire and brimstone 'destroyed them all' — Jesus interprets Sodom as destruction
  • Dan 7:11 — Fourth beast slain, body given to burning flame — symbolic beast destroyed
  • Rev 17:9-11 — Seven heads = seven mountains = seven kings — symbolic decoding of beast
  • Rev 13:3 — Beast's deadly wound healed — symbolic characteristics impossible for literal individual
  • Matt 8:6 — Servant 'grievously tormented' (basanizo) — physical illness context
  • 1 Cor 15:26 — Last enemy destroyed is death — parallels death cast into lake in Rev 20:14
  • Matt 7:15 — Generic false prophets (pseudoprophetes, plural) — class of humans, distinct from singular in Rev
  • Matt 24:11 — Many false prophets (plural) — generic class vs. singular apocalyptic entity
  • Acts 13:6 — Bar-Jesus a false prophet (pseudoprophetes, singular) — human individual, not apocalyptic entity
  • 1 John 4:1 — Many false prophets (plural) gone into world — class usage vs. Revelation singular
  • Rev 18:21-23 — Babylon 'found no more at all' — fivefold cessation of symbolic entity
  • Rev 19:3 — Babylon's smoke rises 'for ever and ever' — same formula for an ended entity
  • Rev 20:1-3 — Satan bound 1000 years — narrative context establishing Satan as non-human agent
  • Matt 18:34 — Basanistes (G930) — 'tormentors' in parable context, related word family
  • Mal 4:1 — Day that shall burn as oven — wicked become 'stubble' burned up completely
  • Obad 1:16 — Wicked 'as though they had not been' — cessation language for humans
  • Psa 37:10 — Wicked 'shall not be' — OT destruction language for human wicked
  • Rev 14:11 — Smoke of torment ascending — parallel formula to 20:10 for comparison

docs.title: Focus Areas
docs.text:
1. The Three Named Subjects of Rev 20:10 — Identification: This is the foundational question of the entire study. READ the word studies for G1228-diabolos, G2342-therion, and G5578-pseudoprophetes from the library. For the devil: Rev 12:9 and 20:2 explicitly identify the dragon as 'that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan' — a supernatural spirit being, not a human. For the beast: Rev 13:1-2 describes a composite creature with seven heads, ten horns, body parts from four Daniel 7 beasts — a symbolic political-religious system, not a literal individual. READ the G2342-therion word study, noting that therion in Revelation is ALWAYS the apocalyptic beast-entity (38/46 occurrences). For the false prophet: Rev 19:20 identifies the false prophet as the one 'that wrought miracles before him' — matching the earth beast of Rev 13:11-17 exactly. READ G5578-pseudoprophetes and note the singular/plural distinction (3x singular in Rev = specific apocalyptic entity; 8x plural elsewhere = generic class of humans). Run greek_parser.py on Rev 20:10, 12:9, 13:1, 13:11, 19:20 to verify morphological forms. The verb basanisthesontai is 3rd person plural future passive, matching all three as compound subject. Verses: Rev 20:10, Rev 12:9, Rev 20:2, Rev 13:1-2, Rev 13:11-17, Rev 19:20, Rev 17:8, Rev 16:13 Strong's: G1228, G2342, G5578, G1404, G4567

  2. Basanizo (G928) Complete NT Usage Analysis — All 12 Occurrences: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G928-basanizo.md — the canonical entry documents all 12 tokens across 6 books. Run greek_parser.py on each occurrence: Matt 4:24 (illness), 8:6 (illness), 8:29 (demons), 14:24 (waves tossing ship), Mark 5:7 (demon), 6:48 (rowing), Luke 8:28 (demon), 2 Pet 2:8 (moral distress), Rev 9:5 (time-limited torment), 11:10 (prophetic witness), 12:2 (childbirth), 14:10 (judgment in apocalyptic), 20:10 (judgment in apocalyptic). The distribution is critical: 7 of 12 are NON-judgment (illness, waves, rowing, distress, childbirth), and the 5 judgment uses are ALL either in Revelation's apocalyptic framework or involve demons speaking of their own future. No epistle, no Gospel didactic section, and no OT passage uses basanizo for the final fate of generic human wicked. Also READ the word studies for G929-basanismos (6 occurrences, ALL in Revelation, 3 describing Babylon's completed destruction) and G931-basanos (3 occurrences — physical diseases and parabolic context). Check G930-basanistes (1 occurrence, Matt 18:34, parabolic). The word family root meaning is 'touchstone for testing metals' — the metaphorical extension to 'torment' is secondary. Verses: Matt 4:24, Matt 8:6, Matt 8:29, Matt 14:24, Mark 5:7, Mark 6:48, Luke 8:28, 2 Pet 2:8, Rev 9:5, Rev 11:10, Rev 12:2, Rev 14:10, Rev 20:10 Strong's: G928, G929, G931, G930

  3. Tree 3 Subject Gate Application to Rev 20:10: The research agent MUST read D:/bible/bible-studies/etc6-series-methodology.md to understand the Tree 3 decision tree. For each of the three subjects: (1) THE DEVIL — Is the devil a literal human being? Rev 12:9 identifies the devil as the dragon, that old serpent — a supernatural spirit being who predates humanity (Gen 3:1-5). Gate 1 automatic FAIL: 'a non-human spirit being.' (2) THE BEAST — Is the beast a literal human being? Rev 13:1 describes a creature with seven heads and ten horns rising from the sea, a composite of Daniel 7's four beasts. Rev 17:8 says the beast 'was, and is not, and shall ascend' — a temporal description impossible for a single human. Gate 1 automatic FAIL: 'a symbolic entity (a figure in an apocalyptic vision).' (3) THE FALSE PROPHET — Is the false prophet a literal human being? Rev 19:20 identifies the false prophet by the miracles matching Rev 13:13-14, making it the second beast of Rev 13:11 — described with symbolic features (two horns like a lamb, speaks as dragon, gives pneuma to an image). Gate 1 automatic FAIL: 'a symbolic entity.' Document each walkthrough with verse evidence from parser tools. Verses: Rev 20:10, Rev 12:9, Rev 13:1, Rev 17:8, Rev 19:20, Rev 13:11-14 Strong's: G1228, G2342, G5578, G1404

  4. The Beast — Symbolic Entity Identification (Rev 13, 17 Connections): READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G2342-therion.md — note the concentration of therion in Revelation (38 of 46 NT occurrences). The sea beast of Rev 13:1-2 has seven heads, ten horns, body parts from leopard, bear, lion — a deliberate composite of all four Daniel 7 beasts in reverse order. The seven heads = seven mountains = seven kings (Rev 17:9-11), making the beast a multi-century political-religious system. Rev 17:8 says the beast 'was, and is not, and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit' — a temporal existence pattern that no single human can fulfill. The beast counterfeits the Lamb through shared sphazo vocabulary (Rev 13:3 deadly wound parallel to Rev 5:6 Lamb slain). Run greek_parser.py on Rev 13:1-2, 17:8-11, and Dan 7:3-7 LXX for comparison. Also READ G4969-sphazo word study for the sphago counterfeit pattern. The prior study rev-11-sea-beast-daniels-composite extensively documents this — note its key findings about the composite nature. Verses: Rev 13:1-2, Rev 13:3, Rev 17:8, Rev 17:9-11, Dan 7:3-7, Dan 7:11, Rev 5:6 Strong's: G2342, G4969, G2776

  5. The False Prophet — Pseudoprophetes Singular vs. Plural Distinction: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G5578-pseudoprophetes.md — the canonical study documents all 11 NT occurrences. The crucial distinction: SINGULAR pseudoprophetes in Revelation (3x: Rev 16:13, 19:20, 20:10) always refers to one specific apocalyptic entity, while PLURAL pseudoprophetai (7x: Matt 7:15, 24:11, 24:24, Mark 13:22, Luke 6:26, 2 Pet 2:1, 1 John 4:1) refers to a class of human deceivers. Acts 13:6 is the one singular occurrence outside Revelation (Bar-Jesus, a specific human), but with a definite article and personal name — unlike the anarthrous apocalyptic entity. Rev 19:20 provides the identification key: the false prophet 'wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark' — this vocabulary matches Rev 13:13-14 exactly (poiesas ta semeia enopion autou), confirming the false prophet IS the earth beast of Rev 13:11-17. Run greek_parser.py on Rev 19:20 and Rev 13:13-14 to verify the vocabulary match. The earth beast has entirely symbolic characteristics: two horns like a lamb, speaks as a dragon, exercises delegated authority, gives breath to an image. Verses: Rev 16:13, Rev 19:20, Rev 20:10, Rev 13:11-17, Rev 13:13-14, Matt 7:15, Matt 24:11, Acts 13:6, 1 John 4:1, 2 Pet 2:1 Strong's: G5578, G4592, G4160

  6. Devil/Satan as Non-Human Entity — Biblical Identification: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G1228-diabolos.md (38 occurrences) and G4567-satanas.md (36 occurrences). Also READ H7854-satan.md for OT background. The identification chain: Gen 3:1-5 (serpent, pre-human), Rev 12:9 (dragon = serpent = devil = Satan), Ezek 28:14-19 (anointed cherub covering), Isa 14:12-15 (morning star/Lucifer). Key attributes that exclude human identity: existed before humanity (Gen 3), identified as a spirit being (Eph 2:2 'prince of the power of the air'), has angels under him (Matt 25:41, Rev 12:7-9), operates across millennia (Gen 3 through Rev 20). Critically, Heb 2:14 says Christ came to 'destroy' (katargeo) the devil — READ G2673-katargeo.md for the semantic range (27 occurrences: abolish, render powerless, nullify, destroy). Even the supernatural entity receives DESTRUCTION vocabulary. 1 John 3:8 adds 'to destroy (luo) the works of the devil.' Matt 25:41 identifies eternal fire as 'prepared for the devil and his angels' — the primary designation is for non-human entities. Run greek_parser.py on Heb 2:14 to verify katargeo morphology and on Matt 25:41 for the dative of advantage/purpose. Verses: Rev 12:9, Rev 20:2, Gen 3:1-5, Isa 14:12-15, Ezek 28:14-19, Heb 2:14, 1 John 3:8, Matt 25:41, Eph 2:2, Rev 12:7-9, Matt 8:29 Strong's: G1228, G4567, G2673, G3089, H7854

  7. Rev 20:10 vs. Rev 20:14-15 — Different Vocabulary for Different Subjects: This focus area examines the internal evidence of Rev 20:7-15 as a continuous literary unit. The text uses FOUR distinct vocabulary sets for FOUR distinct outcomes: (1) Human nations — 'devoured' (katephagen G2719, aorist active) by fire from heaven (v.9); (2) The devil — 'cast into' (eblethe) the lake, 'tormented' (basanisthesontai G928, future passive) day and night forever (v.10); (3) Death and hades — 'cast into' (eblethesan) the lake (v.14), personified entities destroyed per 1 Cor 15:26; (4) Humans not in book of life — 'cast into' (eblethe) the lake (v.15), identified as 'second death' (v.14). READ G2719-katesthio word study for the 'devoured' vocabulary. The torment formula (basanisthesontai eis tous aionas ton aionon) is applied ONLY in v.10 to the non-human/symbolic trio. When humans enter the lake (vv.14-15, 21:8), the term is consistently 'second death' (ho thanatos ho deuteros) — READ G2288-thanatos word study. Rev 19:20-21 provides a parallel contrast: beast and false prophet cast 'alive' (zontes, present participle) into the lake, while the human remnant is 'slain' (apektanthesan G615, aorist passive) — READ G615-apokteino word study. Run greek_parser.py on Rev 20:9, 20:10, 20:14, 20:15, 19:20, 19:21 to verify the vocabulary distribution. Verses: Rev 20:7-8, Rev 20:9, Rev 20:10, Rev 20:14, Rev 20:15, Rev 21:8, Rev 19:20, Rev 19:21, 1 Cor 15:26 Strong's: G928, G2719, G2288, G615, G3041, G979

  8. OT Background — Symbolic Entities Judged (Isa 14, Ezek 28, Dan 7): Three OT passages form the background for the fate of the entities in Rev 20:10. (1) ISAIAH 14:12-15 — The 'morning star' (Lucifer) brought down to sheol, to the sides of the pit. While the primary referent is the king of Babylon, the language transcends any human king and has been applied to Satan since the NT era (cf. Luke 10:18 'I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven'). The fate described is descent and humiliation, not ongoing torment. (2) EZEKIEL 28:14-19 — The 'anointed cherub that covereth' (again with dual reference) becomes 'ashes upon the earth' (v.18) and shall 'never be any more' (v.19). This is the most striking parallel: the SAME entity referenced in Rev 20:10 as 'tormented forever' is described in Ezek 28 as becoming ASHES and existing NO MORE. The Hebrew is absolute: lo od lo olam (never again forever). Run hebrew_parser.py on Ezek 28:18-19 to verify. (3) DANIEL 7:11 — The fourth beast is 'slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame' — destruction vocabulary for a symbolic beast-entity, which is the conceptual predecessor of Revelation's beast. Also note Isa 34:9-10 where identical 'for ever' smoke language describes Edom, which is not still burning — demonstrating that 'for ever' smoke language in the OT describes completed destruction. Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py on Rev 20:10 for additional OT connections. Verses: Isa 14:12-15, Ezek 28:14-19, Dan 7:11, Isa 34:9-10, Luke 10:18, Gen 3:14-15 Strong's: H1966, H3742, H665, H6083

  9. Lake of Fire as Symbol — Rev 20:14 Self-Interpretation: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G3041-limne.md (10 NT occurrences: 4x Lake of Gennesaret in Luke, 6x lake of fire in Revelation). The lake of fire appears in Rev 19:20, 20:10, 20:14, 20:15, and 21:8. Rev 20:14 provides an explicit self-interpretation: 'This is the second death' (houtos ho thanatos ho deuteros estin he limne tou pyros). Check the grammar reference for the symbol-decoding predicate-nominal entry at D:/bible/bible-studies/grammar-reference/greek/anarthrous-predicate-nominative.md and the Hebrew equivalent at D:/bible/bible-studies/grammar-reference/hebrew/symbol-decoding-predicate-nominal.md. The 'X is Y' formula in Revelation (Rev 1:20, 17:9, 17:15, 17:18) consistently functions as symbolic interpretation, not as a mere label. The lake of fire is identified as 'the second death' — a death concept, not a torment concept. READ G2303-theion (brimstone/sulfur) word study for the fire-and-brimstone imagery background. Also note that death and hades are cast INTO the lake (Rev 20:14), which are personified abstractions, not physical entities — the lake 'destroys' death itself, paralleling 1 Cor 15:26. Run greek_parser.py on Rev 20:14 to parse the predicate nominative construction. Verses: Rev 20:14, Rev 21:8, Rev 19:20, Rev 1:20, Rev 17:9, Rev 17:15, 1 Cor 15:26 Strong's: G3041, G2303, G2288, G4442

  10. Basanizo in Non-Judgment Contexts — Testing, Touchstone, Physical Distress: The basanizo word family derives from G931 basanos, originally a touchstone used for testing the purity of metals (a Lydian stone rubbed with gold to assess quality). READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G931-basanos.md — 3 NT occurrences: Matt 4:24 (physical diseases), Luke 16:23 (parabolic torment), Luke 16:28 (parabolic torment). The extended family: G928 basanizo (12x, 'test/torment/toss/vex/pain'), G929 basanismos (6x, all in Revelation), G930 basanistes (1x, Matt 18:34 parabolic 'tormentors'), G931 basanos (3x). READ G930-basanistēs.md. The non-judgment occurrences of basanizo are revealing: Matt 4:24 and 8:6 use it for physical illness with no moral component; Matt 14:24 applies it to a ship being 'tossed' by waves — the word does NOT require a conscious subject experiencing punishment; Mark 6:48 uses it for the physical strain of rowing against wind; 2 Pet 2:8 uses it for Lot's righteous soul being 'vexed' by Sodom's wickedness — moral distress, not divine punishment; Rev 12:2 uses it for the pain of childbirth. The KJV translators used five DIFFERENT English words for this single Greek word (tormented, tossed, toiling, vexed, pained), recognizing its semantic breadth. Run search_strongs.py --lexicon G928 for the full lexical entry. Verses: Matt 4:24, Matt 8:6, Matt 14:24, Mark 6:48, 2 Pet 2:8, Rev 12:2, Matt 18:34, Luke 16:23, Luke 16:28 Strong's: G928, G931, G930, G929

  11. The 'Beast-as-Representative' Counter-Argument: etc6-12 addressed this in its 'What CANNOT Be Said' section. The key question: even if the beast represents a system composed of human adherents, does Rev 20:10's torment formula transfer to those humans? The text's own vocabulary argues NO. Rev 19:20-21 provides the clearest evidence: the beast and false prophet are cast 'alive' (zontes) into the lake, while the human remnant is 'slain' (apektanthesan) by the sword. The text deliberately uses DIFFERENT verbs for the symbolic entities and for their human followers IN THE SAME NARRATIVE. Rev 20:9 likewise describes the human followers of the post-millennium Satan as 'devoured' (katephagen) by fire — destruction vocabulary, not torment vocabulary. Rev 21:8 lists eight categories of human sinners and assigns them 'the second death' — not the torment formula. The text itself maintains the vocabulary distinction even when describing the same event. What CAN be said: the beast represents a system. What CANNOT be said from the text: that the torment formula applied to the symbolic entity automatically transfers to the humans within that system, because the text explicitly applies different vocabulary to them. Verses: Rev 20:10, Rev 19:20-21, Rev 20:9, Rev 21:8, Rev 14:9-11, Rev 13:7-8 Strong's: G2342, G615, G2719, G2288, G979

  12. The 'For Ever and Ever' Formula — Subject-Determined Meaning: READ D:/bible/bible-studies/word-studies/G165-aion.md and G166-aionios.md for the semantic range of the aion word family. The formula 'eis tous aionas ton aionon' (unto the ages of the ages) occurs approximately 13 times in Revelation: 9x for God's existence and reign (genuinely endless: Rev 1:6, 4:9-10, 5:13, 7:12, 10:6, 11:15, 15:7, 22:5), 1x for saints' reign (genuinely endless: Rev 22:5), and 3x for judgment contexts (Rev 14:11, 19:3, 20:10). The crucial observation: the formula's meaning appears SUBJECT-DETERMINED. Applied to the eternal God, it is genuinely eternal. Applied to judgment, the OT parallel in Isa 34:10 (smoke of Edom ascending 'for ever' — yet Edom is not still burning and animals inhabit the ruins, Isa 34:11-17) shows the formula can describe a permanent, irreversible result rather than an ongoing process. Rev 19:3 applies the identical formula to Babylon's smoke, and Rev 18:21-23 describes Babylon as 'found no more at all' with fivefold cessation — the smoke formula describes a completed, permanent destruction. Cross-reference the prior study for-ever-and-ever-revelation which extensively documents this pattern. Verses: Rev 20:10, Rev 14:11, Rev 19:3, Rev 1:6, Rev 4:9-10, Isa 34:9-10, Isa 34:11-17, Rev 18:21-23 Strong's: G165, G166

docs.title: Research Instructions
docs.text:
You are the Research Agent. Execute this study by:

  1. Read the SKILL.md for full tool documentation and principles
  2. Read your agent instructions at agents/research-agent.md
  3. Read ALL library entries listed in "Available Library Entries" above
  4. Follow the workflow from the skill
  5. Write research files to this folder:
  6. 01-topics.md — Nave's topics and full entries (retrieve full entries for: SATAN, DEMONS, ANTICHRIST, TORMENTS, LAKE, SECOND DEATH, BRIMSTONE, JUDGMENT, SODOM, DEATH, LUCIFER, KINGDOM OF SATAN, HADES, ASHES)
  7. 02-verses.md — All verse texts retrieved with context for:
    • Rev 20:10 — Crux text and immediate context (Rev 20:7-8, Rev 20:9, Rev 20:10, Rev 20:14, Rev 20:15) — retrieve with FULL chapter context
    • Beast/False Prophet identification passages (Rev 13:1-2, Rev 13:11-17, Rev 17:8, Rev 17:9-11, Rev 19:20...) — retrieve with FULL chapter context
    • Devil/Satan identification passages (Rev 12:9, Rev 20:2, Rev 20:1-3, Gen 3:1-5, Heb 2:14...)
    • All 12 basanizo (G928) occurrences (Matt 4:24, Matt 8:6, Matt 8:29, Matt 14:24, Mark 5:7...)
    • OT background — fate of symbolic/supernatural entities (Isa 14:12-15, Ezek 28:14-19, Dan 7:11, Isa 34:9-10, Gen 19:24-25)
    • Human fate vocabulary (non-torment) (Rev 21:8, Rom 6:23, Mal 4:1, Obad 1:16, Psa 37:10...)
    • All additional verses from Nave's topic entries
  8. 04-word-studies.md — Strong's research:
    • FROM LIBRARY (read, don't re-derive): G928 (basanizo), G929 (basanismos), G931 (basanos), G930 (basanistes), G2342 (therion), G5578 (pseudoprophetes), G1228 (diabolos), G4567 (satanas), G1404 (drakon), G3041 (limne), G2303 (theion), G2673 (katargeo), G2719 (katesthio), G2288 (thanatos), G165 (aion), G166 (aionios), G622 (apollymi), G615 (apokteino), G4969 (sphazo), G4442 (pyr)
  9. raw-data/ — Raw tool output organized by category
  10. Do NOT write 03-analysis.md or CONCLUSION.md — those are for the analysis agent

docs.title: Specific Research Directives
docs.text:
1. Priority verses to retrieve with FULL CHAPTER context:
  2. Rev 20:1-15
  3. Rev 19:11-21
  4. Rev 13:1-18
  5. Rev 17:1-18
  6. Rev 12:1-17
  7. Rev 21:1-8
  8. Ezek 28:11-19

  9. Isa 14:3-20

  10. Required Greek/Hebrew parsing:

  11. Rev 20:10 — Parse basanisthesontai (future passive 3pl) — confirm compound subject agreement; parse 'eis tous aionas ton aionon' formula
  12. Rev 20:9 — Parse katephagen (aorist active) — confirm human subject with destruction verb
  13. Rev 20:14 — Parse predicate nominative 'houtos ho thanatos ho deuteros estin' — X=Y identification formula
  14. Rev 19:20 — Parse zontes (present participle 'alive') — confirm symbolic entities cast 'alive' vs. humans slain
  15. Rev 19:21 — Parse apektanthesan (aorist passive) — confirm human remnant 'slain' with different vocabulary
  16. Heb 2:14 — Parse katargese (aorist subjunctive of katargeo) — destruction vocabulary applied to the devil
  17. Rev 12:9 — Parse the four-part identification chain: dragon = serpent = devil = Satan
  18. Rev 13:1-2 — Parse beast description — seven heads, ten horns, composite body; symbolic features
  19. Rev 9:5 — Parse basanismos with time limit (menas pente) — bounded duration with torment word

  20. Ezek 28:18-19 — Parse Hebrew 'epher' (ashes) and 'eneka od lo olam' (never any more) — destruction of Satan figure

  21. Required cross-testament parallels (run BOTH --hybrid-ot AND --hybrid-nt):

  22. Rev 20:10 — OT and NT parallels for the torment formula and lake of fire judgment
  23. Rev 20:14 — OT background for 'second death' concept and death personification
  24. Heb 2:14 — OT and NT parallels for destruction of the devil
  25. Matt 25:41 — Parallels for 'eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels'

  26. Isa 34:9-10 — Parallel formula 'smoke shall go up for ever' for ended judgment

docs.title: "Tormented Forever and Ever" -- What Does Rev 20:10 Actually Say?
The Verse in Question
docs.text:
"And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever." -- Rev 20:10

This is the strongest verse cited in favor of eternal conscious torment. It deserves careful attention. What does the phrase "tormented day and night for ever and ever" actually communicate when read inside its own context?

docs.title: "Forever and Ever" Communicates Total Completeness
docs.text:
The phrase "for ever and ever" (Greek: eis tous aionas ton aionon) does not carry a single fixed meaning throughout Scripture. Its meaning depends on what it is applied to.

Applied to God, it means genuinely eternal -- God lives and reigns forever (Rev 4:9-10, 15:7). Applied to judgment, the Old Testament shows it communicates the total completeness and permanence of the result. Isaiah 34:9-10 says Edom's smoke "shall go up for ever" and its fire is "not quenched night nor day" -- yet the very next verses (34:11-17) describe animals nesting in the ruins. Edom is not still burning. The "forever" language describes how complete the destruction was, not an ongoing process.

Revelation itself confirms this pattern. Babylon's smoke rises "for ever and ever" (Rev 19:3), yet five times the text says Babylon is "found no more at all" (Rev 18:21-23). The forever language and the cessation language sit side by side for the same subject. "Forever" describes the permanence of the outcome, not an unending process.

docs.title: The Torment Leads to Destruction
docs.text:
The Old Testament consistently shows a pattern where torment is a process that produces destruction as its outcome. Prophets like Isaiah, Nahum, and Zephaniah describe anguish and distress leading to consumption and ruin (Isa 13:8-9, Nah 1:9-10, Zeph 1:15,18). Torment is the road; destruction is the destination.

Rev 20:10 sits inside a destruction framework. One verse earlier, fire from heaven "devoured" the human armies (Rev 20:9) -- that is completed destruction. Four verses later, the lake of fire is defined as "the second death" (Rev 20:14). The torment of verse 10 is bracketed on both sides by destruction language. "Forever and ever" applied to the torment tells us the process runs to total completion -- and completed torment produces the destruction that the surrounding verses describe.

docs.title: The Broader Biblical Picture
docs.text:
When the Bible describes the final fate of human beings outside of Revelation's apocalyptic imagery, it uses destruction and death vocabulary consistently:

  • Jesus: "Fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body" (Matt 10:28). Fire and brimstone "destroyed them all" (Luke 17:29).
  • Paul: "The wages of sin is death" (Rom 6:23) -- not torment, but death.
  • Peter: Sodom was "turned to ashes," set as "an example to those that after should live ungodly" (2 Pet 2:6).
  • Old Testament prophets: The wicked become stubble burned up with "neither root nor branch" (Mal 4:1). They "shall be as though they had not been" (Obad 1:16).

The word "torment" (basanizo) in judgment contexts appears only in Revelation's symbolic visions and in demons speaking of their own fate (Matt 8:29). It never appears in any epistle, any teaching passage, or any Old Testament prophecy describing what happens to human beings in the end. Destruction and death language for the human fate spans every genre and every biblical author.

docs.title: What the Lake of Fire Is
docs.text: Revelation interprets itself. Rev 20:14 states plainly: "This is the second death." The lake of fire is a death -- the final, permanent, irreversible death. When human beings enter it, the text calls it death, not torment. The contrast Paul draws is not torment versus bliss, but death versus eternal life (Rom 6:23).

docs.title: The Bottom Line
docs.text: "Tormented day and night for ever and ever" communicates the absolute completeness of the judgment process. The "forever" formula, as the Old Testament and Revelation itself demonstrate, describes how total and permanent the result is -- not an unending activity. The torment runs to full completion, and completed torment produces destruction, exactly as the verses on either side of Rev 20:10 describe. The lake of fire is the second death. The wages of sin is death. The fire and brimstone that fell on Sodom "destroyed them all." That is the Bible's own interpretation of its own imagery.

docs.title: Cross-Testament Parallels
docs.text:
• Rev 20:10 → Isa 34:10 (ot, vocabulary + formula: 'for ever' smoke language for ended judgment; 'night nor day' parallels 'day and night')
  • Rev 20:10 → Rev 19:20 (nt, direct narrative link: beast/false prophet already in lake when devil arrives; vocabulary match for false prophet identification)
  • Rev 20:10 → Rev 14:11 (nt, vocabulary + formula: ages-of-ages formula, torment language, beast-worshippers)
  • Rev 20:10 → Rev 20:14 (nt, same narrative unit: different vocabulary for different subjects at the same lake)
  • Rev 20:10 → Matt 25:41 (nt, shared subject: eternal fire 'prepared for the devil and his angels' — primary non-human designation)
  • Rev 20:10 → Rev 12:9 (nt, identification: dragon = serpent = devil = Satan (subject identification for Rev 20:10))
  • Rev 20:10 → Ezek 28:18-19 (ot, same entity (Satan-figure): becomes ashes, exists no more — destruction language for same being)
  • Rev 20:10 → Heb 2:14 (nt, shared subject: Christ came to 'destroy' (katargeo) the devil — destruction vocabulary for same entity)
  • Rev 20:10 → Rev 16:13 (nt, counterfeit trinity unit: dragon + beast + false prophet identified as a unit)
  • Rev 20:10 → Rev 21:8 (nt, vocabulary contrast: human categories at lake = 'second death' (no torment formula))
  • Rev 19:3 → Rev 18:21-23 (nt, same entity (Babylon): smoke 'for ever and ever' (19:3) yet 'found no more at all' (18:21))
  • Rev 20:14 → 1 Cor 15:26 (nt, shared concept: death as last enemy to be 'destroyed' — parallels death cast into lake)
  • Heb 2:14 → Gen 3:15 (ot, proto-evangelium: seed of woman to crush serpent's head — destruction of the devil promised from Eden)
  • Rev 20:9 → Ezek 38:22 (ot, Gog/Magog: fire from heaven against nations surrounding God's people — destruction vocabulary)
  • Jude 1:7 → Gen 19:24 (ot, Sodom paradigm: 'eternal fire' that produced ashes — permanent result, not ongoing process)

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Lake of fire in Revelation. 'Second death' (Rev 2:11; 20:6,14; 21:8). Rev 20:14 ('lake of fire IS the second death'). Death/hell cast into lake (Rev 20:14). What is the lake of fire? What is the second death? What does it mean that Rev 20:14 identifies the lake of fire AS the second death? What does it mean that death and hades are cast into the lake of fire? Who are the subjects who enter the lake? What do Rev 2:11 and 20:6 say about overcomers and the second death? How does the 'second death' function as the text's own explanation of what the lake does?

docs.text: Lake of fire in Revelation. 'Second death' (Rev 2:11; 20:6,14; 21:8). Rev 20:14 ('lake of fire IS the second death'). Death/hell cast into lake (Rev 20:14). What is the lake of fire? How does the 'second death' function as the text's own explanation of what the lake does?

docs.title: Beast and false prophet cast alive into lake; human remnant slain
docs.text:
19:20 And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. 19:21 And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which [sword] proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.

Context: Armageddon battle scene. Christ on white horse defeats the beast and its coalition. First subjects cast into the lake of fire. Critical vocabulary differentiation: beast/false prophet cast 'alive' (zontes) vs human remnant 'slain' (apektanthesan).

Notes: Rev 19:20 uses zontes (V-PAP-NPM, present active participle of zao G2198) for the beast/false prophet being cast 'alive' into the lake. Rev 19:21 uses apektanthesan (V-API-3P, aorist passive indicative of apokteino G615) for the human remnant being 'slain.' The vocabulary differentiation is stark: symbolic entities receive 'alive' language; humans receive death/slaying language.

docs.title: First resurrection and second death pairing
docs.text:
20:5 But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This [is] the first resurrection. 20:6 Blessed and holy [is] he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him a thousand years.

Context: Millennium passage. First resurrection participants are exempt from the second death. The structural pairing implies: first resurrection exempts from second death; implied second resurrection (of 'the rest of the dead') leads to second death.

Notes: Rev 20:6: 'ho deuteros thanatos ouk echei exousian' -- the second death does not have authority/jurisdiction/power (exousia G1849) over first resurrection participants. Exousia is a delegated-authority word, not a force word. The second death's domain is limited; it has no jurisdictional reach over the blessed.

docs.title: Fire from heaven devours human armies -- destruction vocabulary for humans
docs.text:
And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.

Context: Post-millennium. Gog and Magog armies surround the beloved city. Fire from God devours them. ONE VERSE before the torment formula for the devil in v.10.

Notes: katephagen (V-2AAI-3S, second aorist active indicative of katesthio G2719) -- 'devoured.' This is consumption/destruction vocabulary. The word means to eat down, consume utterly. Applied to human armies. The contrast with v.10 (basanisthesontai for the devil) is immediate and dramatic.

docs.title: Torment formula -- applied ONLY to devil, beast, false prophet
docs.text:
And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet [are], and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.

Context: The devil joins the beast and false prophet in the lake. The torment formula (basanisthesontai eis tous aionas ton aionon) appears here and ONLY here for lake-of-fire subjects. Never applied to any human.

Notes: basanisthesontai (V-FPI-3P, future passive indicative of basanizo G928) -- 'they shall be tormented.' The subject is the devil, beast, and false prophet -- all non-human/symbolic entities. The future tense (only future verb in the aorist chain of vv.9-14) projects the consequence beyond the vision's timeframe. 'hemeras kai nyktos' (genitive of time) = continuous; 'eis tous aionas ton aionon' (ages of the ages) = Semitic superlative formula.

docs.title: Great white throne judgment -- death/hades cast in; humans not in book of life cast in
docs.text:
20:13 And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. 20:14 And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. 20:15 And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

Context: The culmination of the judgment sequence. Death and hades first act as agents (deliver up the dead, v.13) then become patients (are cast into the lake, v.14). The predicate nominative identification formula defines the lake of fire AS the second death. The book of life is the criterion for human subjects.

Notes: Rev 20:14: 'houtos ho thanatos ho deuteros estin, he limne tou puros' -- this is the X=Y identification formula. Subject: houtos ho thanatos ho deuteros (demonstrative + articular noun + articular ordinal, maximally definite). Copula: estin (V-PAI-3S). Predicate nominative: he limne tou puros (articular, definite). The text uses thanatos (death) vocabulary, NOT basanismos (torment) or kolasis (punishment). This is the text's own interpretive key: the lake of fire IS death -- the second death. Rev 20:15: first-class conditional (ei + indicative) -- the condition is assumed to have occurred.

docs.title: No more death -- the stated outcome of the lake of fire sequence
docs.text:
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

Context: New creation passage. Immediately following the lake of fire sequence. This is the STATED OUTCOME: no more death. If death and hades have been cast into the lake (Rev 20:14), and the lake IS the second death, then the result is the abolition of death itself.

Notes: ho thanatos ouk estai eti (the death not shall-be anymore) -- future middle indicative of eimi with negation. Death as a category of existence is abolished. The key question for ECT: if billions are being consciously tormented forever, how can there be 'no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain'?

docs.title: Eight categories of wicked -- their part IS the second death
docs.text:
But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.

Context: New creation passage. Eight categories of wicked humans identified. Their 'part' (meros G3313) is the lake. The identification formula repeats: 'ho estin ho thanatos ho deuteros' -- which IS the second death.

Notes: to meros auton (N-NSN, their part/portion) -- meros denotes an allotted share or portion. The eight categories: deilois (fearful/cowardly), apistois (unbelieving), ebdelygmenois (abominable, perf pass ptcp of bdelyssomai), phoneusin (murderers), pornois (fornicators), pharmakois (sorcerers), eidololatrais (idolaters), pasin tois pseudesin (all liars). Again, the identification formula uses thanatos vocabulary, not basanismos.

docs.title: Overcomer promise: second death cannot hurt the overcomer
docs.text:
2:10 Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast [some] of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. 2:11 He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.

Context: Letter to Smyrna. First/second death contrast: 'faithful unto death' (first death, martyrdom) in v.10, then 'not hurt of the second death' in v.11. The overcomer who endures the first death is exempt from the second.

Notes: Rev 2:11: 'ho nikon ou me adikethei ek tou thanatou tou deuterou.' ou me + adikethei (V-APS-3S, aorist passive subjunctive of adikeo G91) = strongest possible Greek negation. The overcomer will ABSOLUTELY NOT be hurt/wronged by the second death. adikeo means to wrong, injure, harm -- the second death's effect is described as 'hurting,' consistent with it being actual death rather than ongoing torment.

docs.title: Book of life overcomer promise -- complementary to second death exemption
docs.text:
He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.

Context: Letter to Sardis. Overcomer promise: not blotted from book of life. Two sides of the same coin with Rev 2:11: in the book = exempt from second death; NOT in the book = subject to second death (Rev 20:15).

Notes: ou me exaleipso (V-FAI-1S under ou me) -- emphatic future denial with ou me + future indicative. 'I will by no means blot out.' Same emphatic negation construction as Rev 2:11.

docs.title: Christ holds keys of death and hades -- authority over entities later destroyed
docs.text:
[I am] he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.

Context: Christ's self-identification. He holds the keys (authority) of hades and death -- the very entities that are later cast into the lake of fire (Rev 20:14). Christ's authority over death is the precondition for death's eventual abolition.

Notes: Christ's resurrection ('was dead, and am alive for evermore') gives him authority (keys) over death and hades. These are the same two entities personified as the fourth horseman's companions (Rev 6:8) and later cast into the lake (Rev 20:14).

docs.title: Death and hades personified as riders -- same entities later destroyed
docs.text:
And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.

Context: Fourth seal. Death personified as a named rider; hades follows. They are given authority (exousia) to kill. The same pair appears in Rev 20:13-14 delivering up the dead and then being cast into the lake.

Notes: Death and hades are consistently personified in Revelation as powers/entities, not persons. Their casting into the lake of fire (Rev 20:14) abolishes them as conditions/states, resulting in 'no more death' (Rev 21:4).

docs.title: X=Y identification formula: stars ARE angels, candlesticks ARE churches
docs.text:
The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.

Context: First occurrence of the X=Y self-interpreting formula in Revelation. Uses eisin (V-PAI-3P) copula to equate symbols with their referents. Same grammatical pattern as Rev 20:14.

Notes: Pattern: subject (symbol) + copula eisin/estin + predicate nominative (referent). This is the text's self-interpretation mechanism. Rev 20:14 uses the identical construction.

docs.title: X=Y identification formulas: heads ARE mountains, waters ARE peoples, woman IS city
docs.text:
17:9 And here [is] the mind which hath wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman sitteth. 17:15 And he saith unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues. 17:18 And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.

Context: Three more X=Y identification formulas in Rev 17, all using eisin/estin. The same interpretive pattern as Rev 20:14.

Notes: These formulas demonstrate that when Revelation says X IS Y, the text commits to full identity between the image and its referent. When Rev 20:14 says 'this is the second death,' it is using the identical hermeneutical mechanism.

docs.title: X=Y formula: odours ARE prayers of saints
docs.text:
And when he had taken the book, the four beasts and four [and] twenty elders fell down before the Lamb, having every one of them harps, and golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints.

Context: Another X=Y identification: odours = prayers. Same eisin copula pattern.

Notes: The X=Y formula appears across Revelation consistently equating symbolic images with their referents.

docs.title: OT prototype of X=Y symbol-decoding formula
docs.text:
41:26 The seven good kine [are] seven years; and the seven good ears [are] seven years: the dream [is] one. 41:27 And the seven thin and ill favoured kine that came up after them [are] seven years; and the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind shall be seven years of famine.

Context: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dream using verbless nominal clauses (Hebrew NmCl). The prototype of the X=Y symbol-decoding pattern that runs through Daniel and Revelation.

Notes: Hebrew verbless nominal clause (juxtaposition): subject (visionary element) + predicate (referent). Same pattern as Dan 2:38, Dan 8:20-21.

docs.title: OT X=Y formula: Thou ART this head of gold
docs.text:
And wheresoever the children of men dwell, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the heaven hath he given into thine hand, and hath made thee ruler over them all. Thou [art] this head of gold.

Context: Daniel's interpretation of Nebuchadnezzar's dream using Aramaic pronominal copula. 'ante-hu resha di dahaba' -- Thou art this head of gold.

Notes: Aramaic pronominal copula: ante-hu (2ms pron + 3ms pron as copula). Same X=Y pattern as Revelation's identification formulas.

docs.title: The last enemy destroyed is death -- katargeo applied to death
docs.text:
The last enemy [that] shall be destroyed [is] death.

Context: Paul's resurrection argument. Death is an enemy that will be destroyed (katargeo G2673). The verb means to render inoperative, abolish, do away with. This is fulfilled in Rev 20:14.

Notes: katargeitai (V-PPI-3S, present passive indicative of katargeo G2673) -- 'is being destroyed' or 'shall be destroyed.' Present tense here may be futuristic or progressive. Same word used for Christ abolishing death in 2 Tim 1:10 and destroying the devil in Heb 2:14.

docs.title: Death swallowed up in victory -- quoting Isa 25:8 and Hos 13:14
docs.text:
15:54 So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory. 15:55 O death, where [is] thy sting? O grave, where [is] thy victory?

Context: Paul quotes two OT texts: Isa 25:8 ('death swallowed up in victory') and Hos 13:14 ('O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?'). The death-of-death theme connects to Rev 20:14.

Notes: Katephothe (V-API-3S, aorist passive indicative of katapino G2666) -- 'was swallowed up.' Death is swallowed/consumed -- destruction vocabulary applied to death itself. nikos (G3534) = victory, conquest. The apostrophe to death in v.55 personifies death as a defeated enemy.

docs.title: OT foundation: God will swallow up death in victory
docs.text:
He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken [it].

Context: Isaiah's prophecy of death's end. Directly quoted in 1 Cor 15:54. The 'wipe away tears' language is echoed in Rev 21:4.

Notes: Hebrew: bala (H1104, to swallow up) + maveth (H4194, death) + lanetsach (H5331, forever/in victory). The LXX renders this with katapino + thanatos + nikos. Rev 21:4 directly echoes 'wipe away tears from all faces.'

docs.title: OT apostrophe to death: O death, I will be thy plagues
docs.text:
I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction: repentance shall be hid from mine eyes.

Context: God addresses death and the grave directly, promising to be their plagues and destruction. Quoted in 1 Cor 15:55.

Notes: maveth (H4194) and sheol (H7585) paired. God promises to destroy death itself -- the same theme that culminates in Rev 20:14.

docs.title: Christ hath abolished death -- katargeo applied to death
docs.text:
But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who hath abolished death, and hath brought life and immortality to light through the gospel:

Context: Paul declares Christ has abolished (katargeo G2673) death. Same verb as 1 Cor 15:26.

Notes: katargesantos (V-AAP-GSM, aorist active participle of katargeo G2673) -- 'having abolished.' The aorist participle treats the abolition as a completed act at the cross/resurrection. The contrast: death abolished vs. life and incorruption brought to light.

docs.title: Christ destroys the devil who had the power of death
docs.text:
Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;

Context: Christ took on flesh to destroy (katargeo) the devil who had the power (kratos) of death. This connects to Rev 20:10 (devil cast into lake) and Rev 20:14 (death cast into lake).

Notes: katargese (V-AAS-3S, aorist active subjunctive of katargeo G2673) -- 'he might destroy.' Purpose clause (hina + aorist subjunctive). The same katargeo applied to death (1 Cor 15:26, 2 Tim 1:10) is here applied to the devil. The identification 'tout' estin ton diabolon' ('that is, the devil') uses the same X=Y formula.

docs.title: Binding of Satan -- millennium context (preceding the lake of fire)
docs.text:
20:1 And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. 20:2 And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, 20:3 And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.

Context: Sets up the millennium context. The dragon/devil/Satan identification in v.2 uses the naming-copula pattern (four-fold identification). After the millennium, Satan is loosed (20:7) and eventually cast into the lake (20:10).

Notes: Rev 20:2: four-fold identification of the dragon: ho drakon ho archaios, hos estin Diabolos kai ho Satanas -- the great dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan. Confirms the non-human identity of the entity tormented in Rev 20:10.

docs.title: OT fire-and-brimstone paradigm: Sodom destroyed, not eternally tormented
docs.text:
19:24 Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven; 19:25 And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.

Context: The original fire-and-brimstone event. The outcome is destruction/overthrow (haphak H2015), not ongoing torment. Every NT reference to Sodom interprets the event as destruction.

Notes: haphak (H2015) = to overthrow, overturn, destroy completely. The fire produced total destruction, not eternal burning.

docs.title: Wicked as stubble burned up, become ashes under feet
docs.text:
4:1 For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch. 4:2 But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall. 4:3 And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do [this], saith the LORD of hosts.

Context: Final OT prophecy. The wicked = stubble, burned up, leaving neither root nor branch. They become ashes. The outcome is complete cessation of existence.

Notes: Three outcome words: stubble (qash), burned up (lahat), ashes (epher H665). The wicked become ashes under the feet of the righteous. This is annihilation/cessation language, not eternal torment.

docs.title: Edom's smoke ascending forever -- yet the fire ended
docs.text:
34:9 And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. 34:10 It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.

Context: Edom's judgment uses 'smoke ascending forever' language. Yet Isa 34:11-17 describes animals dwelling in the ruins -- the fire ended. The 'forever' language describes finality of destruction, not duration of burning.

Notes: The 'smoke ascending forever' formula appears in Rev 14:11 and 19:3 (Babylon). In both cases, the context shows the entities are destroyed, not eternally burning. Isa 34 is the OT paradigm for this formula.

docs.title: Sodom turned to ashes as an ensample for the ungodly
docs.text:
And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned [them] with an overthrow, making [them] an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;

Context: Peter explicitly states the fire-and-brimstone event produced ASHES (tephroo G5077) and serves as an ENSAMPLE (hupodeigma) for future ungodly persons. The exemplary outcome is ashes/destruction.

Notes: tephrosas (aorist active participle of tephroo G5077) = 'having turned to ashes.' The word is unique in the NT. katastrophe (G2692) = 'overthrow/catastrophe.' Peter identifies the Sodom outcome as the paradigm for what awaits the ungodly.

docs.title: Sodom suffering vengeance of eternal fire -- yet the fire ended
docs.text:
Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.

Context: Jude describes Sodom as 'suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.' Yet the fire ended -- the cities were destroyed. 'Eternal fire' describes the permanence of the result, not the duration of the burning.

Notes: puros aioniou (G4442 + G166) = 'eternal fire.' Sodom is not still burning. The 'eternal' qualifies the finality/irreversibility of the judgment, not the duration of the flames.

docs.title: Jesus interprets Sodom fire: destroyed them all (apollymi)
docs.text:
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed [them] all.

Context: Jesus's own interpretation of the Sodom event. He uses apollymi (G622) -- 'destroyed them all.' Not 'tormented them all.'

Notes: apolesen (V-AAI-3S, aorist active indicative of apollymi G622) = 'destroyed.' Jesus interprets the fire-and-brimstone paradigm as destruction. This is Jesus's own hermeneutical key for the fire-and-brimstone motif.

docs.title: Eternal fire prepared for the devil; everlasting punishment for humans
docs.text:
25:41 Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels: 25:46 And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.

Context: The fire's primary designation is for the devil and his angels (non-human). Humans are sent into fire that was 'prepared for' (hetoimazo G2090) non-human entities. The punishment vocabulary for humans is kolasis (G2851), not basanismos.

Notes: hetoimasmenon (V-RPP-ASN, perfect passive participle of hetoimazo G2090) = 'having been prepared.' The fire is pre-prepared for the devil, not for humans. kolasis aionion (G2851 + G166) = 'everlasting punishment' for humans. kolasis (only 2 NT uses: Matt 25:46, 1 John 4:18) etymologically derives from kolazo = to curtail/prune, carrying corrective connotation. The Aristotelian distinction: kolasis = corrective; timoria = retributive.

docs.title: Satan-figure becomes ashes, exists never any more
docs.text:
28:18 Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee. 28:19 All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never [shalt] thou [be] any more.

Context: The anointed cherub (Satan-figure) of Ezek 28. Outcome: devoured by fire, turned to ashes, exists 'never any more.' OT destruction language for the same being that Revelation says is 'tormented.'

Notes: akal (H398) = devour; epher (H665) = ashes; ayin (H369) = not exist, 'never any more.' The OT describes the Satan-figure's end as annihilation. Revelation's 'torment' language for the same figure must be read in light of this OT background.

docs.title: Fourth beast slain, body destroyed, given to burning flame
docs.text:
I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld [even] till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame.

Context: Daniel's vision of the fourth beast. The beast is slain, its body destroyed, and given to the burning flame. OT destruction language for a symbolic beast entity.

Notes: The Danielic beast is slain (qetal) and destroyed (abad H7) and given to fire. This is destruction vocabulary for a symbolic entity -- compare with Rev 19:20 where the Revelation beast is cast 'alive' into the lake.

docs.title: Wages of sin is death -- same word as 'second death'
docs.text:
For the wages of sin [is] death; but the gift of God [is] eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Context: Paul's clearest statement of the sin-death nexus. The penalty (opsonia = wages, soldier's pay) of sin is thanatos. The same word thanatos is used in 'second death.' The binary: death vs. eternal life -- no third option.

Notes: thanatos (G2288) = death. zoe aionios (G2222 + G166) = eternal life. The binary is death vs. life, not torment vs. life.

docs.title: Perish vs. everlasting life -- the fundamental binary
docs.text:
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

Context: The most quoted verse in the Bible. The binary: perish (apollymi G622) vs. everlasting life (zoe aionios). No third category of 'eternal conscious torment.'

Notes: apoletai (V-2AMS-3S, aorist middle subjunctive of apollymi G622) = 'should perish.' The opposite of eternal life is perishing, not torment.

docs.title: God able to destroy both soul and body in gehenna
docs.text:
And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

Context: Jesus's warning. God is able to apollymi (destroy) both soul AND body in gehenna. The verb is destruction, not torment. Both components are destroyed.

Notes: apolesai (aorist active infinitive of apollymi G622) = 'to destroy.' Applied to both psyche (soul) and soma (body). If the soul were inherently immortal, it could not be destroyed. Jesus uses destruction vocabulary for gehenna.

docs.title: Fire-and-brimstone / smoke ascending formula -- apocalyptic context
docs.text:
