docs.title: Beast and False Prophet Cast Alive into Lake of Fire: Symbolic Entities
docs.text:
And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone.

Context: The beast and false prophet are cast 'alive' (zontes) into the lake of fire -- symbolic entities. In Rev 20:10, they are already 'where' (hopou) in the lake when the devil joins them. The human remnant is separately handled: 'slain with the sword' (Rev 19:21).

Notes: Vocabulary differentiation: beast/false prophet cast alive (symbolic), human remnant slain (Rev 19:21). These are non-human/symbolic entities -- Rev 13:1-2 describes the beast as having 7 heads, 10 horns, and composite Daniel 7 body; Rev 17:8-11 decodes it as political-religious system.

docs.title: Edom Fire Paradigm: Smoke Ascending Forever for a Historically Ended Fire
docs.text:
Isaiah 34:9 And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. Isaiah 34:10 It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.

Context: Edom's judgment. 'Not quenched night nor day' and 'smoke ascending forever' for a fire that historically ended. Edom is not still burning. This OT paradigm provides the interpretive context for NT 'unquenched fire' and 'smoke ascending' language.

Notes: The etc7-07 and etc7-11 studies established: fire/smoke judgments called olam that historically ended demonstrate that the language describes permanent evidence of completed destruction, not ongoing burning. Same formula used in Rev 14:11 and Rev 19:3.

docs.title: Day Burns as an Oven: Wicked Become Stubble, Burned Up, Ashes Under Feet
docs.text:
Malachi 4:1 For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch. Malachi 4:2 But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall. Malachi 4:3 And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do [this], saith the LORD of hosts.

Context: Explicit cessation language for the wicked's final fate. Stubble burned up, leaving neither root nor branch. The wicked become ASHES under the feet of the righteous.

Notes: Every element describes cessation: stubble (consumed), burned up (destroyed), neither root nor branch (total), ashes (residue of completed destruction). The righteous TREAD on the ashes -- the wicked are gone.

docs.title: Sodom Turned to Ashes: Ensample to Those Living Ungodly
docs.text:
And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned [them] with an overthrow, making [them] an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;

Context: Peter explicitly identifies Sodom's destruction as an 'ensample' (hupodeigma, example/pattern) for ungodly judgment. Sodom was turned to ASHES -- not kept in ongoing torment.

Notes: The word for 'ensample' (hupodeigma) means pattern/example of what will happen. If Sodom is the pattern, and Sodom was reduced to ashes, the pattern is destruction to ashes.

docs.title: Perish vs Everlasting Life: The Core Binary in Gospel's Most Cited Verse
docs.text:
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

Context: The foundational perish-vs-life binary. Two options: apollymi (perish/destroy) or zoe aionios (everlasting life). Not two forms of eternal existence.

Notes: Apollymi (G622) = perish/be destroyed. The binary is destruction vs life, not torment vs bliss.

docs.title: Broad Way to Destruction vs Narrow Way to Life
docs.text:
Matthew 7:13 Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide [is] the gate, and broad [is] the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Matthew 7:14 Because strait [is] the gate, and narrow [is] the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.

Context: Two ways, two outcomes: apoleia (destruction) vs zoe (life). Structurally decisive binary.

Notes: Apoleia (G684) = destruction/ruin (Louw-Nida 20.031). Matt 7:13 is a structurally decisive binary -- the opposite of life is destruction, not ongoing torment.

docs.title: Wages of Sin Is Death vs Gift of God Is Eternal Life
docs.text:
For the wages of sin [is] death; but the gift of God [is] eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Context: Paul's most concise statement of the binary: thanatos (death) vs zoe aionios (eternal life).

Notes: The wages of sin is death (thanatos, G2288) -- not eternal conscious torment. Death is the opposite of life.

docs.title: Destroy Both Soul and Body in Gehenna: Soul Is Destructible
docs.text:
And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

Context: Jesus declares God is able to DESTROY (apollymi, G622) both soul (psyche, G5590) and body (soma, G4983) in gehenna. The soul is destructible.

Notes: Apollymi (G622) = destroy. Psyche (G5590) = soul. The soul CAN be destroyed. This is an anthropological E-tier finding established in etc7-01.

docs.title: The Soul That Sins Shall Die: Mortality of the Soul
docs.text:
Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.

Context: God's declaration: the nephesh (soul) that sins shall die (muth, H4191). The soul is mortal and subject to death.

Notes: Nephesh (H5315) = the whole person/soul. Muth (H4191) = to die. The soul can and does die. This is an anthropological E-tier finding established in etc7-01.

docs.title: God Alone Has Immortality: Anthropological Prerequisite
docs.text:
Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom [be] honour and power everlasting. Amen.

Context: Paul's doxological declaration: God ALONE (monos) has immortality (athanasia, G110). If God alone possesses immortality, humans do not inherently have it.

Notes: Monos (G3441) = alone/only. Athanasia (G110, 3 NT uses) = immortality. The etc7-02 study established at E-tier: monos in doxological contexts marks unqualified exclusivity.

docs.title: Mortal Puts On Immortality at Resurrection: Future Acquisition
docs.text:
1 Corinthians 15:53 For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal [must] put on immortality. 1 Corinthians 15:54 So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.

Context: Paul describes the resurrection transformation. Immortality is PUT ON (endyo, G1746) at a future event. Endyo always describes acquiring something NOT previously possessed.

Notes: The etc7-02 study established at E-tier: endyo (G1746) 'put on' describes acquiring something not previously possessed. Thnetos (G2349) = mortal -- the present human condition. The wicked never 'put on' immortality.

docs.title: Enemies of the Cross: End Is Destruction
docs.text:
Philippians 3:18 (For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, [that they are] the enemies of the cross of Christ: Philippians 3:19 Whose end [is] destruction, whose God [is their] belly, and [whose] glory [is] in their shame, who mind earthly things.)

Context: Paul's Pauline binary: telos (end) is apoleia (destruction). Another author using destruction vocabulary for the final fate of the wicked.

Notes: Apoleia (G684) = destruction. The end (telos) of the enemies of the cross is destruction -- not eternal conscious torment.

docs.title: Sodom Suffering Vengeance of Eternal Fire: Fire That Ended
docs.text:
Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.

Context: Sodom suffers 'eternal fire' (pyros aioniou) -- but Sodom is not still burning. The fire ended but the result is permanent. Contrast with v.6 which uses aidios (G126, from aei 'always') for the chains binding fallen angels -- showing the author uses different Greek words for different temporal concepts.

Notes: The etc7-08 study noted: Jude uses aidios (v.6, strict eternality) and aionios (v.7, age-pertaining) in adjacent verses -- the author distinguishes the concepts. Aionios fire that ended = permanent-result fire, not endless-duration fire.

docs.title: Sodom Fire: Destroyed Them All
docs.text:
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed [them] all.

Context: Jesus uses Sodom as paradigm: 'destroyed them all' (apollymi). The fire-and-brimstone event produces destruction, not ongoing torment.

Notes: Apollymi (G622) = destroyed them all. Every OT/NT reference to Sodom's fire describes destruction/ashes/annihilation.

docs.title: Satan Brought to Ashes, Never Shalt Thou Be Any More
docs.text:
Ezekiel 28:18 Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee. Ezekiel 28:19 All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never [shalt] thou [be] any more.

Context: OT description of the same Satan-figure who is 'tormented forever' in Rev 20:10. Ezekiel describes this entity being brought to ASHES and ceasing to exist ('never shalt thou be any more').

Notes: The etc7-12 study noted: the OT describes the same figure with destruction vocabulary (ashes, devour, never be any more) that Revelation describes with torment vocabulary. Same entity, different genre conventions.

docs.title: Eternal Judgment: Hebrews Pattern Instance
docs.text:
Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

Context: Aionios + krima = 'eternal judgment.' Under the Hebrews pattern (aionios + result-noun = permanent result of completed act), this means judgment whose RESULT is permanent -- like 'eternal redemption' (Heb 9:12), not an eternal process of judging.

Notes: The Hebrews pattern established in etc7-08: eternal salvation (Heb 5:9, one act of saving with permanent result), eternal judgment (Heb 6:2, one act of judging with permanent result), eternal redemption (Heb 9:12, one act of redeeming with permanent result), eternal inheritance (Heb 9:15), blood of eternal covenant (Heb 13:20).

docs.title: Death Swallowed Up in Victory: Beginning of Death-of-Death Chain
docs.text:
He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken [it].

Context: Beginning of the death-of-death chain: Isa 25:8 -> 1 Cor 15:26 -> Rev 20:14 -> Rev 21:4. Death itself is abolished.

Notes: The death-of-death chain results in Rev 21:4 'no more death.' Death and Hades are cast into the lake of fire (Rev 20:14). The lake of fire IS the second death. The result is the abolition of death itself.

docs.title: Man Became a Living Soul: Anthropological Foundation
docs.text:
And the LORD God formed man [of] the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

Context: Man BECAME (wayehi) a living nephesh -- he did not receive a separate immortal soul. The same term nephesh chayyah is applied to animals (Gen 1:21,24).

Notes: Anthropological foundation established in etc7-01 at E-tier. Man IS a soul, does not HAVE a separable immortal soul.

docs.title: Return to Dust; Barred from Tree of Life: Conditional Immortality Foundation
docs.text:
Genesis 3:19 In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou [art], and unto dust shalt thou return. Genesis 3:22 And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:

Context: After sin: (1) man returns to dust (reversal of Gen 2:7); (2) man is barred from the tree of life LEST he live forever -- demonstrating immortality is conditional on access to the tree of life, not an inherent property.

Notes: v.22 is decisive: God bars access to the tree of life to PREVENT humans from living forever. This means humans do NOT inherently live forever. Established at E-tier in etc7-02.

docs.title: Great White Throne Judgment: Books Opened, Book of Life, Lake of Fire = Second Death
docs.text:
Revelation 20:11 And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them. Revelation 20:12 And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is [the book] of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works. Revelation 20:13 And the sea gave up the dead which were in it; and death and hell delivered up the dead which were in them: and they were judged every man according to their works. Revelation 20:14 And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. Revelation 20:15 And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

Context: The great white throne judgment. Dead are raised, books of works and book of life are opened, judgment 'according to their works,' those not in the book of life cast into the lake of fire, identified as the second death.

Notes: Primary passage for Rev 20 analysis. Two criteria: books of works (v.12) and book of life (v.15). The identification formula in v.14: 'This is the second death' -- thanatos (death), not basanismos (torment). See also the grouped entry Rev 20:9-15 for full vocabulary differentiation analysis.

docs.title: Vocabulary Differentiation: Devoured (Humans) vs Tormented (Devil/Beast/False Prophet)
docs.text:
Revelation 20:9 And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them. Revelation 20:10 And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet [are], and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.

Context: Consecutive verses with different verbs for different subjects: v.9 katephagen (devoured, G2719) for human armies; v.10 basanisthesontai (tormented, G928) for devil, beast, and false prophet -- all three non-human/symbolic entities.

Notes: Critical vocabulary differentiation in consecutive verses. Humans devoured (destruction verb); non-human entities tormented. The etc7-12 and etc7-13 studies established this differentiation at E-tier.

docs.title: Predicate Nominative: Lake of Fire IS the Second Death

And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.

Context: The predicate nominative construction: houtos ho thanatos ho deuteros estin, he limne tou pyros. The identification word chosen by the text is thanatos (death, G2288), not basanismos (torment, G929).

docs.title: Dual-Outcome Resurrection: Chayyei Olam vs Dera'on Olam in Parallel Construct Chains
docs.text:
And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame [and] everlasting contempt.

Context: The only OT text explicitly naming two resurrection outcomes. Construct chain parallelism: chayyei olam (life of eternity) and dir'on olam (abhorrence of eternity). Dera'on (H1860) has only 2 OT uses -- both judgment contexts (Dan 12:2, Isa 66:24).

docs.title: Fiery Indignation That Shall Devour Adversaries: Pyros Zelos + Esthio
docs.text:
But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.

Context: The outcome for willful sinners: pyros zelos (fire of zeal/jealousy, G4442 + G2205) + esthio (G2068, to eat/devour). Fire DEVOURS the adversaries -- destruction vocabulary.

docs.title: Fearful Thing to Fall into the Hands of the Living God
docs.text:
[It is] a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

Context: Severity emphasis closing the Heb 10:26-31 warning. The 'living God' (theou zontos) contrasts with the death that results from falling under his judgment.

Notes: Emphasizes the severity of divine judgment without specifying its nature as torment or destruction. The surrounding context (v.27 devour, v.29 sorer punishment, v.39 destruction vs saving) provides the vocabulary for the judgment's nature.

docs.title: According to Deeds: Eternal Life for Patience vs Indignation and Wrath for Disobedience
docs.text:
Romans 2:6 Who will render to every man according to his deeds: Romans 2:7 To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life: Romans 2:8 But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,

Context: Paul's proportionality principle: God renders to every person 'according to his deeds.' Two outcomes: eternal life (for those seeking immortality) vs thumos and orge (for the disobedient). v.7 establishes that immortality is sought (not possessed).

Notes: v.7 zetousin (G2212, V-PAP-DPM, Pres Act Ptcp) = present active participle 'seeking' -- ongoing action seeking what is not yet possessed. v.8 orge (G3709) and thumos (G2372) = wrath vocabulary describing divine response, not specifying duration. See Rom 2:5-11 grouped entry.

docs.title: Tribulation and Anguish upon Every Soul That Does Evil
docs.text:
Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile;

Context: Thlipsis (G2347, tribulation) and stenochoria (G4730, anguish/constriction) upon every psyche (soul) that does evil. Suffering vocabulary that does not specify duration.

docs.title: The Wicked Shall Not Be: Ayin (Non-Existence Language)
docs.text:
For yet a little while, and the wicked [shall] not [be]: yea, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it [shall] not [be].

Context: Non-existence language (ayin, H369). The wicked shall 'not be' -- their place shall 'not be.' Total cessation of existence.

Notes: Ayin (H369) = non-existence, 'not-be.' The wicked cease to exist. Their very place becomes empty. Part of the non-existence language cluster with Psa 104:35, Oba 1:16.

docs.title: The Wicked Shall Perish: Consume Away into Smoke
docs.text:
But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the LORD [shall be] as the fat of lambs: they shall consume; into smoke shall they consume away.

Context: Cessation simile: wicked compared to fat of lambs that consumes away into smoke. The substance ceases to exist.

Notes: Every biblical simile for the wicked's fate depicts a substance that ceases to exist: chaff, wax, smoke, fat, stubble, ashes. No simile depicts ongoing existence in a ruined state.

docs.title: Transgressors Destroyed Together: The End of the Wicked Cut Off
docs.text:
But the transgressors shall be destroyed together: the end of the wicked shall be cut off.

Context: Karat (H3772, 'cut off') -- covenant-sanction and destruction vocabulary. The 'end' (acharith) of the wicked is being cut off.

Notes: Destruction and cutting-off language for the wicked's end.

docs.title: Isaiah 2 Allusion Behind 2 Thess 1:9: Hiding from the Glory/Majesty of the LORD
docs.text:
Isaiah 2:10 Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty. Isaiah 2:19 And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth. Isaiah 2:21 To go into the clefts of the rocks, and into the tops of the ragged rocks, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

Context: The source text for Paul's apo prosopou language in 2 Thess 1:9. The LXX of these verses uses 'apo prosopou tou phobou kyriou kai apo tes doxes tes ischyos autou' -- identical phrasing to 2 Thess 1:9. In Isaiah 2, the divine presence causes people to flee and hide -- the glory IS the destructive agent.

Notes: Critical for the apo prosopou debate in 2 Thess 1:9. In the source text, people hide FROM the LORD's glory because it is terrifying/destructive. This favors the source-reading (destruction proceeds FROM God's presence) over the separation-reading (excluded from presence but still existing).

docs.title: As Though They Had Not Been: Strongest Non-Existence Language
docs.text:
For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, [so] shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.

Context: The strongest non-existence language for judgment outcome in the OT. The heathen 'shall be as though they had not been' -- total cessation of existence.

Notes: 'As though they had not been' = the most explicit non-existence statement for the wicked's final state. Part of the ayin/non-existence cluster.

docs.title: Sinners Consumed Out of the Earth, Wicked Be No More
docs.text:
Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless thou the LORD, O my soul. Praise ye the LORD.

Context: Tamam (H8552, consumed/completed) + ayin (H369, not-be/no more). Dual cessation language.

Notes: Two cessation verbs: tamam (consumed completely) and ayin (be no more). The wicked are consumed AND cease to exist.

docs.title: Heavens and Earth Reserved unto Fire: Day of Judgment and Perdition of Ungodly
docs.text:
2 Peter 3:7 But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men. 2 Peter 3:10 But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up. 2 Peter 3:11 [Seeing] then [that] all these things shall be dissolved, what manner [of persons] ought ye to be in [all] holy conversation and godliness, 2 Peter 3:12 Looking for and hasting unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?

Context: Peter uses apoleia (G684, 'perdition/destruction') for the fate of the ungodly in v.7. The cosmic fire dissolves, melts, burns up -- all destruction/cessation vocabulary.

Notes: v.7 apoleias (G684) = perdition/destruction of ungodly men. The fire-judgment produces dissolution, melting, burning up -- cessation, not ongoing torment.

docs.title: Many Stripes vs Few Stripes: Degrees of Judgment (Proportionality)
docs.text:
Luke 12:47 And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not [himself], neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many [stripes]. Luke 12:48 But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few [stripes]. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.

Context: Degrees of judgment: 'many stripes' vs 'few stripes.' The proportionality principle -- judgment is calibrated to knowledge and responsibility.

Notes: Proportionality implies finite, measured punishment rather than infinite identical punishment for all. 'Few stripes' is incompatible with eternal torment of equal intensity for all.

docs.title: More Tolerable for Sodom: Degrees of Judgment
docs.text:
Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

Context: 'More tolerable' (anektoteron) -- comparative language implying degrees of judgment. Some face more severe judgment than others.

Notes: Degrees of judgment language. Compatible with proportional punishment; difficult to reconcile with identical infinite torment for all.

docs.title: God Has No Pleasure in the Death of the Wicked
docs.text:
Ezekiel 18:23 Have I any pleasure at all that the wicked should die? saith the Lord GOD: [and] not that he should return from his ways, and live? Ezekiel 18:32 For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith the Lord GOD: wherefore turn [yourselves], and live ye.

Context: God's self-disclosure about his character and judgment: he takes no pleasure in the death (muth, H4191) of the wicked. The stated alternative to death is turning and living -- not turning and escaping eternal torment.

Notes: The divine character data: God has no pleasure in death. The binary is death vs life, not torment vs life. If the penalty were eternal conscious torment rather than death, the text would need to say God has no pleasure in the torment of the wicked.

docs.title: Ungodly Like Chaff: Cessation Simile in Judgment Context
docs.text:
Psalm 1:4 The ungodly [are] not so: but [are] like the chaff which the wind driveth away. Psalm 1:5 Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous. Psalm 1:6 For the LORD knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.

Context: Cessation simile: ungodly compared to chaff driven away by wind. v.6: the way of the ungodly 'shall perish' (abad, H6). Judgment context: 'shall not stand in the judgment.'

Notes: Chaff = substance that is driven away and ceases to exist. Abad (H6) = perish/be destroyed. Another cessation simile consistent with the pattern across all biblical similes for the wicked.

docs.title: No More Death: Result of the Death-of-Death Chain
docs.text:
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

Context: The culmination of the death-of-death chain (Isa 25:8 -> 1 Cor 15:26 -> Rev 20:14 -> Rev 21:4). Death itself is abolished. The new creation outcome.

Notes: Death is abolished in the new creation. Since the lake of fire IS the second death (Rev 20:14), and there is 'no more death' (Rev 21:4), the second death resolves the problem of death itself.

docs.title: Beast Slain, Body Destroyed, Given to Burning Flame
docs.text:
I beheld then because of the voice of the great words which the horn spake: I beheld [even] till the beast was slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame.

Context: Daniel's vision: the symbolic beast is slain, body destroyed, given to burning flame. Destruction vocabulary for a symbolic entity -- same beast-figure that appears in Revelation.

Notes: The OT describes the symbolic beast with destruction vocabulary (slain, destroyed, burning flame). In Rev 19:20, the same beast is cast alive into the lake of fire. Different genre conventions for the same symbolic entity.

docs.title: Wicked Perish at the Presence of God: Cessation Simile at Divine Presence
docs.text:
As smoke is driven away, [so] drive [them] away: as wax melteth before the fire, [so] let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

Context: Two cessation similes: smoke driven away, wax melting before fire. The wicked PERISH (abad, H6) at the PRESENCE (panim, H6440) of God -- connecting to the apo prosopou debate in 2 Thess 1:9.

Notes: The wicked perish (cessation) AT the presence of God. Not banished FROM presence but destroyed BY presence. Supports the source-reading of apo prosopou in 2 Thess 1:9.

docs.title: Christ Destroys (Katargeo) Him That Had the Power of Death: The Devil
docs.text:
Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;

Context: Christ destroys (katargeo, G2673) the devil through death. Katargeo = to render inoperative, abolish, nullify. The devil's destruction is accomplished through Christ's death.

Notes: Katargeo (G2673) = abolish/render powerless. Combined with Ezek 28:18-19 (brought to ashes, never be any more), the Bible describes the devil's ultimate fate with destruction vocabulary -- even though Rev 20:10 uses torment vocabulary. Different genre conventions, same outcome.

docs.title: Breath Goes Forth, Thoughts Perish: Death-State Testimony
docs.text:
His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish.

Context: Death-state testimony: at death, breath departs, man returns to earth, thoughts perish. The dead are unconscious.

Notes: Machsheboth (thoughts) abad (perish) -- at death, cognitive activity ceases. Part of the 8+ OT author testimony that the dead are unconscious (Ecc 9:5, 9:10, Psa 115:17, Psa 88:12). Relevant because the dead are 'in the graves' (John 5:28) awaiting resurrection.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: Major judgment passages: Rev 20:11-15, Matt 25:31-46, Dan 12:2, Isa 66:22-24, John 5:28-29, 2 Thess 1:7-10, Heb 10:26-31, Rom 2:5-11. Each analyzed for E/N/I tier.

docs.title: Passage 1: Revelation 20:9-15 — Great White Throne Judgment
Rev 20:9
docs.text:
Context: Post-millennial scene. Satan has been released, deceived the nations (Gog and Magog), and led them against "the camp of the saints" and "the beloved city." Fire comes down from God out of heaven.

Direct statement: Fire from heaven "devoured them" — the human armies surrounding the city.

Original language: The verb is katephagen (G2719, katesthio, V-2AAI-3S, aorist active indicative). Katesthio means "to eat down, devour, consume." It is a compound of kata (down) and esthio (to eat). The aorist tense presents the devouring as a completed, bounded event. The subject of the devouring is pyr (G4442, fire); the object is autous (them — the human armies).

Cross-references: Rev 20:10 uses a different verb (basanisthesontai, G928, future passive) for different subjects (devil, beast, false prophet). This vocabulary differentiation in consecutive verses is a textual fact both sides must acknowledge. The etc7-12 and etc7-13 studies established this at E-tier. Every OT fire-from-heaven event (Sodom, Gen 19:24; Nadab/Abihu, Lev 10:2; Korah, Num 16:35) produces destruction and death, not ongoing torment.

Relationship to other evidence: Establishes the vocabulary pattern for the passage: human subjects receive destruction vocabulary (katephagen = devoured), while non-human/symbolic subjects receive torment vocabulary (basanisthesontai). This pattern carries through to vv.14-15, where human subjects receive "the second death" (thanatos), not basanismos (torment).

docs.title: Rev 20:10
docs.text:
Context: Immediately after the human armies are devoured (v.9), the devil is cast into the lake of fire where the beast and false prophet already are.

Direct statement: The devil, beast, and false prophet "shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever."

Original language: Basanisthesontai (G928, V-FPI-3P, future passive indicative, 3rd person plural) — "they shall be tormented." This is the only future-tense verb in the aorist narrative chain of vv.9-15. The grammar reference confirms it projects forward from the narrative moment. The plural "they" refers to three subjects: ho diabolos (the devil), to therion (the beast), and ho pseudoprophetes (the false prophet). The phrase eis tous aionas ton aionon ("unto the ages of the ages") uses the Semitic superlative-by-repetition idiom.

Cross-references: All three named subjects are non-human/symbolic entities. The devil is a supernatural spirit being (Rev 12:9, Eph 2:2). The beast has 7 heads, 10 horns, and a composite Daniel 7 body (Rev 13:1-2); Rev 17:8-11 decodes it as a political-religious system. The false prophet is identified with the earth beast of Rev 13:11-17 by matching vocabulary (Rev 19:20). Tree 3 Gate 1 (Subject Gate) fails for all three — none is a literal human being. Ezek 28:18-19 describes the same Satan-figure with destruction vocabulary ("ashes," "never shalt thou be any more"). Dan 7:11 describes the symbolic beast with destruction vocabulary ("slain, body destroyed, given to the burning flame").

Relationship to other evidence: This is the only verse in all 8 judgment passages that uses basanizo (torment) — and all its subjects are non-human or symbolic. No verse in any of the 8 passages uses basanizo for human wicked. The etc7-12 study established this at E-tier.

docs.title: Rev 20:11-13
docs.text:
Context: The great white throne judgment. The dead, small and great, stand before God. Books are opened, including the book of life. The dead are judged "according to their works." The sea, death, and hades give up their dead.

Direct statement: The dead are raised from graves/sea/hades and judged according to their works. Two criteria are mentioned: books of works (v.12) and the book of life (v.15).

Original language: Nekrous (G3498, dead) — the subjects are called "the dead" throughout. Ekkrithesan (G2919, krino, V-API-3P, aorist passive indicative) — "were judged." The aorist passive suppresses the agent (divine passive — God is the unnamed judge). Kata ta erga auton (according to their works, G2041 ergon, N-APN) — the standard proportionality formula. The grammar reference identifies the progressive passivization: hostile actors who were grammatical subjects become grammatical patients acted upon by the divine agent.

Cross-references: The "according to their works" formula appears in 11+ passages across 9 authors (Rom 2:6, Job 34:11, Psa 62:12, Jer 17:10). The proportionality principle established in etc6-17 and confirmed here. The "book of life" parallels Dan 12:1 ("every one that shall be found written in the book").

Relationship to other evidence: The passage describes the judgment mechanism but does not specify the nature of the punishment. The nature is specified in v.14 (second death) and by the absence of torment vocabulary for humans.

docs.title: Rev 20:14
docs.text:
Context: After the judgment, death and hades are cast into the lake of fire. The text then provides a self-interpreting identification: "This is the second death."

Direct statement: Death and hades are cast into the lake of fire. The lake of fire IS the second death.

Original language: The predicate nominative construction: houtos ho thanatos ho deuteros estin, he limne tou pyros. The grammar reference provides detailed analysis: the subject (houtos ho thanatos ho deuteros) is maximally definite with demonstrative + articular noun + articular ordinal adjective. The copula estin (V-PAI-3S) links it to the predicate nominative he limne tou pyros (the lake of fire). The identification word chosen by the text is thanatos (G2288, death), not basanismos (G929, torment). This formula belongs to Revelation's self-interpreting pattern (Rev 1:20, 5:8, 17:9, 17:15, 17:18, 19:8).

Cross-references: Rev 21:8 repeats the formula: "which is the second death." The death-of-death chain: Isa 25:8 ("death swallowed up in victory") → 1 Cor 15:26 ("last enemy that shall be destroyed is death") → Rev 20:14 (death cast into lake of fire) → Rev 21:4 ("no more death"). Death itself is abolished.

Relationship to other evidence: The text names the fate of humans cast into the lake of fire as "death" — the same word that means cessation of life in 119 NT uses. The text does NOT call it "the second torment" or use any basanizo/basanismos vocabulary for the human subjects.

docs.title: Rev 20:15
docs.text:
Context: The conditional coda: anyone not found written in the book of life is cast into the lake of fire.

Direct statement: "Whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire."

Original language: The first-class conditional (ei + indicative) presents the condition as assumed true for the sake of the argument. The grammar reference confirms: ei tis ouch heurethe (if anyone was not found) uses the strong objective negation ouch with the aorist passive indicative. The perfect passive participle gegramenos ("having been written") carries stative aspect — the inscription either existed as a prior standing condition or did not.

Cross-references: The lake of fire has already been identified as "the second death" in v.14. No additional vocabulary specifying the nature of the fate is provided. The description is casting (eblethe) into what has been named death.

Relationship to other evidence: Combined with v.14's identification formula, the text states that humans not in the book of life receive "the second death." The vocabulary for human fate in this passage is: devoured (v.9), cast into the lake of fire (v.15), which is the second death (v.14). Torment vocabulary is reserved for non-human/symbolic entities (v.10).

docs.title: Passage 2: Matthew 25:31-46 — Sheep and Goats Judgment
Matt 25:31-33
docs.text:
Context: The Son of man comes in glory with holy angels. All nations are gathered. He separates them as a shepherd divides sheep from goats — sheep on the right, goats on the left.

Direct statement: Universal judgment at the parousia: all nations gathered, separated into two groups.

Original language: Standard narrative Greek. Kathisei (G2523, future active indicative, "he shall sit") epi thronou doxes autou ("upon the throne of his glory"). Aforisei (G873, future active indicative, "he shall separate") — judicial separation.

Cross-references: The judgment scene parallels Rev 20:11-15 (throne, judgment, separation). The shepherd-and-flock imagery is a parabolic/illustrative framework.

Relationship to other evidence: Establishes the judgment setting. The parabolic genre affects how details are classified (Tree 3 Gate 3).

docs.title: Matt 25:34-40
docs.text:
Context: The king invites the sheep (righteous) to inherit the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world. The basis: acts of mercy toward "the least of these my brethren."

Direct statement: The righteous inherit the kingdom based on works of mercy.

Relationship to other evidence: Establishes the judgment-by-works principle, consistent with Rom 2:6 and Rev 20:12-13. The kingdom is "prepared" for the righteous (hetoimasmenen, perfect passive participle), parallel to the fire "prepared" for the devil and his angels (v.41).

docs.title: Matt 25:41
docs.text:
Context: The king says to those on the left: "Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels."

Direct statement: The cursed are sent into aionion fire that was prepared (hetoimasmenon, G2090, V-RPP-ASN, perfect passive participle) for the devil and his angels.

Original language: Hetoimasmenon (perfect passive participle, "having been prepared") — the fire was designed for the devil and his angels, not originally for humans. The dative recipients (to diabolo kai tois aggelois autou) are the devil and his angels. Pyr to aionion ("the age-pertaining fire") — aionios modifies fire, not the experience of those in it.

Cross-references: The fire is designated for non-human entities. Jude 1:7 uses "eternal fire" for Sodom — a fire that historically ended but whose result is permanent. Matt 3:12 and Luke 3:17 describe asbestos fire that "burns up" chaff — the result is complete consumption. The etc7-08 study established that aionios means "pertaining to the age(s)" with duration determined by subject.

Relationship to other evidence: The fire's intended recipients are non-human (devil and his angels). Humans are sent into a fire not originally designed for them. The fire itself is described with aionios — but aionios fire in Jude 1:7 (Sodom) historically ended.

docs.title: Matt 25:46
docs.text:
Context: The concluding verse: "And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal."

Direct statement: Two outcomes: kolasin aionion (age-pertaining punishment) for the cursed, zoen aionion (age-pertaining life) for the righteous.

Original language: Parser confirms parallel constructions: kolasin (G2851, N-ASF) aionion (G166, A-ASF) and zoen (G2222, N-ASF) aionion (G166, A-ASF). Same adjective, same case, same construction. Kolasis (G2851) has only 2 NT uses (here and 1 John 4:18). Root kolazo means "to curtail/prune" — distinct from basanismos ("experiential torment process"). Louw-Nida places kolasis in the Punish domain (38), not in the Torture domain.

Cross-references: The Hebrews pattern (established in etc7-08): aionios + result-noun = permanent result of completed act. Eternal salvation (Heb 5:9) = one act of saving with permanent result. Eternal redemption (Heb 9:12) = one act of redeeming with permanent result. Eternal judgment (Heb 6:2) = one act of judging with permanent result. By this pattern, "eternal punishment" = one act of punishing with permanent result. The symmetry argument (same adjective = same duration) was falsified by Tit 1:2, where the same adjective modifies two different temporal scopes in the same verse.

Relationship to other evidence: This is the primary ECT-cited verse among the 8 passages. The grammatical symmetry is real — both outcomes are modified by the same adjective. The symmetry, however, does not require identical duration, as Tit 1:2 demonstrates. The word used is kolasis (punishment), not basanismos (torment). The passage is parabolic genre (Gate 3 consideration). This remains an I-B item requiring SIS resolution.

docs.title: Dan 12:1
docs.text:
Context: Michael the great prince stands up. A time of trouble unprecedented in history. Deliverance for those "found written in the book."

Direct statement: Deliverance is for those written in the book — parallel to Rev 20:15 (book of life criterion).

Cross-references: Rev 20:12,15 use the same book-of-life criterion. The "time of trouble, such as never was" parallels Matt 24:21.

docs.title: Dan 12:2
docs.text:
Context: The only OT text explicitly naming two resurrection outcomes.

Direct statement: "Many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt."

Original language: Parser confirms identical construct chain grammar: chayyei (Noun.mp.Cst, "life of") olam (Noun.ms.Abs, "eternity") parallel to dir'on (Noun.ms.Cst, "abhorrence of") olam (Noun.ms.Abs, "eternity"). The dead are described as "sleeping in the dust of the earth" — unconscious in physical death. The verb yaqitsu (Verb.Hiphil.Impf.3mp, from quts, "to awake") describes physical awakening from sleep.

Dera'on (H1860) has only 2 OT occurrences — Dan 12:2 and Isa 66:24. In Isa 66:24, the objects of dera'on are explicitly peger (corpses/dead bodies). Peger always means dead body in all 24 OT uses. Dera'on describes what the transgressors BECOME — objects of visceral revulsion viewed by the living — not what they experience.

Cross-references: Isa 66:24 shares the rare word dera'on and depicts the living looking upon the corpses of the transgressors. The olam nature-of-subject principle (established in etc7-07): olam life for those receiving immortality = genuinely eternal; olam contempt for corpses = permanent result because the subject is dead. Fire/smoke judgments called olam that historically ended (Isa 34:10 Edom, Jer 17:4 Jerusalem) demonstrate that olam does not always mean "endless."

Relationship to other evidence: The construct chain parallelism establishes two outcomes: eternal life and everlasting contempt/abhorrence. The dera'on-peger connection (shared rare vocabulary, only 2 OT uses) links Dan 12:2 with Isa 66:24, where the objects of dera'on are dead bodies. This creates an I-B item: does dera'on describe the conscious experience of the shamed, or the permanent state of being viewed as objects of revulsion? The Isa 66:24 usage (corpses) governs by SIS, since it provides the only other occurrence with an explicit subject.

docs.title: Passage 4: Isaiah 66:15-17, 22-24 — New Creation Juxtaposed with Corpse-Viewing
Isa 66:15-17
docs.text:
Context: The LORD comes with fire and chariots, rendering anger with fury. The slain of the LORD are many. Those eating forbidden things "shall be consumed together."

Direct statement: The transgressors are slain (chalalim, "slain/pierced," v.16) and consumed together (kalah, H3615, "consumed/completed," v.17) before the scene in v.24.

Original language: Parser confirms: v.15 uses chemah (H2534, "heat/fury") and aph (H639, "anger"). Esh (H784, "fire") appears twice. v.17 uses kalah (H3615) — a cessation/completion verb. The chronological sequence is: slain/consumed (vv.16-17) → new creation (v.22) → corpse-viewing (v.24).

Relationship to other evidence: Establishes that the subjects of v.24 are already dead before the viewing begins. They are slain and consumed, then their corpses are viewed.

docs.title: Isa 66:22-23
docs.text:
Context: The new heavens and new earth promise. The seed and name of God's people shall remain. From new moon to new moon, all flesh comes to worship before the LORD.

Direct statement: New creation established; worship continues in the new heavens and earth.

Cross-references: Rev 21:1 ("new heaven and a new earth") parallels Isa 66:22. The juxtaposition of new creation with the corpse-viewing in v.24 shows the permanent evidence of completed destruction alongside the new order.

docs.title: Isa 66:24
docs.text:
Context: The redeemed "go forth and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed." Their worm does not die, their fire is not quenched. They are an abhorring to all flesh.

Direct statement: The living view the peger (corpses/carcasses) of the transgressors. Worm and fire act upon the corpses. The transgressors become an abhorring (dera'on) to all flesh.

Original language: Parser confirms: pigrei (Noun.mp.Cst, "corpses of") ha-anashim (Noun.mp.Abs, "the men") ha-posh'im (Verb.Qal.Ptcp.mp.Abs, "the rebelling/transgressing"). Peger (H6297) always means dead body/corpse in all 24 OT occurrences — never living persons. Towla'tam (Noun.fs.Abs + 3mp suffix, "their worm") lo tamut (Neg + Verb.Qal.Impf.3fs, "shall not die") — the worm that consumes corpses does not die until its work is complete. Ishsham (Noun.s.Abs + 3mp suffix, "their fire") lo tikhbeh (Neg + Verb.Qal.Impf.3fs from kabah H3518, "shall not go out/be quenched") — fire that cannot be extinguished until it completes its work. Dera'on (Noun.ms.Abs, "abhorrence") — describes what they become, not what they experience.

Cross-references: Mark 9:43-48 quotes this verse. Jesus uses the Isa 66:24 language, and in the source text the subjects are peger (corpses). Jer 17:27 uses the same "not quenched" concept for Jerusalem's gates — a fire that historically ended. The "undying worm" and "unquenched fire" describe an irresistible consuming process, not eternal duration (the fire burns what it burns without being stopped, but the fuel is finite).

Relationship to other evidence: This is the interpretive key for Mark 9:43-48. The subjects of the worm and fire are dead bodies, not conscious, suffering persons. The word peger eliminates any reading that has living persons being endlessly eaten by worms. Dera'on connects to Dan 12:2, where the same rare word describes the second resurrection outcome — and here in its other occurrence, the objects are corpses.

docs.title: Passage 5: John 5:22, 28-29 — Resurrection of Life vs Resurrection of Judgment
John 5:22
docs.text:
Context: Jesus' discourse on his authority. The Father has delegated all judgment to the Son.

Direct statement: "The Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son."

Original language: Krisin (G2920, krisis, judgment) — judicial authority, a verdict-event, not ongoing torment.

docs.title: John 5:28-29
docs.text:
Context: Jesus describes the future general resurrection. All in the graves shall hear his voice and come forth.

Direct statement: Two outcomes from the graves: "resurrection of life" (anastasis zoes) for those who have done good; "resurrection of judgment/damnation" (anastasis kriseos) for those who have done evil.

Original language: Parser confirms: v.28 — pantes hoi en tois mnemeion (all who are in the graves/tombs, G3419, N-DPN) akousousin (shall hear, G191, V-FAI-3P, future active indicative). The dead are IN graves — not already conscious elsewhere. V.29 — anastasin (G386, N-ASF) zoes (G2222, N-GSF) parallel with anastasin (G386, N-ASF) kriseos (G2920, N-GSF). Krisis (G2920, 47 NT uses) means judgment/decision — it describes a verdict-event, not a mode of ongoing existence. No NT use of krisis implies ongoing torment.

Cross-references: Dan 12:2 is the OT parallel: dual-outcome resurrection from death-state (sleeping in dust of earth → awake to two outcomes). John 6 confirms the timing: "I will raise him up at the last day" repeated 4 times (6:39, 40, 44, 54) — reward at resurrection, not at death. Acts 2:34: "David is not ascended into the heavens" — believers await resurrection.

Relationship to other evidence: The passage specifies resurrection from graves as the mechanism, with two outcomes described by the words "life" and "judgment/krisis." The negative outcome is called krisis (verdict/judgment), not basanismos (torment) or kolasis (punishment). This is judgment vocabulary without specifying the nature of what follows the verdict.

docs.title: Passage 6: 2 Thessalonians 1:7-10 — Everlasting Destruction from the Presence of the Lord
2 Thess 1:7-8
docs.text:
Context: Paul describes the parousia. The Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with mighty angels "in flaming fire taking vengeance."

Direct statement: The Lord comes with flaming fire, taking vengeance on those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel.

Original language: En pyri phlogos (in fire of flame) — fire vocabulary. Ekdikesin (G1557, vengeance/retribution) — divine justice enacted.

Cross-references: The flaming fire connects to the fire-and-brimstone paradigm (Sodom, Edom, Malachi 4). Fire in OT judgment paradigms produces destruction, ashes, and cessation.

docs.title: 2 Thess 1:9
docs.text:
Context: The penalty for those who do not obey the gospel.

Direct statement: "Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power."

Original language: Parser confirms: diken (G1349, N-ASF, "penalty/justice") tisousin (G5099, V-FAI-3P, "they shall pay") olethron (G3639, N-ASM, "destruction") aionion (G166, A-ASM, "everlasting") apo (G575, PREP, "from") prosopou (G4383, N-GSN, "face/presence").

Olethros (G3639) has only 4 NT uses — ALL mean destruction/ruin. Tino (G5099) appears only here in NT — "to pay a penalty." Paul had basanizo available and did not use it. He chose olethros (destruction).

The apo prosopou debate: "from the presence of the Lord" — does apo mean "away from" (separation = ECT reading) or "from" (source = Cond. reading: destruction proceeds FROM God's glorious presence)?

Cross-references: Paul's phrasing (apo prosopou tou kyriou kai apo tes doxes tes ischyos autou) echoes Isa 2:10,19,21 LXX, where people hide "apo prosopou tou phobou kyriou kai apo tes doxes tes ischyos autou." In Isaiah 2, the divine presence causes people to flee — the glory IS the destructive agent. Psa 68:2 confirms: the wicked "perish at the presence of God" — cessation AT the divine presence, not banishment FROM it. The Hebrews pattern applies: aionios + olethros (result-noun) = permanent result of completed destruction.

Relationship to other evidence: Paul uses destruction vocabulary (olethros), not torment vocabulary (basanizo). The Isa 2 allusion favors the source-reading of apo prosopou. This passage is one of the clearest didactic statements about the fate of the wicked in the NT.

docs.title: 2 Thess 1:10
docs.text:
Context: The Lord comes to be glorified in his saints.

Direct statement: Christ glorified in his saints at his coming.

Relationship to other evidence: The positive outcome (glorification) contrasts with the negative (destruction) — a binary similar to the perish-vs-life pattern.

docs.title: Passage 7: Hebrews 10:26-31, 39 — Fiery Indignation, Sorer Punishment, Devouring Fire
Heb 10:26
docs.text:
Context: Warning against willful sin after receiving knowledge of the truth. No more sacrifice remains.

Direct statement: For willful sin after knowledge, there remains no more sacrifice for sins.

Relationship to other evidence: Sets up the warning that follows — the severity of the judgment for apostasy.

docs.title: Heb 10:27
docs.text:
Context: What remains instead of sacrifice: fearful expectation of judgment and fiery indignation.

Direct statement: "A certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries."

Original language: Parser confirms: pyros (G4442, N-GSN, "of fire") zelos (G2205, N-NSN, "zeal/jealousy") — "fire of zeal." Esthiein (G2068, V-PAN, Pres Act Inf) — "to eat/devour." Mellontos (G3195, V-PAP-GSN) — "being about to." The fire SHALL DEVOUR (esthio) the adversaries. Esthio is a consumption/destruction verb, not a torment verb.

Cross-references: The pyros zelos alludes to Isa 26:11 LXX (zelos/fire imagery). Heb 10:27 is didactic genre — a direct warning from an epistle. The verb esthio (devour) is destruction vocabulary.

Relationship to other evidence: The Hebrews author uses devour (destruction vocabulary) for the fate of adversaries, not torment vocabulary.

docs.title: Heb 10:28
docs.text:
Context: The comparison baseline: "He that despised Moses' law died without mercy under two or three witnesses."

Direct statement: Under the Mosaic law, capital punishment was the penalty for despising the law.

Relationship to other evidence: The baseline is death. The escalation in v.29 is from death, not from some other category.

docs.title: Heb 10:29
docs.text:
Context: The escalation: "Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy?"

Direct statement: Those who trample the Son of God, count the covenant blood unholy, and insult the Spirit of grace deserve "sorer punishment" (timoria) than death.

Original language: Parser confirms: timorias (G5098, N-GSF, "of punishment"). Only 1 NT use. Timoria = retributive penalty focused on what the offender deserves. Distinguished from kolasis (judicial/deterrent) and basanismos (experiential torment process). The comparison: v.28 "died without mercy" → v.29 "how much sorer punishment." The baseline is death; the escalation is something more severe than death.

Cross-references: The escalation could be read as quantitative (longer or more intense than death) or qualitative (permanent, irreversible death — "the second death"). The surrounding vocabulary (v.27 devour, v.39 destruction vs saving) favors the destruction reading.

Relationship to other evidence: The passage does not specify whether "sorer punishment" means ongoing torment or total, permanent destruction. The vocabulary context (devour, destruction, saving of the soul) frames it within destruction language.

docs.title: Heb 10:30-31
docs.text:
Context: Severity emphasis. "Vengeance belongeth unto me." "It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God."

Direct statement: Divine vengeance and the severity of judgment are affirmed.

Relationship to other evidence: Emphasizes severity without specifying nature as torment or destruction. The surrounding vocabulary provides the specification.

docs.title: Heb 10:39
docs.text:
Context: The conclusion of the warning: "But we are not of them who draw back unto perdition; but of them that believe to the saving of the soul."

Direct statement: Two outcomes: apoleia (destruction/perdition) vs peripoiesis psyches (preservation/saving of the soul).

Original language: Parser confirms: apoleian (G684, N-ASF, "destruction/perdition") contrasted with peripoiesin (G4047, N-ASF, "preserving/saving") psyches (G5590, N-GSF, "of soul"). Apoleia = destruction (Louw-Nida 20.031, Violence/Destroy domain).

Cross-references: This is the perish-vs-save binary. Matt 7:13: apoleia (destruction) vs zoe (life). The passage says "draw back unto destruction" — not "draw back unto eternal conscious torment."

Relationship to other evidence: The Hebrews author concludes the warning passage with a binary: destruction vs saving. Combined with v.27 (devour) and v.29 (sorer punishment than death), the passage consistently uses destruction vocabulary.

docs.title: Passage 8: Romans 2:5-12 — Day of Wrath, Righteous Judgment, Seeking Immortality
Rom 2:5
docs.text:
Context: Paul addresses the impenitent: "thou treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God."

Direct statement: Wrath is stored up for a future "day of wrath" — an event. God's judgment is characterized as "righteous" (dikaiokrisia, G1341, only 1 NT use).

Original language: Parser confirms: orgen (G3709, N-ASF, "wrath") en hemera (G2250, N-DSF, "in day") orges (G3709, N-GSF, "of wrath"). Hemera orges = "day of wrath" — orge as an event tied to a specific day, not an eternal state. Dikaiokrisia (G1341, N-GSF, only 1 NT use) = "righteous judgment" — a compound Paul created to emphasize the just character of divine judgment.

Cross-references: The "day of" formulation frames wrath as an eschatological event (cf. "day of the Lord" across OT prophets). Dikaiokrisia frames divine judgment as inherently just — compatible with proportional punishment, difficult to reconcile with infinite punishment for finite sin.

docs.title: Rom 2:6
docs.text:
Context: The proportionality principle: "Who will render to every man according to his deeds."

Direct statement: God renders to every person according to their deeds — proportional judgment.

Cross-references: This principle appears in 11+ passages across 9 authors (Job 34:11, Psa 62:12, Jer 17:10, Matt 16:27, Rev 20:12-13). The etc6-17 study established this. Proportionality implies measured punishment calibrated to works, not identical infinite punishment for all.

docs.title: Rom 2:7
docs.text:
Context: The positive outcome: "To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life."

Direct statement: Those who seek immortality (aphtharsia) receive eternal life.

Original language: Parser confirms: aphtharsia (G861, N-ASF) zetousin (G2212, V-PAP-DPM, Pres Act Ptcp) — "seeking." The present active participle describes ongoing action of seeking what is NOT YET POSSESSED. Believers are actively seeking immortality — it is not something they already have.

Cross-references: 1 Tim 6:16: God alone has immortality (monos echon athanasian). 1 Cor 15:53-54: mortals "put on" (endyo) immortality at resurrection — future acquisition. The etc7-02 study established at E-tier: immortality is sought by believers (Rom 2:7), not inherently possessed.

Relationship to other evidence: This is an anthropological prerequisite embedded within a judgment passage. If immortality must be sought and received, the wicked — who do not seek it — do not receive it. Without immortality, they cannot be tormented forever.

docs.title: Rom 2:8
docs.text:
Context: The negative outcome: "But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath."

Direct statement: The disobedient receive thumos (indignation/passion, G2372) and orge (wrath, G3709).

Original language: Orge (G3709, N-NSF) and thumos (G2372, N-NSM) — wrath vocabulary describing divine response. Neither word specifies eternal duration.

Relationship to other evidence: Wrath vocabulary without duration specification. The text says the disobedient receive wrath — it does not say they receive eternal conscious torment.

docs.title: Rom 2:9
docs.text:
Context: Further description of the negative outcome: "Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil."

Direct statement: Thlipsis (tribulation, G2347) and stenochoria (anguish/constriction, G4730) upon every soul that does evil.

Original language: Parser confirms: thlipsis (G2347, N-NSF) kai stenochoria (G4730, N-NSF) epi pasan psychen (G5590, N-ASF). Neither thlipsis nor stenochoria inherently implies eternal duration. Both describe the experience of judgment without specifying temporal extent.

Relationship to other evidence: Suffering vocabulary that does not specify duration. This is judgment vocabulary without temporal qualification. The suffering is real but the text does not say it is endless.

docs.title: Rom 2:10
docs.text:
Context: The positive parallel: "But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good."

Direct statement: Glory, honor, and peace for those who do good.

Relationship to other evidence: The binary: v.7 (immortality/eternal life) vs v.8-9 (wrath/tribulation/anguish), and v.10 (glory/honor/peace). The positive outcome includes immortality; the negative does not include immortality.

docs.title: Rom 2:12
docs.text:
Context: Paul states the outcome for sinners: "For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law."

Direct statement: Sinners shall perish (apollymi, G622).

Original language: Apollymi (G622) = perish/be destroyed. The standard NT destruction verb. Paul uses apollymi for the final outcome of sinners — not basanizo, not timoria in an eternal sense.

Cross-references: Apollymi appears in the perish-vs-life binary (John 3:16) and the perish-vs-save binary (apollymi-sozo, 14 verses). The etc7-06 study established: no lexicon defines apollymi as "torment."

Relationship to other evidence: Paul, within the same passage, describes the wicked's fate as "perishing" — destruction vocabulary. Combined with v.7 (seeking immortality they do not possess) and v.5 (day of wrath = event), the passage consistently uses destruction/cessation vocabulary for the final state of the wicked.

docs.title: John 3:16
docs.text:
Direct statement: "Whosoever believeth in him should not perish (apollymi, G622), but have everlasting life."

Relationship to other evidence: The foundational perish-vs-life binary. Two options: destruction or life. Not two forms of eternal existence.

docs.title: Matt 7:13-14
docs.text:
Direct statement: "Wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction (apoleia, G684)... narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life (zoe, G2222)."

Relationship to other evidence: Structurally decisive binary. The opposite of life is destruction, not torment.

docs.title: Rom 6:23
docs.text:
Direct statement: "The wages of sin is death (thanatos, G2288); but the gift of God is eternal life."

Relationship to other evidence: Paul's most concise binary: death vs eternal life.

docs.title: Matt 10:28
docs.text:
Direct statement: "Fear him which is able to destroy (apollymi, G622) both soul (psyche, G5590) and body in hell (gehenna)."

Relationship to other evidence: God can destroy both soul and body. The soul is destructible. This is an anthropological E-tier finding from etc7-01.

docs.title: Ezek 18:4
docs.text:
Direct statement: "The soul (nephesh, H5315) that sinneth, it shall die (muth, H4191)."

Relationship to other evidence: The soul can and does die. Mortality of the soul established at E-tier in etc7-01.

docs.title: Phil 3:18-19
docs.text:
Direct statement: "Enemies of the cross of Christ: whose end (telos) is destruction (apoleia, G684)."

Relationship to other evidence: Another Pauline binary: the end of enemies is destruction. Four NT authors use destruction vocabulary for the wicked's final fate.

docs.title: 1 Tim 6:16
docs.text:
Direct statement: God "only hath immortality" (monos echon athanasian, G110).

Relationship to other evidence: If God alone possesses immortality, humans do not inherently have it. Established at E-tier in etc7-02.

docs.title: 1 Cor 15:53-54
docs.text:
Direct statement: "This mortal must put on (endyo, G1746) immortality."

Relationship to other evidence: Immortality is PUT ON at resurrection — future acquisition. The wicked never "put on" immortality. Established at E-tier in etc7-02.

docs.title: Gen 2:7
docs.text:
Direct statement: Man "became a living soul (nephesh chayyah)" — not "received a soul."

Relationship to other evidence: Man IS a soul, does not HAVE a separable immortal soul. Same term applied to animals. Established at E-tier in etc7-01.

docs.title: Gen 3:19, 22
docs.text:
Direct statement: Man returns to dust (v.19). God bars access to the tree of life "lest he... live for ever" (v.22).

Relationship to other evidence: Immortality is conditional on access to the tree of life. Humans do not inherently live forever. Established at E-tier in etc7-02.

docs.title: Isa 34:9-10
docs.text:
Direct statement: Edom's fire and smoke: "not quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever (olam)."

Relationship to other evidence: Edom is not still burning. Fire/smoke called olam that historically ended. Provides the OT paradigm for "smoke ascending forever" language in Rev 14:11 and Rev 19:3.

docs.title: Mal 4:1-3
docs.text:
Direct statement: The wicked become stubble, burned up, leaving neither root nor branch. They become ashes under the feet of the righteous.

Relationship to other evidence: Explicit cessation language. Every element describes total consumption: stubble, burned up, ashes.

docs.title: 2 Pet 2:6
docs.text:
Direct statement: Sodom and Gomorrah turned to ashes, "making them an ensample (hupodeigma) unto those that after should live ungodly."

Relationship to other evidence: Peter identifies Sodom as the pattern/example for ungodly judgment. The pattern is: ashes.

docs.title: Jude 1:7
docs.text:
Direct statement: Sodom suffers "the vengeance of eternal (aionios) fire."

Relationship to other evidence: Sodom's fire is called "eternal" (aionios) but has ended. Jude uses aidios (G126, from aei "always") in v.6 for a different concept and aionios in v.7 — the author distinguishes the two Greek words.

docs.title: Luke 17:29-30
docs.text:
Direct statement: Fire and brimstone from heaven "destroyed them all" (apollymi). "So shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed."

Relationship to other evidence: Jesus uses Sodom as paradigm: the result is "destroyed them all." "So shall it be" — the Sodom paradigm applies to the parousia judgment.

docs.title: Psa 37:10
docs.text: Direct statement: "The wicked shall not be" — ayin (H369), non-existence language.

docs.title: Psa 37:20
docs.text: Direct statement: "The wicked shall perish... consume; into smoke shall they consume away."

docs.title: Psa 37:38
docs.text: Direct statement: "The transgressors shall be destroyed together: the end of the wicked shall be cut off."

docs.title: Oba 1:16
docs.text: Direct statement: "They shall be as though they had not been" — the strongest non-existence language in the OT.

docs.title: Psa 104:35
docs.text: Direct statement: "Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more."

docs.title: Psa 1:4-6
docs.text: Direct statement: The ungodly are like chaff driven away. "The way of the ungodly shall perish" (abad, H6).

docs.title: Psa 68:2
docs.text:
Direct statement: "As wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God."

Relationship to other evidence: The wicked perish AT the divine presence — cessation, not banishment. Supports the source-reading of apo prosopou in 2 Thess 1:9.

docs.title: Supporting Passages: Rev 14:9-11, Mark 9:43-48, Rev 19:20, Rev 21:8
Rev 14:9-11
docs.text:
Direct statement: Beast-worshippers "shall be tormented with fire and brimstone" and "the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever."

Original language: Basanisthesetai (G928, tormented) and basanismou (G929, torment). The "smoke ascending" formula draws on Isa 34:10 (Edom — historically ended). Rev 19:3 uses the same formula for Babylon (completely destroyed, five-fold "found no more at all"). The etc7-11 study established: the smoke-ascending formula describes permanent evidence of completed destruction. Anapausis (G372) "no rest day and night" = same word and construction as Rev 4:8 for living creatures' uninterrupted praise.

Relationship to other evidence: This passage is apocalyptic genre (Tree 3 Gate 3 fails). The subjects are specifically beast-worshippers within Revelation's symbolic framework. The Isa 34:10 paradigm and Rev 19:3 parallel govern interpretation.

docs.title: Mark 9:43-48
docs.text:
Direct statement: Jesus warns about gehenna: "the fire that never shall be quenched" and "where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched."

Relationship to other evidence: Jesus quotes Isa 66:24. In the source text, the subjects are peger (corpses). The worm and fire act on dead bodies, not on living persons. Gehenna collocates with fire 6 times, apollymi 3 times, basanizo 0 times (etc7-05 E-tier finding).

docs.title: Rev 19:20
docs.text:
Direct statement: Beast and false prophet cast alive into the lake of fire — symbolic entities.

Relationship to other evidence: Vocabulary differentiation: symbolic entities cast "alive" (zontes); human remnant separately "slain with the sword" (Rev 19:21).

docs.title: Rev 21:8
docs.text:
Direct statement: List of sinners who receive "the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death."

Relationship to other evidence: Second instance of the predicate nominative identification formula: lake of fire = second death. Consistent with Rev 20:14.

docs.title: Supporting Passages: Death-of-Death Chain and New Creation
Isa 25:8
docs.text: Direct statement: God "will swallow up death in victory."

docs.title: Rev 21:4
docs.text:
Direct statement: "There shall be no more death."

Relationship to other evidence: The death-of-death chain (Isa 25:8 → 1 Cor 15:26 → Rev 20:14 → Rev 21:4) abolishes death itself. Since the lake of fire IS the second death, and "no more death" is the outcome, the second death resolves the problem of death.

docs.title: Luke 12:47-48
docs.text: Direct statement: "Many stripes" vs "few stripes" — proportional judgment.

docs.title: Matt 10:15
docs.text:
Direct statement: "More tolerable for Sodom" — comparative language implying degrees.

Relationship to other evidence: Proportionality implies finite, measured punishment. "Few stripes" is incompatible with identical infinite torment for all.

docs.title: Supporting Passages: OT Testimony on the Devil's Fate
Ezek 28:18-19
docs.text:
Direct statement: Fire devours the being; brought to ashes, "never shalt thou be any more."

Relationship to other evidence: The OT describes the same figure that Rev 20:10 describes with torment vocabulary — but with destruction/ashes/cessation vocabulary. Same entity, different genre conventions (OT prophetic vs NT apocalyptic).

docs.title: Heb 2:14
docs.text:
Direct statement: Christ "might destroy (katargeo, G2673) him that had the power of death, that is, the devil."

Relationship to other evidence: The devil's destruction is accomplished through Christ's death. Katargeo = render inoperative, abolish. The Bible consistently describes the devil's ultimate fate as destruction in non-apocalyptic genres.

docs.title: Pattern 1: Vocabulary Distribution by Subject Category
docs.text: The 8 judgment passages collectively use the following vocabulary for the fate of human wicked: - Destruction/death vocabulary (4 passages): Rev 20:9,14-15 (devoured, second death), 2 Thess 1:9 (olethros/destruction), Heb 10:27,39 (devour, apoleia), Rom 2:12 (apollymi/perish) - Penalty/judgment vocabulary without specifying nature (2 passages): Matt 25:46 (kolasis/punishment), John 5:29 (krisis/judgment) - Dead viewed with abhorrence (2 passages): Dan 12:2 (dera'on/contempt), Isa 66:24 (peger/corpses viewed with dera'on) - Torment vocabulary for human wicked (0 passages): None of the 8 passages uses basanizo or basanismos for human subjects.

docs.title: Pattern 2: The Perish-vs-Life Binary Across Authors
docs.text: Five passages from four authors establish a consistent binary: destruction/death vs life. John 3:16 (perish vs life), Matt 7:13-14 (destruction vs life), Rom 6:23 (death vs life), Phil 3:19 (destruction), Psa 145:20 (preserves vs destroys). The binary framework is destruction vs life — not torment vs bliss, and not two forms of eternal existence.

docs.title: Pattern 3: Torment Vocabulary Confined to Non-Human/Symbolic Entities
docs.text: Basanizo (G928, 12 NT uses) is used for final judgment only in Revelation's apocalyptic framework and demonic speech. Rev 20:10 is the ONLY verse with torment for final judgment — and all three subjects are non-human/symbolic (devil, beast, false prophet). No didactic passage uses basanizo for human final fate.

docs.title: Pattern 4: Fire-and-Brimstone Paradigm Produces Cessation
docs.text: Every OT fire-and-brimstone event produces destruction, ashes, and cessation: Sodom (Gen 19:24-25, 2 Pet 2:6 "ashes"), Edom (Isa 34:9-10), Jerusalem (Jer 17:27), Malachi's day (Mal 4:1-3 "stubble, ashes"), Nadab/Abihu (Lev 10:2), Korah (Num 16:35). No fire judgment in the OT produces ongoing torment.

docs.title: Pattern 5: Aionios + Result-Noun = Permanent Result of Completed Act
docs.text: The Hebrews pattern: eternal salvation (Heb 5:9), eternal judgment (Heb 6:2), eternal redemption (Heb 9:12), eternal inheritance (Heb 9:15), blood of eternal covenant (Heb 13:20). Each describes a single completed act with a permanent result. "Eternal punishment" (Matt 25:46) and "eternal destruction" (2 Thess 1:9) follow the same pattern.

docs.title: Pattern 6: Anthropological Prerequisites
docs.text: God alone has immortality (1 Tim 6:16). Immortality is sought by believers (Rom 2:7, present active participle = not yet possessed). Immortality is put on at resurrection (1 Cor 15:53-54, endyo = acquiring what is not previously possessed). The soul can die (Ezek 18:4) and be destroyed (Matt 10:28). Without immortality, the wicked cannot be tormented forever.

docs.title: Destruction Vocabulary Cluster
docs.text: Seven destruction words studied across OT and NT (abad, shamad, kalah, shachath, apollymi, apoleia, olethros) share a common semantic core: ending/cessation. No lexicon defines any of them as "torment" or "ongoing conscious suffering." Four of these appear in the 8 judgment passages: apollymi (Rom 2:12), apoleia (Heb 10:39), olethros (2 Thess 1:9), and katesthio/esthio (Rev 20:9, Heb 10:27 — the "devour" family).

docs.title: Judgment Vocabulary Cluster
docs.text: Kolasis (G2851, 2 NT uses), krisis (G2920, 47 NT uses), and timoria (G5098, 1 NT use) are penalty/judgment words, not torment words. Kolasis = penal infliction (from kolazo "to curtail/prune"), distinct from basanismos. Krisis = verdict/judicial decision — all 47 NT uses describe a judicial event or verdict. Timoria = retributive penalty (what is deserved). None of these carries the semantic content of "ongoing conscious suffering."

docs.title: Torment Vocabulary Cluster
docs.text: Basanizo (G928, 12 NT uses) and basanismos (G929, 6 NT uses) form the torment vocabulary. Basanizo judgment uses are confined to Revelation and demonic speech. Basanismos ALL 6 uses are in Revelation; 3 describe Babylon's COMPLETED destruction. The torment vocabulary is genre-bound (apocalyptic) and subject-bound (non-human/symbolic entities for final judgment).

docs.title: The Aionios Word
docs.text: Aionios (G166, 71 NT uses) means "pertaining to the age(s)" with actual duration determined by the nature of the subject. Three past-time uses prove it does not inherently mean "endless." The Tit 1:2 precedent falsifies the symmetry argument. The Hebrews pattern governs interpretation of aionios + result-nouns across the judgment passages.

docs.title: The Dera'on-Peger Connection
docs.text: Dera'on (H1860, 2 OT uses only) appears in Dan 12:2 and Isa 66:24. In its only other occurrence (Isa 66:24), the objects of dera'on are explicitly peger (corpses/dead bodies). Peger ALWAYS means dead body in 24 OT uses. This connects the two passages and establishes that dera'on describes how the living view the dead — not the conscious experience of the dead.

docs.title: Cross-Testament Connections
docs.text:
1. Dan 12:2 ↔ Isa 66:24: Linked by the rare word dera'on (only 2 OT uses). In Isa 66:24, the objects are corpses (peger). This governs the reading of Dan 12:2's "everlasting contempt."

  2. Dan 12:2 ↔ John 5:28-29: Both describe dual-outcome resurrection from death-state. Dan 12:2: sleeping in dust → awake to life or contempt. John 5:28-29: in graves → come forth to resurrection of life or judgment.

  3. 2 Thess 1:9 ↔ Isa 2:10,19,21: Paul's phrasing echoes Isaiah 2 LXX verbatim (apo prosopou tou kyriou kai apo tes doxes tes ischyos autou). In the source text, the divine presence is the destructive agent.

  4. Heb 10:27 ↔ Isa 26:11: The pyros zelos (fiery indignation) alludes to Isaiah's fire imagery where fire devours adversaries.

  5. Rev 20:14 ↔ Isa 25:8 → 1 Cor 15:26: The death-of-death chain across testaments: death swallowed up (Isa 25:8), last enemy destroyed is death (1 Cor 15:26), death cast into lake of fire (Rev 20:14), no more death (Rev 21:4).

  6. Mark 9:43-48 ↔ Isa 66:24: Jesus quotes Isaiah. The source text specifies corpses as the subjects of worm and fire.

  7. Rev 14:11 ↔ Isa 34:10: The "smoke ascending forever" formula in Revelation draws on Edom's fire — a fire that historically ended.

  8. Ezek 28:18-19 ↔ Rev 20:10: The same Satan-figure described with destruction vocabulary (OT) and torment vocabulary (NT apocalyptic). Different genre conventions, same entity.

docs.title: 1. Matt 25:46 — The Symmetry Argument
docs.text: The grammatical symmetry between kolasin aionion and zoen aionion is real. The same adjective modifies both outcomes in the same construction. This is the strongest argument for the ECT reading of this passage. However, the symmetry argument was falsified by the Tit 1:2 precedent (same adjective, same verse, different scopes), and the Hebrews pattern (aionios + result-noun = permanent result) provides an alternative reading that accounts for the symmetry while interpreting "eternal punishment" as a permanent result rather than an endless process.

docs.title: 2. Rev 14:9-11 — Smoke of Torment Ascending
docs.text: This passage explicitly uses basanismos vocabulary for what appears to be human subjects (beast-worshippers). This is the passage most cited for ECT. The complicating factors: (a) apocalyptic genre (Gate 3 issue); (b) the "smoke ascending forever" formula draws on Isa 34:10, where the smoke ascending "forever" describes a fire that historically ended; (c) Rev 19:3 uses the same formula for Babylon, which is documented as completely annihilated (five-fold "found no more at all"); (d) "no rest day and night" uses the same word (anapausis) and construction as Rev 4:8, where it characterizes quality of activity, not eternal duration.

docs.title: 3. Rom 2:9 — Tribulation and Anguish
docs.text: The suffering vocabulary (thlipsis, stenochoria) in Rom 2:9 does not specify duration.
