docs.title: Primary Verses (35 — full analysis required)
docs.text:
Eight Major Judgment Passages: The 8 primary passages to be analyzed individually for E/N/I classification - Rev 20:11-15 — Primary passage — great white throne judgment: books opened, book of life, lake of fire = second death - Matt 25:31-46 — Primary passage — sheep and goats judgment; kolasin aionion vs zoen aionion in v.46 - Dan 12:2 — Primary passage — dual-outcome resurrection: chayyei olam vs dera'on olam; construct chain parallelism - Isa 66:22-24 — Primary passage — new heavens/earth juxtaposed with corpses (peger) viewed with abhorrence (dera'on); worm and fire on dead bodies - John 5:28-29 — Primary passage — resurrection of life vs resurrection of krisis (judgment/damnation) - 2 Thess 1:7-10 — Primary passage — Lord revealed in flaming fire, olethron aionion, apo prosopou debate - Heb 10:26-31 — Primary passage — willful sin, no more sacrifice, fiery indignation, sorer punishment (timoria) - Rom 2:5-11 — Primary passage — day of wrath, righteous judgment, eternal life for patience vs wrath for disobedient

Immediate Context Passages: Verses immediately surrounding or critical to interpreting the 8 major passages - Rev 20:9-10 — Immediate context — fire devours armies (humans) vs. devil tormented (non-human); vocabulary differentiation - Rev 20:14 — Predicate nominative: lake of fire IS the second death — identification word is thanatos, not basanismos - Rev 21:8 — Second death reiterated — parallel identification of lake of fire; list of sinners who receive it - Matt 25:41 — Fire prepared for the devil and his angels — designation of fire's intended subjects - Dan 12:1 — Context — Michael stands, time of trouble, book of life; deliverance for those written in the book - Isa 66:15-17 — Context — LORD comes with fire and sword to judge; slain and consumed (kalah); precedes v.22-24 - John 5:22 — Context — all judgment committed to the Son - 2 Thess 1:9 — Key verse — everlasting destruction (olethron aionion) from the presence (apo prosopou) of the Lord - Heb 10:27 — Fiery indignation (pyros zelos) that shall devour (esthio) adversaries — destruction vocabulary - Heb 10:29 — Sorer punishment (timoria) — only NT use; how much sorer than death without mercy - Heb 10:39 — Contrast: apoleia (perdition/destruction) vs. saving of the soul — binary outcome - Rom 2:7 — Seeking (zeteo) immortality (aphtharsia) — present active participle implies not yet possessed - Rom 2:12 — Sinners without law shall perish (apollymi) without law — destruction verb for final outcome

Fire-and-Brimstone Paradigm: OT fire judgment precedents that establish the interpretive framework - Isa 34:9-10 — Edom fire paradigm — smoke ascending forever (olam) for a historically ended fire - Mal 4:1-3 — Day that burns as an oven — wicked become stubble, burned up, ashes under feet of righteous - 2 Pet 2:6 — Sodom turned to ashes — ensample to those that should live ungodly; fire paradigm precedent

Perish-vs-Life Binary: Core binary framework passages: destruction/death vs eternal life - John 3:16 — Perish (apollymi) vs everlasting life — the perish-vs-life binary in Gospel's most cited verse - Matt 7:13-14 — Broad way to destruction (apoleia) vs narrow way to life (zoe) — binary outcome framework - Rom 6:23 — Wages of sin is death (thanatos), gift of God is eternal life — death-vs-life binary - Matt 10:28 — Fear Him who can destroy (apollymi) both soul (psyche) and body in gehenna — destructibility of soul - Ezek 18:4 — The soul (nephesh) that sins, it shall die — mortality of the soul; divine death sentence on sinners

Additional Primary Verses: - Heb 10:31 — Fearful thing to fall into hands of the living God — severity emphasis - Rom 2:6-8 — According to deeds: eternal life vs indignation (thumos) and wrath (orge) - Rom 2:9 — Tribulation (thlipsis) and anguish (stenochoria) upon every soul that does evil - Rev 14:9-11 — Smoke of torment ascending — fire-and-brimstone paradigm; cross-reference with Isa 34:10 - Mark 9:43-48 — Gehenna reference quoting Isa 66:24 — worm not die, fire not quenched; subjects are corpses per source text - Rev 19:20 — Beast and false prophet cast alive into lake of fire — symbolic entities; vocabulary for non-human subjects

docs.title: Supporting Verses (27 — retrieve for context, no individual analysis)
docs.text:
• Psa 37:10 — The wicked shall not be — ayin (non-existence language); 'thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it shall not be'
  • Psa 37:20 — The wicked shall perish, consume away like smoke — cessation simile
  • Isa 2:10,19,21 — Isaiah 2 allusion behind 2 Thess 1:9 — hiding from the glory/majesty of the LORD; apo prosopou source
  • Psa 37:38 — The end of the wicked shall be cut off — karat, transgressors destroyed together
  • Oba 1:16 — As though they had not been — strongest non-existence language for judgment outcome
  • Psa 104:35 — Let sinners be consumed out of the earth, let the wicked be no more — tamam + ayin
  • Luke 17:29-30 — Sodom fire paradigm — 'destroyed them all' (apollymi); 'so shall it be' in the day of the Son of man
  • 2 Pet 3:7,10-12 — Heavens and earth reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition (apoleia) of ungodly
  • Jude 1:7 — Sodom suffering vengeance of eternal (aionios) fire — fire that ended; aidios vs aionios contrast with v.6
  • 1 Tim 6:16 — God alone has immortality (monos echon athanasian) — anthropological premise for the study
  • 1 Cor 15:53-54 — Mortal puts on immortality at resurrection — future acquisition; endyo verb
  • Luke 12:47-48 — Many stripes vs few stripes — degrees of judgment (proportionality principle)
  • Matt 10:15 — More tolerable for Sodom — degrees of judgment; comparative language
  • Ezek 18:23,32 — God has no pleasure in the death of the wicked — divine character and judgment
  • Phil 3:18-19 — Enemies of the cross whose end (telos) is destruction (apoleia) — Pauline binary
  • Psa 1:4-6 — The ungodly like chaff — cessation simile; shall not stand in judgment; way of the ungodly shall perish
  • Heb 6:2 — Eternal judgment (krima aionion) — Hebrews pattern: aionios + result-noun = permanent result of completed act
  • Rev 21:4 — No more death — result of death-of-death chain; new creation outcome
  • Isa 25:8 — Death swallowed up in victory — beginning of death-of-death chain
  • Ezek 28:18-19 — Satan brought to ashes, never shalt thou be any more — OT destruction language for the same figure tormented in Rev 20:10
  • Dan 7:11 — Beast slain, body destroyed, given to burning flame — destruction vocabulary for symbolic entity
  • Psa 68:2 — Wicked perish at the presence of God — as wax melts; cessation simile at divine presence
  • Heb 2:14 — Christ destroys (katargeo) him that had the power of death — devil's destruction
  • Rev 20:4-6 — First resurrection context — blessed; second death has no power over them; implied second death has power over others
  • Gen 2:7 — Man became (wayehi) a living nephesh — anthropological foundation; man IS a soul, does not HAVE one
  • Gen 3:19,22 — Return to dust; barred from tree of life — conditional immortality foundation
  • Psa 146:4 — Breath goes forth, thoughts perish — death-state testimony

docs.title: Focus Areas
docs.text:
1. Rev 20:11-15 — Great White Throne Judgment Mechanism and Vocabulary: READ the established library entries: $WORD_STUDIES/G2288-thanatos.md (death), $WORD_STUDIES/G928-basanizo.md and $WORD_STUDIES/G929-basanismos.md (torment), $WORD_STUDIES/G684-apoleia.md (destruction). Also READ $GRAMMAR_REF/passages/rev-20-7-15.md for existing grammatical analysis. Run greek_parser.py --verse on Rev 20:11-15 to parse the judgment vocabulary. The critical observation is the vocabulary differentiation between Rev 20:9 (katephagen 'devoured' for human armies), Rev 20:10 (basanisthesontai 'tormented' for devil/beast/false prophet), and Rev 20:14-15 (second death for humans). Note that Rev 20:14 uses a predicate nominative construction: the lake of fire IS the second death — the identification word is thanatos (death), not basanismos (torment). Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py --hybrid-nt on Rev 20:14. The etc7-13 study established this vocabulary differentiation at E-tier; verify whether these findings hold under etc7 classifier methodology. Verses: Rev 20:11-15, Rev 20:9-10, Rev 20:14, Rev 21:8, Rev 20:4-6 Strong's: G2288, G928, G929, G684, G2719

  2. Matt 25:31-46 — Kolasin Aionion and the Sheep/Goats Judgment: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G2851-kolasis.md (punishment) and $WORD_STUDIES/G166-aionios.md (aionios). The etc7-08 study established that aionios does not inherently mean 'eternal/endless' — it means 'pertaining to the age(s)' with duration determined by subject. The symmetry argument (same adjective = same duration) was falsified by Tit 1:2 (same adjective, same verse, different scopes). The Hebrews pattern (aionios + result-noun = permanent result of completed act) was established across Heb 5:9, 6:2, 9:12, 9:15, 13:20. Run greek_parser.py --verse on Matt 25:41 and 25:46. Note v.41: fire is 'prepared for the devil and his angels' — not originally designed for humans. Kolasis (only 2 NT uses: Matt 25:46 and 1 John 4:18) derives from kolazo 'to curtail/prune,' distinct from basanismos 'torment.' The I-B resolution from etc6-14 was Strong toward Cond. — verify this holds. Also analyze the parabolic genre: the passage is a judgment parable, and parabolic details may be illustrative rather than definitional. Verses: Matt 25:31-46, Matt 25:41, Matt 25:46, Tit 1:2, Heb 5:9, Heb 6:2, Heb 9:12 Strong's: G2851, G166, G2849, G165

  3. Dan 12:2 — Dera'on Olam and Dual-Outcome Resurrection: READ $WORD_STUDIES/H1860-draown.md (dera'on/contempt), $WORD_STUDIES/H5769-owlam.md (olam/everlasting), and $WORD_STUDIES/H6297-peger.md (corpse). Also READ $GRAMMAR_REF/hebrew/construct-state.md and $GRAMMAR_REF/passages/dan-12-4-sealing.md for context. Run hebrew_parser.py --verse on Dan 12:2 to confirm the construct chain analysis. The dera'on word has ONLY 2 OT occurrences — both in judgment contexts. In Isa 66:24, the objects of dera'on are explicitly peger (corpses/dead bodies) — peger always means dead body in all 24 OT uses. This links Dan 12:2 and Isa 66:24 through shared rare vocabulary. The olam nature-of-subject principle (established in etc7-07): olam life for those who receive immortality = genuinely eternal; olam contempt = permanent result because the subject is a corpse that ceases to exist. The I-B resolution from etc6-14 was Strong toward Cond. — verify this holds under etc7 methodology. Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py --hybrid-ot on Dan 12:2. Verses: Dan 12:2, Dan 12:1, Isa 66:24, Dan 12:3, Dan 12:13 Strong's: H1860, H5769, H6297, H2416

  4. Isa 66:22-24 — New Creation Juxtaposed with Corpse-Viewing: READ $WORD_STUDIES/H6297-peger.md (corpse), $WORD_STUDIES/H1860-draown.md (abhorrence), $WORD_STUDIES/G4663-skṓlēx.md (worm), and $WORD_STUDIES/G762-ásbestos.md (unquenchable). The critical lexical fact: peger means dead body/corpse in ALL 24 OT occurrences — it NEVER refers to living persons. Isa 66:24 says 'they shall look upon the peger (carcasses) of the men that have transgressed.' The worm and fire act upon corpses, not upon living, suffering persons. The undying worm and unquenched fire describe an irresistible, unstoppable consuming process, not an eternal duration of that process (cf. Jer 17:27, 'not be quenched' for Jerusalem's gates — a fire that historically ended). Run hebrew_parser.py --verse on Isa 66:24 and Isa 66:15-17. The context of vv.15-17 establishes that the transgressors are 'slain of the LORD' and 'consumed together' BEFORE the viewing in v.24. Also compare with Isa 34:9-10 (Edom's fire and smoke paradigm) and Mal 4:1-3 (stubble burned up, ashes). Verses: Isa 66:22-24, Isa 66:15-17, Mark 9:43-48, Isa 34:9-10, Jer 17:27 Strong's: H6297, H8438, H1860, G4663, G762, H3518

  5. John 5:28-29 — Resurrection of Life vs Resurrection of Krisis: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G2920-krisis.md (judgment), $WORD_STUDIES/G2917-krima.md (judgment/verdict), and $WORD_STUDIES/G2919-krino.md (to judge). The etc6-14 study noted krisis = judgment/decision (E078, E408, E409). John 5:28-29 specifies 'all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth' — the dead are IN graves (not already conscious somewhere). Two outcomes: 'resurrection of life' (anastasis zoes) and 'resurrection of judgment' (anastasis kriseos). Krisis (G2920, 47 NT uses) means judgment/decision — it describes a verdict-event, not a mode of ongoing existence. Run greek_parser.py --verse on John 5:28-29. The 00-references.md directs: 'krisis word family should be examined for whether any NT use of krisis implies ongoing torment rather than a verdict-event.' Examine whether any of the 47 uses mean ongoing torment. Run search_strongs.py --verses G2920 to get full distribution. Also note the John 6 pattern: 'I will raise him up at the last day' repeated 4x (6:39,40,44,54) — reward at resurrection, not at death. Verses: John 5:28-29, John 5:22, John 5:25-27, John 6:39-40, John 6:44, John 6:54 Strong's: G2920, G2917, G2919, G386

  6. 2 Thess 1:7-10 — Olethron Aionion and the Apo Prosopou Debate: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G3639-olethros.md (destruction) and $WORD_STUDIES/G166-aionios.md (aionios). Olethros (G3639) has only 4 NT uses — ALL mean destruction/ruin: 1 Cor 5:5 (remedial, with explicit salvation-purpose clause), 1 Thess 5:3 (sudden destruction), 2 Thess 1:9 (everlasting destruction), 1 Tim 6:9 (destruction and perdition). Paul had basanizo available and DID NOT use it. The etc7-08 and etc7-06 studies established this at E-tier. The apo prosopou debate: does 'apo' mean 'away from' (separation = ECT reading: excluded from God's presence but still existing) or 'from' (source = Cond. reading: destruction proceeds FROM God's glorious presence)? The 00-references.md directs verification of the Isaiah 2 allusion. Paul's language 'apo prosopou tou kyriou kai apo tes doxes tes ischyos autou' echoes Isa 2:10,19,21 LXX where people hide 'apo prosopou tou phobou kyriou kai apo tes doxes tes ischyos autou.' Run greek_parser.py --verse on 2 Thess 1:9. Retrieve Isa 2:10,19,21 in LXX to verify the allusion. In Isaiah 2, the divine presence causes people to flee — the glory IS the destructive agent, favoring source-reading. Verses: 2 Thess 1:7-10, 2 Thess 1:9, Isa 2:10, Isa 2:19, Isa 2:21, 1 Thess 5:3 Strong's: G3639, G166, G4383, G575

  7. Heb 10:26-31 — Fiery Indignation, Timoria, and Devouring Fire: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G2719-katesthio.md (devour/consume) and $GRAMMAR_REF/passages/heb-10-1-25.md for context. Timoria (G5098) has only 1 NT use (Heb 10:29). The 00-references.md directs: 'Verify whether the LXX usage of timoria adds any data.' Run greek_parser.py --verse on Heb 10:26-31. The fiery indignation (pyros zelos, v.27) alludes to an OT passage — identify whether it draws on Isa 26:11 (LXX: 'zelos lempsetai laon apaideunton, kai nyn pyr tous hypenantious edetai') or Zeph 1:18/3:8. The critical E-tier observation: v.27 says fire 'shall devour (esthio) the adversaries' — esthio means to eat/consume/devour. Combined with v.39's contrast between apoleia (destruction) and 'saving of the soul' — the passage frames the outcome as destruction vs. preservation, not torment vs. bliss. Also note v.28: under Moses' law, sinners 'died without mercy' — and v.29 asks 'how much sorer punishment' (timoria), which ECT reads as quantitative intensification but the text may mean qualitative difference (permanent vs. temporary death). Verses: Heb 10:26-31, Heb 10:27, Heb 10:29, Heb 10:39, Isa 26:11, Zeph 1:18 Strong's: G5098, G2068, G2719, G684, G4442, G2205

  8. Rom 2:5-11 — Day of Wrath, Orge/Thumos, and the Proportionality Principle: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G3709-orge.md (wrath), $WORD_STUDIES/G2372-thumos.md (indignation/passion), $WORD_STUDIES/G2347-thlipsis.md (tribulation), $WORD_STUDIES/G861-aphtharsia.md (incorruption/immortality), and $WORD_STUDIES/G1341-dikaiokrisia.md (righteous judgment). The 00-references.md directs: 'orge word study is needed — does orge describe an event or a state?' Run greek_parser.py --verse on Rom 2:5-11. Key observations: (1) v.5 'day of wrath' (hemera orges) — orge as an EVENT (day of), not an eternal state; (2) v.6 'render to every man according to his deeds' — proportionality principle (cf. Luke 12:47-48); (3) v.7 'patient continuance in well doing, seek for glory, honour, and immortality (aphtharsia)' — the present active participle zetousin means they are SEEKING what they do not possess; (4) v.8 'indignation (thumos) and wrath (orge)' for the disobedient; (5) v.9 'tribulation (thlipsis) and anguish (stenochoria)' — suffering vocabulary but does it specify duration? (6) v.12 'perish (apollymi)' — destruction vocabulary for final outcome. Note that Rom 2:5 uses dikaiokrisia (G1341, only 1 NT use) — 'righteous judgment' — which frames divine judgment as just, not capricious or disproportionate. Verses: Rom 2:5-11, Rom 2:6-8, Rom 2:7, Rom 2:9, Rom 2:12, Luke 12:47-48 Strong's: G3709, G2372, G2347, G861, G1341, G622, G4730

  9. Cross-Cutting Theme: The Perish-vs-Life Binary Across All 8 Passages: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G622-apollymi.md (perish/destroy), $WORD_STUDIES/G684-apoleia.md (destruction), $WORD_STUDIES/G3639-olethros.md (destruction), $WORD_STUDIES/WG-destroy.md and $WORD_STUDIES/WG-perish-save.md (word group studies). The etc7-06 study established the semantic core: all 7 destruction words (abad H6, shamad H8045, kalah H3615, shachath H7843, apollymi G622, apoleia G684, olethros G3639) denote ending/cessation — no lexicon defines any as 'torment.' The perish-vs-life binary spans five passages from four authors: John 3:16 (perish vs eternal life), Matt 7:13-14 (destruction vs life), Rom 6:23 (death vs eternal life), Phil 3:19 (destruction vs glory), Psa 145:20 (preserves vs destroys). Every biblical simile for the wicked's fate depicts a substance that ceases to exist: chaff, wax, smoke, fat, stubble, ashes, morning cloud, dew, dung. Non-existence language (ayin H369 'not-be') in Psa 37:10, 59:13, 104:35, Oba 1:16. Map which specific binary appears in each of the 8 judgment passages. Verses: John 3:16, Matt 7:13-14, Rom 6:23, Phil 3:18-19, Psa 145:20, Psa 37:10, Psa 37:20, Oba 1:16 Strong's: G622, G684, G3639, G2288, G2222, H6, H8045

  10. Cross-Cutting Theme: Basanizo/Basanismos Distribution — Human vs Non-Human Subjects: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G928-basanizo.md (torment verb) and $WORD_STUDIES/G929-basanismos.md (torment noun). The etc7-11 and etc7-12 studies established: basanismos (G929, 6 NT uses) ALL appear in Revelation; 3 of 6 describe Babylon's completed destruction. Basanizo (G928, 12 NT uses): 7 non-judgment uses (sickness, sea storms, demonic affliction), 5 judgment uses ALL in Revelation or demonic speech. Rev 20:10 is the ONLY verse with torment (basanisthesontai) for final judgment — and ALL three subjects are non-human/symbolic (devil, beast, false prophet). The etc6-14 study's E418 finding: 0 of 8 judgment passages use basanizo for human wicked. Run search_strongs.py --verses G928 and search_strongs.py --verses G929 to verify full distribution. Cross-reference with the etc7-05 gehenna study: gehenna collocates with fire 6 times, apollymi 3 times, basanizo 0 times. Verses: Rev 20:10, Rev 14:10-11, Rev 18:7, Rev 18:10, Rev 18:15, Rev 9:5 Strong's: G928, G929, G622, G684

  11. Cross-Cutting Theme: Fire-and-Brimstone Paradigm — OT Precedents for Judgment Fire: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G4442-pyr.md (fire), $WORD_STUDIES/G762-ásbestos.md (unquenchable), and $WORD_STUDIES/WG-burning.md (burning word group). The paradigm spans: (1) Sodom/Gomorrah — Gen 19:24-25, 2 Pet 2:6 'turning to ashes,' Luke 17:29 'destroyed them all'; (2) Edom — Isa 34:9-10 smoke ascending 'from generation to generation' for a historically ended fire; (3) Jerusalem — Jer 17:27 'fire shall not be quenched' for gates that are not still burning; (4) Malachi 4:1-3 — stubble, burned up, ashes under feet; (5) Nadab/Abihu — Lev 10:1-2 fire from LORD devoured them; (6) Korah — Num 16:35 fire consumed them. Every case: fire produces destruction, cessation, ashes. No OT fire-and-brimstone event produces ongoing torment. This paradigm provides the interpretive context for 'everlasting fire' in Matt 25:41, 'fiery indignation' in Heb 10:27, 'flaming fire' in 2 Thess 1:8, and the 'lake of fire' in Rev 20:14-15. Verses: Isa 34:9-10, 2 Pet 2:6, Mal 4:1-3, Jude 1:7, Luke 17:29, Jer 17:27, Lev 10:1-2 Strong's: G4442, G762, H784, H1614

  12. Cross-Cutting Theme: Anthropological Prerequisites — Can Humans Be Eternally Tormented?: READ $WORD_STUDIES/G110-athanasia.md (immortality), $WORD_STUDIES/G861-aphtharsia.md (incorruption), $WORD_STUDIES/G2349-thnetos.md (mortal), $WORD_STUDIES/G1746-endyo.md (put on), $WORD_STUDIES/H5315-nephesh.md (soul), and $WORD_STUDIES/G5590-psyche.md (soul). The etc7-01 and etc7-02 studies established at E-tier: (1) God ALONE has immortality (1 Tim 6:16, monos echon athanasian), (2) immortality is a FUTURE gift at resurrection (1 Cor 15:53-54), (3) the soul (nephesh/psyche) CAN die (Ezek 18:4) and be destroyed (Matt 10:28), (4) immortality is SOUGHT by believers (Rom 2:7, present active participle — seeking what they do not possess), (5) 'immortal soul' never appears in Scripture. These are structural prerequisites: if the wicked do not have immortality, they cannot be tormented forever. The etc7-02 study also established that endyo (G1746) 'put on' describes acquiring something NOT previously possessed — the wicked never 'put on' immortality. This connects directly to Rom 2:7 in the current study. Verses: 1 Tim 6:16, 1 Cor 15:53-54, Rom 2:7, Ezek 18:4, Matt 10:28, Gen 3:22 Strong's: G110, G861, G2349, G1746, H5315, G5590

docs.title: Research Instructions
docs.text:
You are the Research Agent. Execute this study by:

  1. Read the SKILL.md for full tool documentation and principles
  2. Read your agent instructions at agents/research-agent.md
  3. Read ALL library entries listed in "Available Library Entries" above
  4. Follow the workflow from the skill
  5. Write research files to this folder:
  6. 01-topics.md — Nave's topics and full entries (retrieve full entries for: JUDGMENT, JUDGMENT, WICKED (PEOPLE), WICKED (PEOPLE), WICKED (PEOPLE), RESURRECTION, SECOND DEATH, LAKE, HELL, IMMORTALITY, VENGEANCE, RETRIBUTION, EVERLASTING FIRE, BOOK, FIRE, WRATH)
  7. 02-verses.md — All verse texts retrieved with context for:
    • Eight Major Judgment Passages (Rev 20:11-15, Matt 25:31-46, Dan 12:2, Isa 66:22-24, John 5:28-29...) — retrieve with FULL chapter context
    • Immediate Context Passages (Rev 20:9-10, Rev 20:14, Rev 21:8, Matt 25:41, Dan 12:1...)
    • Fire-and-Brimstone Paradigm (Isa 34:9-10, Mal 4:1-3, 2 Pet 2:6, Jude 1:7, Luke 17:29...)
    • Perish-vs-Life Binary (John 3:16, Matt 7:13-14, Rom 6:23, Phil 3:18-19, Matt 10:28...)
    • Non-Existence and Cessation Language (Psa 37:10, Psa 37:20, Psa 37:38, Psa 104:35, Oba 1:16...)
    • Anthropological Foundation (1 Tim 6:16, 1 Cor 15:53-54, Gen 2:7, Gen 3:22, Psa 146:4)

docs.title: Passage-by-Passage Analysis Requirements
docs.text: For EACH of the 8 major judgment passages, the research agent must: 1. Retrieve the full passage text (KJV) with surrounding context 2. Run greek_parser.py or hebrew_parser.py on every verse containing key judgment vocabulary 3. Identify the specific vocabulary used for the fate of the wicked 4. Note whether the vocabulary denotes (a) destruction/death, (b) torment/suffering, (c) penalty/judgment without specifying nature, or (d) abhorrence/contempt of the dead 5. Cross-reference with prior study E-tier findings from etc7 series

docs.title: Isaiah 2 LXX Verification for 2 Thess 1:9
docs.text: Retrieve Isa 2:10,19,21 LXX text and compare with 2 Thess 1:9 to verify the apo prosopou allusion. This determines whether 'from the presence of the Lord' means source (the glory causes destruction) or separation (excluded from God's presence).

docs.title: Heb 10:27 OT Allusion Source
docs.text: Identify which OT passage Heb 10:27's 'fiery indignation' (pyros zelos) alludes to. Check Isa 26:11 LXX, Zeph 1:18, Zeph 3:8 as candidates.

docs.title: Timoria LXX Usage (Heb 10:29)
docs.text: Search for timoria/timōria in LXX usage to determine whether it means retributive penalty, corrective discipline, or ongoing torment. The etc6-14 study identified it as retributive penalty (E413) but LXX data was noted as a gap.

docs.title: Krisis Distribution (John 5:29)
docs.text: Run search_strongs.py --verses G2920 to get full distribution of krisis across 47 NT uses. Specifically: does ANY use of krisis imply ongoing torment rather than a verdict-event?

docs.title: Proportionality Principle (Rom 2:5-11)
docs.text: Verify the 'according to deeds' principle across its 11+ occurrences (Rom 2:6, Job 34:11, Psa 62:12, Jer 17:10, etc.). Does proportional judgment support ECT (infinite punishment for finite sin) or Cond. (the punishment matches the crime)?

docs.title: Classification Methodology
docs.text: The analysis agent must apply the classification decision trees from D:/bible/bible-studies/etc6-series-methodology.md to every evidence item. Follow all instructions in CUSTOM-INSTRUCTIONS.md for the etc7 classifier methodology.

docs.title: What Do the Major Judgment Passages Actually Say?
docs.text: Eight key Bible passages describe God's final judgment of the wicked. This study examines the vocabulary each passage uses to describe what happens to the lost.

docs.title: The Passages
docs.text:
• Revelation 20:11-15
  • Matthew 25:31-46
  • Daniel 12:2
  • Isaiah 66:22-24
  • John 5:28-29
  • 2 Thessalonians 1:7-10
  • Hebrews 10:26-31
  • Romans 2:5-11

docs.title: What the Passages Say About the Wicked
docs.text:
When biblical authors describe the final fate of the wicked, they consistently use destruction and death language:

  • "Everlasting destruction" -- 2 Thess 1:9
  • "Fire shall devour the adversaries" -- Heb 10:27
  • "Destruction" vs "saving of the soul" -- Heb 10:39
  • "Sinners shall perish" -- Rom 2:12
  • "The second death" -- Rev 20:14
  • Fire "devoured" the wicked armies -- Rev 20:9

Four of the eight passages use words that mean destruction, perishing, or devouring. The lake of fire is called "the second death" -- not "the second torment."

docs.title: What About Torment Language?
docs.text:
The word for torment (Greek basanizo) does appear in Revelation 20:10 -- but it describes the devil, the beast, and the false prophet. These are non-human or symbolic figures. In the very next verses, when the text turns to human beings, it switches to different vocabulary: humans are "devoured" (v.9) and face "the second death" (v.14-15). The text uses one set of words for non-human entities and a different set for people.

None of the eight passages applies torment language to human beings.

docs.title: What About "Everlasting Punishment" (Matt 25:46)?
docs.text: This is the strongest verse cited in favor of eternal conscious torment. The same word "everlasting" (aionios) modifies both "punishment" and "life" in the same sentence. However, the Greek word for punishment here is kolasis (penalty), not basanismos (torment). It tells us the punishment is permanent without specifying that it involves ongoing conscious suffering. Other passages define what that punishment is: Paul calls it "everlasting destruction" (2 Thess 1:9).

docs.title: What About "Everlasting Contempt" (Dan 12:2)?
docs.text: The Hebrew word for contempt (dera'on) appears only twice in the Old Testament -- here and in Isaiah 66:24. In Isaiah, the objects of contempt are explicitly identified as corpses. The living look upon the dead bodies of transgressors with abhorrence. The word describes what the wicked become (objects of revulsion), not what they experience.

docs.title: Can the Wicked Live Forever to Be Tormented?
docs.text: The Bible says God alone possesses immortality (1 Tim 6:16). Believers must "seek for immortality" (Rom 2:7) -- meaning they do not yet have it. The wicked, who do not seek it, never receive it. Without immortality, eternal torment is not possible. The phrase "immortal soul" never appears in Scripture.

docs.title: The Pattern from the Old Testament
docs.text: Every recorded fire-and-brimstone judgment in the Old Testament results in destruction and ashes -- not ongoing suffering. Sodom was "turned to ashes" (2 Pet 2:6). Malachi says the wicked become "ashes under the soles of your feet" (Mal 4:3). Jesus pointed to Sodom as the pattern for end-time judgment (Luke 17:29-30).

docs.title: Bottom Line
docs.text: Across eight major judgment passages, the biblical authors chose destruction and death vocabulary when describing the fate of human beings. Torment language is reserved for non-human figures in Revelation's symbolic framework. The consistent picture is one of permanent, irreversible destruction -- not endless conscious suffering.

docs.title: Cross-Testament Parallels
docs.text:
• Rev 20:14 → Rev 20:15 (nt, vocabulary + sequential (cast into lake of fire))
  • Rev 20:14 → Rev 21:8 (nt, vocabulary + identification (second death = lake of fire))
  • Rev 20:14 → Rev 20:10 (nt, vocabulary + contrasting subjects (death/hades vs devil/beast))
  • Rev 20:14 → Rev 20:13 (nt, vocabulary + sequential (death/hades giving up dead then cast in))
  • Rev 20:14 → 1 Cor 15:26 (nt, theological (death-of-death chain: last enemy destroyed is death))
  • Rev 20:14 → Isa 25:8 (ot, theological (death swallowed up in victory))
  • Matt 25:46 → Heb 5:9 (nt, vocabulary + structural (Hebrews pattern: aionios + result-noun))
  • Matt 25:46 → Heb 6:2 (nt, vocabulary + structural (eternal judgment = permanent result))
  • Matt 25:46 → Heb 9:12 (nt, vocabulary + structural (eternal redemption = completed act with permanent result))
  • Dan 12:2 → Isa 66:24 (ot, vocabulary (shared dera'on -- only 2 OT uses; both judgment contexts))
  • Dan 12:2 → John 5:28-29 (nt, structural (dual-outcome resurrection: life vs judgment))
  • 2 Thess 1:9 → Isa 2:10 (ot, vocabulary + allusion (apo prosopou tou kyriou kai apo tes doxes -- identical phrasing))
  • 2 Thess 1:9 → Isa 2:19 (ot, vocabulary + allusion (apo prosopou -- divine presence as destructive agent))
  • Heb 10:27 → Isa 26:11 (ot, vocabulary + allusion (pyros zelos / fire that devours adversaries))
  • John 5:28-29 → Dan 12:2 (ot, structural (dual-outcome resurrection from death-state))
  • Rev 14:11 → Isa 34:10 (ot, vocabulary + formula (smoke ascending forever -- ended fire paradigm))
  • Rev 20:9 → Rev 20:10 (nt, vocabulary differentiation (devoured for humans vs tormented for devil))
  • Ezek 28:18-19 → Rev 20:10 (nt, same entity different vocabulary (ashes/never be vs tormented -- genre difference))

docs.title: ECT Argument #1: Smoke of torment ascending forever and ever
docs.text:
And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive [his] mark in his forehead, or in his hand, The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.

Context: Third angel's message in Revelation 14. Part of the three angels' messages sequence (Rev 14:6-12). Apocalyptic genre. The passage immediately follows Babylon's fall announcement (v.8) and is followed by the blessing on the dead who die in the Lord (v.13).

docs.text:
And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet [are], and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.

Context: Post-millennium judgment scene in Revelation 20. After the thousand years, Satan deceives the nations (vv.7-8), fire from God devours them (v.9), then the devil is cast into the lake where beast and false prophet already are (v.10). The white throne judgment follows (vv.11-15).

Notes: Key datum: basanisthesontai (G928, Fut Pass Ind 3P) — the torment-for-ever formula appears ONCE in all of Scripture, applied only to devil/beast/false prophet — all three are non-human/symbolic entities. The devil is supernatural (Rev 12:9). The beast has 7 heads and 10 horns (Rev 13:1) — symbolic political-religious system. The false prophet = earth beast (Rev 13:11-17). Vocabulary differentiation in consecutive verses: humans are devoured (v.9, katephagen G2719), but the devil is tormented (v.10, basanisthesontai). Prior study etc7-12: E9 classified Neutral (Gate 1 fail — non-human subjects; Gate 3 fail — apocalyptic).

docs.title: Vocabulary differentiation: Humans devoured by fire
docs.text:
And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.

Context: Same passage as Rev 20:10 — one verse prior. The human armies are the subject of katephagen (devoured), while the devil receives basanisthesontai (tormented) in the next verse.

Notes: katephagen (G2719, katesthio) — Aor Act Ind 3S — 'devoured them.' Different verb from basanizo used for the devil in v.10. Same author (John), same passage, different vocabulary for different subjects. This is the critical vocabulary differentiation datum.

docs.title: Lake of fire IS the second death — predicate nominative formula
docs.text:
And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death. And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.

Context: Conclusion of the white throne judgment. Death and hades are destroyed (cast into the lake). The lake is self-interpreted via the X=Y predicate nominative formula: 'This is (estin) the second death.'

Notes: houtos ho thanatos ho deuteros estin — 'this is the second death.' The predicate nominative formula identifies the lake of fire as death, not as ongoing torment. Death and hades are themselves destroyed in the lake — resulting in 'no more death' (Rev 21:4). Humans cast into the lake (v.15) receive the same fate as death itself — destruction.

docs.title: ECT Argument #3: Everlasting punishment — kolasin aionion vs zoen aionion
docs.text:
Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in: naked, and ye clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not. Then shall they also answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, or athirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister unto thee? Then shall he answer them, saying, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did [it] not to one of the least of these, ye did [it] not to me. And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.

Context: Sheep and goats judgment parable in Matthew 25. The sheep/goats imagery is parabolic (v.32 'as a shepherd divideth'). The fire is 'prepared for the devil and his angels' (v.41) — primary non-human designation.

Notes: Key parsing: kolasin aionion (G2851 + G166, Acc Sg F) vs zoen aionion (G2222 + G166, Acc Sg F) — identical grammatical construction. ECT steelman: same adjective = same duration. Counter-evidence: (1) kolasis means punishment/penalty (from kolazo 'to curtail'), NOT torment — Jesus had basanismos available and chose differently; (2) Hebrews pattern: aionios + result-noun = permanent result of completed act; (3) Tit 1:2 uses aionios twice with different temporal scopes; (4) 2 Thess 1:9 defines eschatological punishment as olethros (destruction). Prior study etc7-14: E13 classified Neutral — both readings grammatically possible.

docs.title: ECT Argument #4: Unquenchable fire and undying worm — quoting Isa 66:24
docs.text:
And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched. And if thy foot offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched. And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.

Context: Jesus' teaching on radical discipleship in Mark 9. The threefold repetition of v.48 (worm dieth not, fire not quenched) is a direct quotation of Isaiah 66:24. Jesus cites the OT source text which identifies the subjects as corpses (peger).

Notes: Mark 9:48 parsing: skolex (G4663, Nom Sg M) — worm; teleutao (G5053, Pres Act Ind 3S) — dies; pyr (G4442, Nom Sg N) — fire; sbennymi (G4570, Pres Pass Ind 3S) — is quenched. The OT source (Isa 66:24) identifies subjects as peger (H6297) — corpses/dead bodies in ALL 24 OT uses. Isa 66:16-17 establishes transgressors were 'slain of the LORD' and 'consumed together' BEFORE the viewing in v.24. 'Unquenchable fire' in Jer 17:27 and Ezek 20:47 historically ended — Jerusalem's gates are not still burning.

docs.title: OT source text for Mark 9:43-48 — subjects are corpses
docs.text:
And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.

Context: Final verse of Isaiah. The redeemed go forth and view the aftermath of God's judgment. The subjects being viewed are identified as peger (corpses/carcasses), not living beings. Isa 66:16-17 establishes the transgressors were already slain and consumed before this viewing.

Notes: Hebrew parsing confirms: peger (H6297, Noun mp Cst) = corpses; tola'at (H8438, Noun fs Abs) = worm acting on corpses; muwth (H4191, Qal Impf 3fs) = die; kabah (H3518, Qal Impf 3fs) = go out/be quenched; dera'on (H1860, Noun ms Abs) = abhorrence/revulsion. The subjects of dera'on are always dead bodies. The worm (tola) is a biological organism feeding on corpses, like maggots on a carcass.

docs.title: Transgressors slain and consumed BEFORE viewing in v.24
docs.text:
For by fire and by his sword will the LORD plead with all flesh: and the slain of the LORD shall be many. They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one [tree] in the midst, eating swine's flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together, saith the LORD.

Context: The verses immediately preceding Isaiah 66:24. They establish the sequence: the transgressors are first slain (v.16) and consumed (v.17), then their corpses are viewed (v.24). Death precedes the dera'on.

Notes: H2491 chalal (slain) — the slain of the LORD. H5486 suph (consumed together) — complete consumption. This sequence is critical: death/consumption BEFORE viewing. The objects of dera'on in v.24 are already dead.

docs.title: ECT Argument #5: Rich man and Lazarus — genre and vocabulary analysis
docs.text:
There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores, And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores. And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried; And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame. But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that [would come] from thence. Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father's house: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment. Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them. And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

Context: Part of Luke's discourse unit beginning at Luke 15:3 (single parabole label). The identical 'certain rich man' formula (anthropos tis plousios) appears at Luke 12:16 (explicit parable label) and Luke 16:1 (universally recognized parable). The climactic teaching point is the sufficiency of Moses and the prophets (vv.29,31).

Notes: Vocabulary: basanos (G931, Dat Pl F) in v.23 — NOT basanizo/basanismos. Different vocabulary register from Revelation's eschatological torment. odunao (G3600, Pres Pass Ind 1S) in v.24 — grief/pain, NOT eschatological torment vocabulary. chasma (G5490) — hapax legomenon (chasm). The passage describes hades (intermediate state), not the final hell/lake of fire. ECT scholars themselves acknowledge this. Same author (Luke) records David is dead and NOT ascended (Acts 2:29,34). Prior study etc7-09: genre classified as parabolic via I-B resolution (Strong).

docs.title: ECT Argument #6: Souls under the altar — apocalyptic vision-figures
docs.text:
And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth? And white robes were given unto every one of them; and it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they [were], should be fulfilled.

Context: Fifth seal in Revelation's seal sequence. Apocalyptic vision — 'I saw' (eidon) introduces the scene. The souls occupy the typological position of sacrificial blood poured at the base of the altar (Lev 4:7).

Notes: The souls are sphazō victims (G4969 — slain/slaughtered), connecting to Abel (1 John 3:12) and the Lamb (Rev 5:6). Their 'cry' follows the forensic personification pattern: Abel's blood cries (Gen 4:10), wages cry (Jas 5:4), the altar itself speaks (Rev 16:7). They are told to 'rest' (anapauō G373) — same vocabulary as Rev 14:13 (blessed dead rest). Rev 20:4-5 identifies the same group and locates their 'living' at the first resurrection. Prior study etc7-10: Tree 3 Gate 1 FAILS (symbolic vision-figures), Gate 3 FAILS (apocalyptic genre). All E-items Neutral or Cond.

docs.title: ECT Argument #7: Everlasting destruction — Paul's explicit definition
docs.text:
And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels, In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power; When he shall come to be glorified in his saints, and to be admired in all them that believe (because our testimony among you was believed) in that day.

Context: Didactic epistle — Paul writing to the Thessalonians. This is a doctrinal statement about eschatological punishment, not apocalyptic imagery or parable.

Notes: Key parsing: olethron aionion (G3639 + G166, Acc Sg M) — 'everlasting destruction.' Paul chose olethros (destruction), NOT basanizo (torment). He had the torment vocabulary available and did not use it. The 'apo prosopou' (G575 + G4383) phrase echoes Isa 2:10,19,21 LXX where divine presence is the destructive AGENT — people hide FROM the destroying presence, not are banished from a location. Psa 68:2 confirms: 'as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.' Prior study etc7-14: E7/E15 classified Cond. — all four Tree 3 gates passed. Didactic epistle.

docs.title: ECT Argument #8: Everlasting contempt — chayyei olam vs dera'on olam
docs.text:
And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame [and] everlasting contempt.

Context: The only OT text explicitly naming two resurrection outcomes. Daniel 12 describes the time of trouble (v.1), resurrection (v.2), reward of the wise (v.3), and Daniel's own rest until the end (v.13).

Notes: Hebrew parsing: chayyei olam (H2416 + H5769) = everlasting life; dera'on olam (H1860 + H5769) = everlasting contempt. Identical olam modification. ECT steelman: if life is genuinely eternal, contempt must be genuinely eternal conscious experience. Counter-evidence: dera'on (H1860) has only 2 OT occurrences — Dan 12:2 and Isa 66:24. In Isa 66:24, the objects of dera'on are peger (corpses). Dera'on describes what transgressors BECOME (objects of revulsion), not what they EXPERIENCE. The nature-of-subject principle governs olam duration. Prior study etc7-14: E15/E17 classified Neutral — ambiguous between experienced shame and observed contempt. I-B resolved Strong toward Cond.

docs.title: Daniel's rest until the resurrection
docs.text:
But go thou thy way till the end [be]: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.

Context: Final verse of Daniel. Daniel is told he will rest (nuwach) then stand (qum) at the end — rest = death, standing = resurrection.

Notes: Parallels Rev 6:11 (rest for a little season) and Rev 14:13 (blessed dead rest). The same concept: death is rest, resurrection is the next event.

docs.title: Vocabulary differentiation: Beast/false prophet vs humans at the lake
docs.text:
And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which [sword] proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.

Context: The battle of Armageddon conclusion. Beast and false prophet are cast into the lake of fire. Humans (the remnant) are slain (apektanthesan) — different verb, different fate, consecutive verses, same author.

Notes: v.20: beast and false prophet 'cast alive' into lake of fire. v.21: humans 'slain' (apektanthesan, G615 apokteino — to kill). The vocabulary differentiation is explicit: non-human symbolic entities enter the lake alive; humans are killed. This pattern continues in Rev 20:9-10.

docs.title: Identical smoke formula applied to Babylon — destruction controls
docs.text:
And again they said, Alleluia. And her smoke rose up for ever and ever.

Context: Heavenly response to Babylon's fall. The identical smoke formula (kapnos anabainei eis tous aionas ton aionon) as Rev 14:11 is applied to Babylon, whose destruction is documented as total and complete in Rev 18:8-23.

Notes: Greek parsing: kapnos (G2586) + anabainei (G305, Pres Act Ind 3S) + eis tous aionas ton aionon (G165 x2). Identical formula to Rev 14:11. Babylon's destruction is explicitly total: fivefold 'found no more at all' in Rev 18 (music, craftsmen, millstone, light, voice of bridegroom). The smoke formula marks permanent destruction, not ongoing torment.

docs.title: Second death defined for human sinners
docs.text:
But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death.

Context: New Jerusalem vision. The list of human sinners (fearful, unbelieving, etc.) whose fate is the lake of fire — which is again identified as 'the second death' (not 'the second torment').

Notes: The lake of fire for human sinners is again called 'the second death' — thanatos (G2288), not basanismos (G929). Same X=Y formula as Rev 20:14.

docs.title: Identical 'day and night' construction — ceaseless praise, not guaranteed eternal duration
docs.text:
And the four beasts had each of them six wings about [him]; and [they were] full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.

Context: Throne room vision. The four living creatures praise God without ceasing. The construction 'ouk echousin anapausin hemeras kai nuktos' is structurally identical to Rev 14:11.

Notes: Greek: anapausin ouk echousin hemeras kai nuktos (G372 + G3756 + G2192 + G2250 + G3571). Identical construction to Rev 14:11. In Rev 4:8, it characterizes the quality of uninterrupted activity, not a guaranteed eternal duration claim. The phrase 'day and night' is a temporal-quality marker.

docs.title: OT source of ages-of-ages smoke formula — Edom's fire historically ended
docs.text:
And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.

Context: Prophecy against Edom. Uses the identical smoke-ascending-forever formula later echoed in Rev 14:11. This fire historically ended — Edom is not still burning.

Notes: Hebrew: le'olam ya'aleh 'ashannah (H5769 + H5927 + H6227) = 'forever ascends its smoke.' The identical formula used in Rev 14:11. But Isa 34:11-17 describes animals dwelling in the ruins — the fire ended. The olam/forever language describes permanent destruction, not ongoing burning.

docs.title: Animals dwell in Edom's ruins — proves the 'forever' fire ended
docs.text:
But the cormorant and the bittern shall possess it; the owl also and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion, and the stones of emptiness. They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none [shall be] there, and all her princes shall be nothing. And thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of dragons, [and] a court for owls. The wild beasts of the desert shall also meet with the wild beasts of the island, and the satyr shall cry to his fellow; the screech owl also shall rest there, and find for herself a place of rest. There shall the great owl make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and gather under her shadow: there shall the vultures also be gathered, every one with her mate. Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them. And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.

Context: Immediately follows Isa 34:9-10 — the 'smoke ascending forever' passage. Animals nesting, dwelling, hatching in the ruins proves the fire and smoke ended.

Notes: The animals that dwell in Edom's ruins are cormorant, bittern, owl, raven, wild beasts, screech owl, great owl, vultures. They 'possess it for ever' (olam) and 'dwell therein' from generation to generation. This is incompatible with still-burning fire. The olam fire produced permanent desolation — the result is eternal, not the process.

docs.title: Satan-figure consumed by fire — cessation vocabulary
docs.text:
Thou hast defiled thy sanctuaries by the multitude of thine iniquities, by the iniquity of thy traffick; therefore will I bring forth a fire from the midst of thee, it shall devour thee, and I will bring thee to ashes upon the earth in the sight of all them that behold thee. All they that know thee among the people shall be astonished at thee: thou shalt be a terror, and never [shalt] thou [be] any more.

Context: Lamentation over the king of Tyre — widely recognized as addressing the supernatural being behind the earthly king (the 'anointed cherub,' v.14). Describes the ultimate fate of the Satan-figure with destruction/cessation vocabulary.

Notes: Hebrew parsing: esh (H784) = fire; akal (H398, Qal Perf 3fs) = devoured; epher (H665, Noun ms Abs) = ashes; ayin (H369, Noun ms Abs) = nothing/non-existence; olam (H5769, Noun ms Abs) = forever. The formula 'ayin + ad-olam' = 'thou art nothing unto forever' — permanent cessation. This describes the same being (Satan-figure) who receives the torment formula in Rev 20:10. The OT describes his end as consumption to ashes and permanent non-existence.

docs.title: Counter-evidence: Wages of sin is death, not torment
docs.text:
For the wages of sin [is] death; but the gift of God [is] eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

Context: Didactic epistle — Paul's summary statement on the consequence of sin. The binary is death (thanatos G2288) vs eternal life (zoe aionios) — not torment vs eternal life.

Notes: thanatos (G2288) — death. Paul's explicit definition of sin's wages. Didactic genre, all Tree 3 gates pass. E-tier Cond.

docs.title: Counter-evidence: God alone has immortality
docs.text:
Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom [be] honour and power everlasting. Amen.

Context: Paul's doxology. Didactic epistle. The statement 'who only hath immortality' (monos echon athanasian) is a direct claim about the exclusivity of divine immortality.

Notes: Greek: monos (G3441, Nom Sg M) echon (G2192, Pres Act Ptcp Nom Sg M) athanasian (G110, Acc Sg F). 'The only one having immortality.' If God alone possesses immortality inherently, humans do not inherently possess it. This undermines the ECT assumption that human souls cannot cease to exist. Immortality is a gift received at resurrection (1 Cor 15:53-54), not an inherent human attribute.

docs.title: Counter-evidence: God able to destroy both soul and body in gehenna
docs.text:
And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

Context: Jesus' teaching to the twelve. Didactic instruction. The verb is apollymi (G622) — destroy — applied to both soul (psyche) and body (soma) in gehenna.

Notes: apollymi (G622) with divine subject in Matthew consistently means actual destruction: Matt 2:13 (Herod seeking to destroy the child), 12:14 (plotting to destroy Jesus), 21:41 (destroy those wicked husbandmen), 22:7 (destroyed those murderers). E-tier Cond.

docs.title: Counter-evidence: The soul that sins shall die
docs.text:
Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.

Context: Ezekiel's theodicy chapter. Didactic prophetic teaching on individual accountability. The nephesh (soul) is mortal — it can die.

Notes: nephesh (H5315) — soul/living being. muwth (H4191) — to die. The soul that sins shall die — not be eternally tormented. Didactic prophetic genre. E-tier Cond.

docs.title: Counter-evidence: Wicked become stubble, burned to ashes
docs.text:
For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch. But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall. And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet in the day that I shall do [this], saith the LORD of hosts.

Context: Malachi's eschatological prophecy. Didactic prophetic teaching on the final judgment. The wicked become stubble, are burned up with neither root nor branch remaining, and become ashes under the feet of the righteous.

Notes: qash (H7179) = stubble; saraph (H8313, Piel Perf) = burn up; epher (H665) = ashes. Complete consumption vocabulary — 'neither root nor branch' indicates total destruction. The righteous tread on ashes — the wicked have been reduced to nothing. Didactic genre. E-tier Cond.

docs.title: Core Gospel binary: Perish vs eternal life
docs.text:
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

Context: Jesus' discourse with Nicodemus. The most fundamental Gospel statement presents the binary as apollymi (perish/be destroyed) vs zoe aionios (eternal life).

Notes: apollymi (G622, Aor Mid Subj 3S) — perish. zoe aionios (G2222 + G166) — everlasting life. The Gospel itself frames the alternative to salvation as perishing/destruction, not eternal conscious torment.

docs.title: Counter-evidence: Sodom turned to ashes as example for ungodly
docs.text:
And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned [them] with an overthrow, making [them] an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;

Context: Peter's argument from historical precedent. Sodom's destruction by fire is explicitly called an 'ensample' (hupodeigma) for the ungodly — meaning the ungodly's fate will be similar.

Notes: tephroo (hapax legomenon) — 'turned to ashes.' hupodeigma — 'example/pattern.' If Sodom is the example of what happens to the ungodly, and Sodom was turned to ashes (not eternally tormented), then the ungodly's fate is destruction, not ECT. Jude 1:7 calls Sodom's fire 'eternal fire' (pyr aionion) — but the fire ended; the result (destruction) is permanent.

docs.title: Aionios used twice with different temporal scopes in same verse
docs.text:
In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;

Context: Paul's letter to Titus. The same adjective aionios appears twice: 'eternal life' (zoes aioniou) and 'before the world began' (pro chronon aionion — literally 'before eternal times').

Notes: Greek parsing: zoes aioniou (G2222 + G166, Gen Sg F) = eternal life; chronon aionion (G5550 + G166, Gen Pl M) = 'eternal times' (KJV: 'before the world began'). The 'eternal times' clearly ended — we are past them. Same adjective, different temporal scope, same verse. This falsifies the claim that aionios always means 'endless.' Duration is determined by subject.

docs.title: Hebrews aionios pattern: Eternal redemption obtained once
docs.text:
Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption [for us].

Context: Hebrews argument about Christ's superior priesthood. 'Eternal redemption' (aionion lytrosis) was obtained 'once' (hapax) — the act is completed, the result is permanent.

Notes: aionion lytrosis — eternal redemption. The adjective modifies the result, not the process. Christ does not eternally keep redeeming; He redeemed once and the result is eternal. Same pattern: eternal judgment (Heb 6:2) = judged once, result permanent; eternal salvation (Heb 5:9) = saved once, result permanent; eternal punishment (Matt 25:46) = punished, result permanent.

docs.title: Forensic personification: Abel's blood cries from the ground
docs.text:
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground.

Context: After Cain murders Abel. Abel's blood 'cries' from the ground — a forensic personification where an inanimate thing (blood) is given speech to demand justice.

Notes: This establishes the forensic personification pattern used in Rev 6:9-11. Abel's blood cries but Abel is dead. The 'souls under the altar' cry but this does not require conscious existence — it follows the same literary convention.

docs.title: Forensic personification: Wages cry out
docs.text:
Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth.

Context: James' condemnation of oppressive rich. Unpaid wages 'cry out' — inanimate objects given voice to demand justice.

Notes: Parallel forensic personification pattern: wages cry (Jas 5:4), blood cries (Gen 4:10), altar speaks (Rev 16:7), souls cry (Rev 6:10).

docs.title: Blessed dead rest — same vocabulary as Rev 6:11
docs.text:
And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed [are] the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.

Context: Immediately following the third angel's message (Rev 14:9-11). The blessed dead 'rest' (anapauo G373) — same vocabulary as the souls under the altar being told to 'rest' (Rev 6:11).

Notes: anapauo (G373) — to rest. Same word family as anapausis (G372) in Rev 14:11. The blessed dead rest (positive), beast-worshippers have no rest (negative). Both use rest vocabulary to describe the state of the dead.

docs.title: Mortal must put on immortality at resurrection
docs.text:
For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal [must] put on immortality. So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.

Context: Paul's resurrection argument. Mortal beings must 'put on' (endyo) immortality — it is not inherently possessed. This occurs at the resurrection.

Notes: thnetos (G2349) = mortal; athanasia (G110) = immortality; endyo (G1746) = put on (as clothing). Humans are mortal. Immortality is a future gift to be received. If the wicked do not receive immortality, they cannot exist forever in torment.

docs.title: Death-state: The dead know not anything
docs.text:
For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.

Context: Solomon's wisdom teaching on death. Didactic genre. The dead have no knowledge, no reward, no memory.

Notes: Death-state didactic passage. Contradicts conscious intermediate state required by ECT's use of Luke 16 and Rev 6:9-11.

docs.title: Death-state: Thoughts perish at death
docs.text:
His breath goeth forth, he returneth to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish.

Context: Psalm about trusting God, not human leaders. At death, a person's thoughts (eshtonah) perish.

Notes: abad (H6) = perish. The same verb used for destruction of the wicked. Thoughts cease at death.

docs.title: David is dead and buried — same author as Luke 16
docs.text:
Men [and] brethren, let me freely speak unto you of the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried, and his sepulchre is with us unto this day.

Context: Peter's Pentecost sermon, recorded by Luke. David is identified as currently dead and buried — not consciously alive somewhere.

Notes: Same author (Luke) who records the parable of the rich man and Lazarus also records Peter's statement that David is dead and buried. Acts 2:34: 'David is NOT ascended into the heavens.'

docs.title: Sodom's 'eternal fire' — fire ended but result permanent
docs.text:
Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.

Context: Jude's argument from historical precedent. Sodom suffered 'eternal fire' (pyr aionion) — but the fire is not still burning. The result (destruction) is permanent.

Notes: pyr aionion (G4442 + G166) — 'eternal fire.' But Peter says Sodom was 'turned to ashes' (2 Pet 2:6). The fire is 'eternal' in result, not in duration. This controls interpretation of 'everlasting fire' in Matt 25:41 and 'eternal fire' throughout the NT.

docs.title: Sodom's destruction: Brimstone, fire, smoke — OT fire-judgment paradigm
docs.text:
Then the LORD rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the LORD out of heaven; And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground. But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt. And Abraham gat up early in the morning to the place where he stood before the LORD: And he looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah, and toward all the land of the plain, and beheld, and, lo, the smoke of the country went up as the smoke of a furnace.

Context: The destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. The foundational OT fire-judgment paradigm. Fire, brimstone, smoke — the same vocabulary later used in Revelation.

Notes: gophrith (H1614) = brimstone; esh (H784) = fire; qiytor (H7008) = smoke. Abraham sees the smoke ascending — same imagery as Isa 34:10 and Rev 14:11. But the cities were destroyed, not eternally burning. Jesus cites Sodom as a destruction paradigm (Luke 17:29).

docs.title: Unquenchable fire on Jerusalem — historically ended
docs.text:
But if ye will not hearken unto me to hallow the sabbath day, and not to bear a burden, even entering in at the gates of Jerusalem on the sabbath day; then will I kindle a fire in the gates thereof, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched.

Context: Jeremiah's warning about Sabbath-breaking. The fire on Jerusalem's gates was called 'unquenchable' — but it ended. Jerusalem's gates are not still burning.

Notes: lo' tikbeh (H3808 + H3518) = 'shall not be quenched.' Same vocabulary as Isa 66:24 and Mark 9:43-48. 'Unquenchable' means irresistible (cannot be put out while it burns), not eternal (never stops burning).

docs.title: Wicked perish at the presence of God — parallels 2 Thess 1:9
docs.text:
As smoke is driven away, [so] drive [them] away: as wax melteth before the fire, [so] let the wicked perish at the presence of God.

Context: David's prayer. The wicked perish 'at the presence' (mippanei) of God — the same prepositional concept as 'from the presence' (apo prosopou) in 2 Thess 1:9.

Notes: abad (H6) = perish; mippanei (H4480 + H6440) = from the face/presence of. The divine presence is the destructive agent, not a location from which one is banished. Wax melts and ceases to be wax when exposed to fire — it does not exist in a perpetual state of melting.

docs.title: LXX parallel for 2 Thess 1:9 'apo prosopou' — hiding FROM destroying presence
docs.text:
Enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty.

Context: Isaiah's prophecy of the Day of the LORD. People hide FROM the Lord's presence — the presence is the source of destruction, not a location of banishment.

Notes: mippanei YHWH (H4480 + H6440 + H3068) = from the face of the LORD. The LXX renders this as apo prosopou tou kyriou — the exact phrase Paul uses in 2 Thess 1:9. In Isaiah, the divine presence destroys; people flee FROM it.

docs.title: Four-fold identification of the devil
docs.text:
And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.

Context: The dragon-identification verse. Four titles: dragon, serpent, Devil, Satan — all identifying the same supernatural being.

Notes: The devil of Rev 20:10 is identified as a supernatural spirit being, not a human. This is critical for the subject-classification of the torment formula.

docs.title: Beast is symbolic — 7 heads and 10 horns
docs.text:
And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.

Context: Introduction of the sea beast. A creature with 7 heads and 10 horns is not a literal individual human being — it is a symbolic political-religious system.

Notes: The beast of Rev 20:10 is a multi-headed symbolic entity, not a human being. This is critical for Gate 1 (subject gate) classification.

docs.title: Olam = 3 days — duration governed by subject
docs.text:
I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars [was] about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O LORD my God.

Context: Jonah's prayer from inside the fish. 'For ever' (olam) describes a period of 3 days — demonstrating olam duration is governed by subject.

Notes: le'olam (H5769) — 'forever.' But Jonah was in the fish for 3 days. Olam does not inherently mean 'endless' — its duration is determined by the nature of the subject.

docs.title: Olam promise explicitly revoked
docs.text:
Wherefore the LORD God of Israel saith, I said indeed [that] thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.

Context: God revokes His olam promise to Eli's house. An olam commitment that was explicitly canceled — proving olam does not inherently mean 'irrevocable' or 'endless.'

Notes: ad-olam (H5704 + H5769) — 'for ever.' Yet God explicitly revokes it: 'but now the LORD saith, Be it far from me.' This is an olam that ended by divine declaration.

docs.title: Complete cessation: As though they had not been
docs.text:
For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, [so] shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.

Context: Obadiah's prophecy against Edom. The wicked will be 'as though they had not been' — complete cessation of existence.

Notes: ka'asher lo' hayu (as though they had not been). Complete non-existence. Cessation vocabulary applied to the fate of the wicked.

docs.title: Utter end — affliction shall not rise up second time
docs.text:
What do ye imagine against the LORD? he will make an utter end: affliction shall not rise up the second time.

Context: Nahum's prophecy. God makes a 'complete end' (kalah) — and the affliction does not recur.

Notes: kalah (H3615) = complete end. The concept of a final, complete destruction that never recurs is consistent with annihilationism but inconsistent with ECT (which by definition never ends).

docs.title: Blood poured at base of altar — typological parallel for Rev 6:9
docs.text:
And the priest shall put [some] of the blood upon the horns of the altar of sweet incense before the LORD, which [is] in the tabernacle of the congregation; and shall pour all the blood of the bullock at the bottom of the altar of the burnt offering, which [is at] the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

Context: Levitical sacrificial instructions. Blood is poured at the bottom/base of the altar — the same position as the 'souls under the altar' in Rev 6:9.

Notes: The souls in Rev 6:9 are 'under the altar' — occupying the typological position of poured-out sacrificial blood. They are vision-figures in a symbolic sacrificial setting, not literal conscious beings trapped under a literal altar.

docs.title: Same martyrs as Rev 6:9-11 — living located at first resurrection
docs.text:
And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and [I saw] the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received [his] mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years. But the rest of the dead lived not again until the thousand years were finished. This [is] the first resurrection.

Context: Millennium scene. The same group described in Rev 6:9-11 (five-link verbal parallel) is shown here 'living' at the first resurrection. Their conscious existence is located at resurrection, not at death.

Notes: ezesan (G2198, Aor Act Ind 3P) = they lived. The martyrs' 'living' occurs at the first resurrection, not at death. This controls interpretation of Rev 6:9-11 — the souls 'under the altar' are not shown as consciously living at death but are vision-figures whose actual living is future.

docs.title: Demons use basanizo — not in didactic teaching
docs.text:
And, behold, they cried out, saying, What have we to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of God? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?

Context: Gadarene demoniac encounter. Demons ask about torment — but this is demonic speech, not Jesus' didactic teaching about human eschatological fate.

Notes: basanizo (G928, Aor Act Inf) — torment. Used by demons, about demons. Not in didactic teaching about human fate. This is the only Gospel occurrence of basanizo in an eschatological context — and it comes from demons, not from Jesus.

docs.title: Pauline eschatology: End is destruction
docs.text:
Whose end [is] destruction, whose God [is their] belly, and [whose] glory [is] in their shame, who mind earthly things.)

Context: Paul describing enemies of the cross. Their 'end' (telos) is 'destruction' (apoleia G684) — not torment.

Notes: apoleia (G684) = destruction/perdition. Paul consistently uses destruction vocabulary for eschatological punishment: olethros (2 Thess 1:9), apoleia (Phil 3:19), thanatos (Rom 6:23). Never basanizo/basanismos.

docs.title: No more death — contradicts eternal dying
docs.text:
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.

Context: New earth description. 'No more death' (thanatos) — death itself is destroyed (Rev 20:14). If death is destroyed, the concept of eternal dying/torment is inconsistent with the new creation reality.

Notes: ouk estai eti (G3756 + G1510 + G2089) = 'shall not be any more.' Death, sorrow, crying, pain — all cease. ECT posits eternal pain and crying continuing forever, which contradicts this promise.

docs.title: Fiery indignation to devour the adversaries
docs.text:
But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.

Context: Hebrews' warning about willful sin. The fire 'devours' (esthio G2068) the adversaries — destruction vocabulary.

Notes: esthio (G2068) = to eat/devour. The adversaries are consumed by the fire, not sustained in it.

docs.title: Jesus cites Sodom as destruction paradigm
docs.text:
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone from heaven, and destroyed [them] all.

Context: Jesus' teaching about the coming of the Son of Man. He cites Sodom as a model — and uses apollymi (destroyed), not basanizo (tormented).

Notes: apollymi (G622, Aor Act Ind 3S) — destroyed them all. Jesus' own vocabulary for Sodom's fate is destruction, not torment.

docs.title: Seeking immortality — implies not already possessed
docs.text:
To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:

Context: Paul on divine judgment. Those who 'seek' (zeteo) immortality receive eternal life. You do not seek what you already possess.

Notes: aphtharsia (G861) = immortality/incorruptibility. The act of seeking implies not yet possessing. If humans already had inherent immortality, seeking it would be meaningless.

docs.title: Paul's logic requires dead NOT conscious
docs.text:
Then they also which are fallen asleep in Christ are perished.

Context: Paul's resurrection argument. If Christ is not raised, then the dead in Christ 'are perished' (apolonto). This only works if the dead are not already consciously in bliss — if they were, the lack of resurrection would be irrelevant.

Notes: apollymi (G622, Aor Mid Ind 3P) — have perished. Paul's entire argument in 1 Cor 15 requires that death is actual death (unconsciousness), not transfer to another conscious state.

docs.title: Wicked shall not be — cessation vocabulary
docs.text:
For yet a little while, and the wicked [shall] not [be]: yea, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it [shall] not [be].

Context: David's wisdom psalm. The wicked cease to exist. Their place is empty.

Notes: ayin (H369) — nothing, non-existence. The wicked and their place simply are not.

docs.title: Wicked shall perish, consume into smoke
docs.text:
But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the LORD [shall be] as the fat of lambs: they shall consume; into smoke shall they consume away.

Context: Continuation of Psalm 37's wisdom teaching. The wicked perish and consume away like smoke — they dissipate into nothing.

Notes: abad (H6) = perish; kalah (H3615) = consume, come to an end; ashan (H6227) = smoke. The smoke imagery parallels Isa 34:10 and Rev 14:11 — but here it clearly means the wicked vanish like dissipating smoke.

docs.title: The altar itself speaks — personification pattern
docs.text:
And I heard another out of the altar say, Even so, Lord God Almighty, true and righteous [are] thy judgments.

Context: Revelation's bowl judgments. The altar itself speaks — inanimate objects given voice in apocalyptic vision.

Notes: The altar speaks in Rev 16:7 just as souls cry from under the altar in Rev 6:10. Both are examples of apocalyptic personification — vision-figures performing literary functions.

docs.title: Aionios + result-noun: Eternal judgment rendered once
docs.text:
Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

Context: List of foundational doctrines. 'Eternal judgment' (krimatsos aioniou) — judgment rendered once with permanent result.

Notes: krimatos aioniou (G2917 + G166) — eternal judgment. The judgment is not eternally in process; it is rendered once and the result is permanent. Same aionios + result-noun pattern as Heb 9:12 and Heb 5:9.

docs.title: Aionios + result-noun: Eternal salvation authored once
docs.text:
And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;

Context: Christ's high priesthood. 'Eternal salvation' — Christ saves once and the result is permanent. He does not perpetually keep saving.

Notes: soterias aioniou (G4991 + G166) — eternal salvation. The pattern is consistent: aionios modifies the permanence of the result, not the duration of the process.

docs.title: Death-state: No remembrance in death
docs.text:
For in death [there is] no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?

Context: David's prayer during illness. In death there is no remembrance and no thanksgiving.

Notes: zeker (H2143) = remembrance. In death there is none. Death-state passage contradicting conscious intermediate state.

docs.title: Death-state: The dead praise not the LORD
docs.text:
The dead praise not the LORD, neither any that go down into silence.

Context: Psalm contrasting the living and the dead. The dead do not praise and go down into silence (dumah).

Notes: dumah (H1745) = silence. The dead go into silence — not into conscious torment or conscious bliss.

docs.title: ECT Argument #3 key verse: Kolasin aionion vs zoen aionion
docs.text:
And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.
