RC3: V1 — destruction vocabulary applies (worm/fire acting on dead bodies = decomposition/consumption agents). Corrected observation: Cond. direction.
  • Result: Gate 1 fails. Corrected observation points toward Neutral (the text describes agents of decomposition acting on dead bodies — this is what the text says, without requiring either position). However, the corrected observation could also be classified Cond. since the subjects are dead.
  • Final classification in etc7-21: Neutral (the text describes what happens to corpses — both sides can accept this as textual fact while disagreeing about whether the imagery implies consciousness or death).

E5 (Luke 16:23-25) — Rich man "in torments" in hades — Classified: Neutral

Source: etc7-09-rich-man-lazarus

  • Step 1 Vocabulary Scan: V2 — basanos (G931) "torments" and odunao (G3600) "grieved/pained." Candidate: ECT-direction.
  • Step 2 Validation Gates:
  • Gate 1 (Subject): The rich man is an allegorical character in a parable. The identical "certain rich man" formula appears at Luke 12:16 (explicit parable label) and 16:1 (universally recognized parable). Luke 15:3 provides single parabole label for the discourse unit. FAIL — allegorical character.
  • Gate 2 (Grammar): basanois (G931, N-DPF) — basanos, NOT basanismos (G929). Different vocabulary register. odunao (G3600) — grief, NOT eschatological torment. Grammar noted but Gate 1 already failed.
  • Gate 3 (Genre): Parabolic — classified as parable via I-B resolution (Strong) from 15+ Plain items against 1 Contextually Clear item. FAIL.
  • Gate 4 (Harmony): Not reached.
  • Step 3 Reclassification: Gates 1 and 3 fail — allegorical character in a parable. RC2: "A parabolic character experiences grief (basanos/odunao) in hades." RC3: Parabolic depiction does not constitute didactic teaching. Neither V1 nor V2 applies at the didactic level.
  • Result: Gates 1 and 3 fail. Classification revised to Neutral.

E6 (Rev 6:9-11) — "Souls of them that were slain... cried with a loud voice" — Classified: Neutral

Source: etc7-10-souls-under-altar

  • Step 1 Vocabulary Scan: V2 — conscious souls speaking, implying survival of death. Candidate: ECT-direction (intermediate state consciousness).
  • Step 2 Validation Gates:
  • Gate 1 (Subject): Vision-figures in apocalyptic scene ("I saw" — eidon). The souls occupy the typological position of sacrificial blood poured at the altar's base (Lev 4:7). The "cry" follows forensic personification (Gen 4:10 — Abel's blood cries; Jas 5:4 — wages cry; Rev 16:7 — altar speaks). FAIL — symbolic vision-figures.
  • Gate 2 (Grammar): Not reached (Gate 1 fail).
  • Gate 3 (Genre): Apocalyptic vision — fifth seal in Revelation's seal sequence. FAIL.
  • Gate 4 (Harmony): Not reached.
  • Step 3 Reclassification: Gates 1 and 3 fail. RC2: "An apocalyptic vision shows symbolic figures (martyrs in sacrificial-blood position) crying for justice — following the forensic personification pattern." RC3: Neither V1 nor V2 applies — vision-figure speech does not establish anthropological teaching.
  • Result: Gates 1 and 3 fail. Classification revised to Neutral.

E7 (2 Thess 1:9) — "Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord" — Classified: Cond.

Source: etc7-14-judgment-passages

  • Step 1 Vocabulary Scan: V1 — olethros (G3639) "destruction" — cessation/ending vocabulary. Candidate: Cond.
  • Step 2 Validation Gates:
  • Gate 1 (Subject): Human sinners — "them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel." Literal humans. PASS.
  • Gate 2 (Grammar): olethron (G3639, N-ASM) aionion (G166, A-ASM) — everlasting destruction. olethros means destruction/ruin in ALL 4 NT occurrences. No alternative parsing removes the destruction meaning. apo prosopou (G575 + G4383) echoes Isa 2:10 LXX — divine presence as destructive agent. PASS.
  • Gate 3 (Genre): Didactic epistle — Paul's doctrinal teaching to Thessalonians. PASS.
  • Gate 4 (Harmony): Consistent with Rom 6:23 (wages = death), Matt 10:28 (destroy soul/body), Ezek 18:4 (soul dies), Mal 4:1-3 (ashes). No conflicting E-items. PASS.
  • Result: All four gates pass. Classification Cond. stands.

E8 (Dan 12:2) — "And some to shame and everlasting contempt" — Classified: Neutral

Source: etc7-14-judgment-passages

  • Step 1 Vocabulary Scan: V2 — dera'on (H1860) "contempt/abhorrence" — could imply ongoing conscious shame. Candidate: ECT. V1 — dera'on linked to corpses in Isa 66:24 could be passive observation. Candidate: Cond. Both triggered.
  • Step 2 Validation Gates:
  • Gate 1 (Subject): "Many of them that sleep in the dust" — resurrected humans. PASS.
  • Gate 2 (Grammar): dera'on olam (H1860 + H5769) parallels chayyei olam (H2416 + H5769). Dera'on has only 2 OT occurrences. In Isa 66:24, the objects of dera'on are peger (corpses). The word is ambiguous between experienced shame and observed contempt. FAIL — alternative parsing valid (experienced vs. observed).
  • Gate 3 (Genre): Didactic prophecy. PASS.
  • Gate 4 (Harmony): Not reached (Gate 2 fail on position, not on tier).
  • Step 3 Reclassification: Gate 2 ambiguity — dera'on could be experienced or observed. RC2: "Resurrected humans receive one of two outcomes: everlasting life or everlasting contempt, where the only other occurrence of dera'on describes a reaction to corpses." RC3: Both V1 and V2 potentially apply. Neither can be established over the other from this verse alone.
  • Result: Gate 2 ambiguity. Classification: Neutral — the text states two outcomes but does not specify whether dera'on is experienced or observed.

docs.title: Counter-Evidence E-Item Classifications (Cond.)
docs.text:
These items passed all four Tree 3 gates in their source studies.

E9 (Rom 6:23) — "The wages of sin is death" — Classified: Cond. - V1: thanatos (G2288) — death vocabulary. Gate 1: human subjects. Gate 2: thanatos unambiguous. Gate 3: didactic epistle. Gate 4: consistent with all other destruction E-items. All gates PASS.

E10 (1 Tim 6:16) — "Who only hath immortality" — Classified: Cond. - V1: monos echon athanasian — "only one having immortality" implies humans lack it. Gate 1: divine attribute with human implication. Gate 2: monos (G3441) = only/alone; grammar unambiguous. Gate 3: didactic epistle. Gate 4: consistent. All gates PASS.

E11 (Matt 10:28) — "Fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell" — Classified: Cond. - V1: apollymi (G622) — destroy vocabulary. Gate 1: human subjects. Gate 2: apollymi with divine subject = actual destruction (Matt 2:13; 12:14; 21:41; 22:7). Gate 3: didactic teaching. Gate 4: consistent. All gates PASS.

E12 (Ezek 18:4) — "The soul that sinneth, it shall die" — Classified: Cond. - V1: muwth (H4191) — death vocabulary. Gate 1: human subjects. Gate 2: nephesh muwth unambiguous. Gate 3: didactic prophecy. Gate 4: consistent. All gates PASS.

E13 (Mal 4:1-3) — "Shall be stubble... burn them up... shall be ashes under the soles of your feet" — Classified: Cond. - V1: saraph (H8313), epher (H665) — burning/ashes/destruction vocabulary. Gate 1: human sinners. Gate 2: "neither root nor branch" — complete. Gate 3: didactic prophecy. Gate 4: consistent. All gates PASS.

E14 (John 3:16) — "Should not perish, but have everlasting life" — Classified: Cond. - V1: apollymi (G622) — perish. Gate 1: human subjects (universal). Gate 2: perish/life antithesis unambiguous. Gate 3: didactic teaching. Gate 4: consistent. All gates PASS.

E15 (2 Pet 2:6) — "Turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes... an ensample" — Classified: Cond. - V1: tephroo (hapax) — turned to ashes. Gate 1: historical cities as example (hupodeigma) for ungodly humans. Gate 2: tephroo unambiguous. Gate 3: didactic epistle. Gate 4: consistent. All gates PASS.

docs.title: Neutral E-Item Classifications
docs.text:
The following E-items were classified Neutral because they are factual observations both sides accept:

E16 (Rev 20:9) — "Fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them" — Neutral - Vocabulary differentiation datum — factual observation about which verb the text uses for human subjects (katephagen, not basanisthesontai).

E17 (Rev 20:14) — "This is the second death" — Neutral - Predicate nominative formula: lake of fire = second death. Textual fact both sides accept.

E18 (Rev 21:8) — "Which is the second death" — Neutral - Restatement of X=Y formula for human sinners.

E19 (Rev 19:20-21) — Vocabulary differentiation between beast/humans — Neutral - Factual observation about different verbs for different subjects.

E20 (Rev 19:3) — Identical smoke formula for Babylon — Neutral - Factual observation about formula usage.

E21 (Rev 4:8) — Identical "no rest day and night" construction — Neutral - Factual observation about shared grammatical construction.

E22 (Isa 34:9-10) — Smoke ascending "for ever" — Neutral - Factual observation about OT usage of the smoke formula.

E23 (Isa 34:11-17) — Animals dwell in ruins — Neutral - Factual observation proving the fire/smoke ended.

E24 (Ezek 28:18-19) — Satan-figure consumed to ashes, "never any more" — Neutral - Factual observation about OT description of the Satan-figure's fate. (Could also be classified Cond. but since it describes a non-human entity, Neutral is appropriate.)

E25 (Tit 1:2) — Same adjective (aionios) used twice with different temporal scopes — Neutral - Grammatical fact both sides must accept.

E26 (Heb 9:12) — "Eternal redemption" obtained once — Neutral - Factual observation about the aionios + result-noun pattern.

E27 (Matt 25:41) — "Everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels" — Neutral - Factual observation about the fire's primary designation.

E28 (Isa 66:16-17) — Transgressors slain and consumed before v.24 viewing — Neutral - Factual observation about the textual sequence.

E29 (Rev 12:9) — Four-fold identification of the devil — Neutral - Factual identification data.

E30 (Rev 13:1) — Beast has 7 heads and 10 horns — Neutral - Factual observation establishing the beast is symbolic.

docs.title: N-Item Classifications
docs.text:
N1 — "If God alone has immortality (E10), and the soul can be destroyed (E11), and the soul that sins dies (E12), then humans do not inherently possess immortality" — Based on: E10, E11, E12 — Classified: Cond.

  • Gate 0 (Foundation):
  • N-Test 1 (Universal agreement): An ECT scholar would not necessarily agree — they would argue "God alone has immortality" means "inherent/underived" immortality, while humans receive derived immortality. FAIL.
  • Result: Gate 0 fails. Reclassified as I-A Cond. — the claim is text-derived and aligns with E/N items, but requires choosing between "inherent" and "any" immortality. Moved to I-tier.

N2 — "Basanismos/basanizo for human eschatological fate appears in zero epistles, zero Gospel teachings, zero OT passages" — Based on: word study data — Classified: Neutral

  • Gate 0 (Foundation):
  • N-Test 1: Both sides can verify this distribution fact. PASS.
  • N-Test 2: This is the only possible conclusion from the distribution data. PASS.
  • N-Test 3: No added concepts — pure vocabulary distribution. PASS.
  • Tree 3 Vocabulary Scan: Neither V1 nor V2 — this is a distributional observation.
  • Result: All gates pass. Classification: Neutral — vocabulary distribution is a factual observation.

N3 — "Destruction/death vocabulary for human eschatological fate spans all genres and all major biblical authors" — Based on: E7, E9, E11, E12, E13, E14, E15 — Classified: Neutral

  • Gate 0: All three N-tests pass — both sides acknowledge these passages use destruction vocabulary.
  • Tree 3: Distributional observation.
  • Result: Neutral — vocabulary distribution is factual.

N4 — "In consecutive verses by the same author, humans receive different verbs than non-human entities at the lake of fire" — Based on: E16, E19 — Classified: Neutral

  • Gate 0: All three N-tests pass — both sides can observe the different verbs.
  • Result: Neutral — textual observation.

N5 — "The 'ages of ages' smoke formula (Isa 34:10) describes a fire that historically ended (Isa 34:11-17 — animals dwell in ruins)" — Based on: E22, E23 — Classified: Neutral

  • Gate 0: All three N-tests pass — both sides can observe that the fire ended and animals dwell there.
  • Result: Neutral — historical/textual observation.

N6 — "Dera'on in its only occurrence with specified objects (Isa 66:24) describes a reaction to corpses (peger), not a conscious experience" — Based on: Isa 66:24 parsing — Classified: Neutral

  • Gate 0:
  • N-Test 1: An ECT scholar could argue the Isa 66:24 usage does not control the Dan 12:2 usage. FAIL.
  • Result: Gate 0 fails. Reclassified as I-A Cond. — text-derived, aligns with E/N, but requires the interpretive step that one occurrence governs another.

N7 — "The lake of fire is self-interpreted as 'the second death' via predicate nominative formula (Rev 20:14)" — Based on: E17 — Classified: Neutral

  • Gate 0: All three N-tests pass — both sides accept the predicate nominative formula. The text says "this is the second death."
  • Result: Neutral — self-interpretation is a textual fact.

Classification audit completed. All positional classifications verified against prior study classifier output.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: 8 key ECT arguments evaluated at E/N/I tier: Rev 14:9-11, Rev 20:10, Matt 25:46, Mark 9:43-48, Luke 16:19-31, Rev 6:9-11, 2 Thess 1:9, Dan 12:2.

docs.title: Summary Answer
docs.text: The 8 passages identified by ECT scholars as the strongest biblical case for eternal conscious torment were evaluated using the Classification Decision Trees (Trees 1-5) and the evidence hierarchy (E > N > I-A > I-B > I-C > I-D). Of the 8 passages, 6 classify as Neutral at E-tier (the text says what it says but does not directly teach ECT due to genre, subject, or vocabulary gate failures), 1 classifies as Cond. at E-tier (2 Thess 1:9 — Paul wrote "everlasting destruction"), and 0 classify as ECT at E-tier. The ECT case for all 8 passages exists entirely at the inference level: 4 at I-B (all resolved toward Cond.), 3 at I-C, and 1 at I-D. Across the 6 primary source studies covering these passages, 62 E-tier Cond. items from didactic passages across multiple genres and authors were identified, against 0 E-tier ECT items.

docs.title: Key Verses
docs.text:
Wages of Sin Is Death (Rom 6:23) For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

God Alone Has Immortality (1 Tim 6:16) Who only hath immortality, dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto; whom no man hath seen, nor can see: to whom be honour and power everlasting. Amen.

Destroy Soul and Body (Matt 10:28) And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

Soul That Sins Dies (Ezek 18:4) Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.

Everlasting Destruction (2 Thess 1:9) Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power.

Perish vs. Eternal Life (John 3:16) For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

Wicked Become Ashes (Mal 4:1-3) For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the LORD of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch... And ye shall tread down the wicked; for they shall be ashes under the soles of your feet.

Sodom as Example (2 Pet 2:6) And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly.

Smoke of Torment (Rev 14:10-11) The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.

Tormented Forever (Rev 20:10) And the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever.

docs.title: The Steelman-and-Evaluate Framework
docs.text:
This study takes each of the 8 passages identified by ECT scholars (Peterson, Burk, Morgan, Block) as the strongest biblical case for eternal conscious torment, presents the ECT argument at its strongest (steelman), identifies the tier of the ECT evidence (E, N, or I), identifies counter-evidence at each tier, and applies the evidence hierarchy (E > N > I-A > I-B > I-C > I-D).

The 8 passages are evaluated in order of their strength as perceived by ECT proponents: Rev 14:9-11, Rev 20:10, Matt 25:46, Mark 9:43-48, Luke 16:19-31, Rev 6:9-11, 2 Thess 1:9, Dan 12:2.

docs.title: ECT Argument #1: Rev 14:9-11 — Smoke of Torment Ascending Forever
docs.text:
Steelman: The third angel warns that beast-worshippers "shall be tormented with fire and brimstone" and "the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night." This passage names human subjects (beast-worshippers), uses torment vocabulary (basanisthesetai, basanismou), and includes an explicit denial of cessation ("no rest day and night"). The language appears to describe ongoing conscious suffering without end.

E/N/I Assessment: The ECT reading of this passage classifies as I-B (Competing-Evidence inference). The passage is apocalyptic genre (Tree 3 Gate 3 fails). Prior study etc7-11 classified E1 as Neutral. The ECT claim requires interpreting apocalyptic torment imagery as didactic teaching about the duration and nature of human eschatological fate.

Counter-Evidence:

At E-tier: basanismos (G929) appears 6 times in the NT, all in Revelation. 4 of 6 occurrences are time-bounded (Rev 9:5 — five months; Rev 18:7,10,15 — Babylon's fall in one hour). The word never appears in any epistle, Gospel teaching, or OT passage. Meanwhile, 20 E-tier Cond. items from didactic passages across 5 authors (Isaiah, Malachi, Jesus, Paul, Peter) use destruction/death vocabulary for human eschatological fate (etc7-11).

The smoke-ascending formula (eis aionas aionon) draws on Isa 34:10, where Edom's smoke "shall go up for ever" — but Isa 34:11-17 describes animals nesting in the ruins. The fire ended. Rev 19:3 uses the identical smoke formula for Babylon, whose destruction is documented as total and complete in Rev 18:8-23 with a fivefold "found no more at all" (music, craftsmen, millstone, light, voice of bridegroom).

The "no rest day and night" (anapausis, G372) construction is structurally identical to Rev 4:8, where the living creatures "rest not day and night" in ceaseless praise. The phrase characterizes the quality of uninterrupted activity, not a guaranteed eternal duration.

Hierarchy Resolution: I-B resolved Strong toward Cond. — 9+ Plain didactic items from multiple genres and authors govern 1 Ambiguous apocalyptic item.

docs.title: ECT Argument #2: Rev 20:10 — Tormented Day and Night Forever
docs.text:
Steelman: The devil, beast, and false prophet "shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever." This is the only verse with the full torment-duration formula. The ECT extension argument: humans cast into the same lake of fire (vv.14-15) share the same experience. Same destination, same outcome.

E/N/I Assessment: The ECT reading classifies as I-B (Competing-Evidence inference). Tree 3 Gate 1 fails — all three subjects are non-human or symbolic: the devil is a supernatural being (Rev 12:9), the beast has 7 heads and 10 horns (Rev 13:1 — a symbolic political-religious system), and the false prophet is the earth beast of Rev 13:11-17. Gate 3 also fails — apocalyptic genre. Prior study etc7-12 classified E9 as Neutral.

Counter-Evidence:

The torment-for-ever formula (basanisthesontai eis tous aionas ton aionon) appears once in all of Scripture — applied only to these three non-human/symbolic entities, never to any human subject.

The text's own vocabulary differentiates between subjects in consecutive verses by the same author: Rev 20:9 — humans are devoured (katephagen, G2719 katesthio); Rev 20:10 — the devil/beast/false prophet are tormented (basanisthesontai, G928). Rev 20:14-15 — the lake is identified as "the second death" (thanatos, G2288), not "the second torment." Rev 21:8 repeats this for human sinners: their part is in the lake "which is the second death."

Ezek 28:18-19 describes the same being (the Satan-figure behind the king of Tyre) with cessation vocabulary: fire devours him, he becomes ashes (epher, H665) on the earth, "never shalt thou be any more" (ayin + ad-olam — permanent non-existence, H369 + H5769).

Hierarchy Resolution: I-B resolved Strong toward Cond. — the text's own vocabulary differentiation (devoured vs. tormented for different subjects in the same passage) governs the extension inference.

docs.title: ECT Argument #3: Matt 25:46 — Everlasting Punishment
docs.text:
Steelman: "These shall go away into everlasting punishment (kolasin aionion): but the righteous into life eternal (zoen aionion)." The same adjective (aionios, G166) modifies both outcomes in identical grammatical construction (Accusative Singular Feminine). If eternal life is genuinely endless, everlasting punishment must be genuinely endless. The parallel demands equal duration.

E/N/I Assessment: The ECT reading classifies as I-B (Competing-Evidence inference). The passage is parabolic (v.32 "as a shepherd divideth" — sheep/goats imagery). Prior study etc7-14 classified E13 as Neutral — both readings are grammatically possible.

Counter-Evidence:

At E-tier: kolasis (G2851) means punishment/penalty, from kolazo (G2849, "to curtail/prune"). Only 2 NT occurrences. Jesus chose kolasis, not basanismos (G929). Different Greek word, different semantic range. kolasis denotes a judicial penalty — the penalty itself, not the experience of being tormented.

The Hebrews pattern: aionios + result-noun = permanent result of completed act. Eternal redemption (Heb 9:12) — obtained once, result permanent. Eternal judgment (Heb 6:2) — rendered once, result permanent. Eternal salvation (Heb 5:9) — authored once, result permanent. By this established pattern, eternal punishment = punished once, result permanent.

Tit 1:2 uses aionios twice in one verse with manifestly different temporal scopes: zoes aioniou (eternal life) and chronon aionion ("eternal times" — which ended; we are past them). Same adjective, same verse, different temporal scope. This falsifies the claim that the same adjective always demands the same duration.

2 Thess 1:9 — in a didactic epistle (all Tree 3 gates pass) — defines eschatological punishment as olethron aionion (everlasting destruction). Paul chose olethros (G3639, destruction), not basanizo (G928, torment). This is the explicit didactic definition of what "everlasting punishment" means: everlasting destruction.

The fire is "prepared for the devil and his angels" (Matt 25:41) — its primary designation is non-human.

Hierarchy Resolution: I-B resolved Strong toward Cond. in etc7-14 (Plain didactic statement governs Ambiguous parabolic statement); Moderate toward Cond. in etc7-21 (Hebrews pattern, kolasis vocabulary, Tit 1:2 datum).

docs.title: ECT Argument #4: Mark 9:43-48 — Unquenchable Fire and Undying Worm
docs.text:
Steelman: Jesus warns of a place where "the fire is not quenched" and "their worm dieth not," implying ongoing conscious suffering that never ends. The threefold repetition emphasizes the unending nature of the torment. Ceaseless destruction agents (fire and worm) acting continuously on subjects suggests the subjects are alive and experiencing it.

E/N/I Assessment: The ECT reading classifies as I-C (Compatible External inference). Mark 9:48 is a direct quotation of Isaiah 66:24. The OT source text identifies the subjects as peger (H6297) — corpses/dead bodies in ALL 24 OT occurrences, never a living person. The ECT reading requires adding consciousness to subjects the OT source text identifies as corpses — adding a concept the text does not state.

Counter-Evidence:

At E-tier: Isa 66:16-17 establishes the transgressors were "slain of the LORD" and "consumed together" before the viewing in v.24. Death precedes the dera'on. The worm (tola, H8438) is a biological organism — a maggot feeding on dead flesh. The worm and fire act on corpses, not on conscious living beings.

"Unquenchable fire" in OT usage: Jer 17:27 — fire on Jerusalem's gates "shall not be quenched" — Jerusalem's gates are not still burning. Ezek 20:47 — unquenchable fire in a forest — the forest is not still burning. "Unquenchable" (lo' tikbeh, same Hebrew vocabulary) means irresistible (cannot be extinguished while burning), not eternal (never stops burning).

katakaio (G2618), Jesus' own verb for the fate of the tares in Matthew's parables, means "burn completely/consume."

Hierarchy Resolution: The ECT reading (I-C) requires adding consciousness to subjects identified as corpses. No I-B resolution is needed because the ECT reading does not have E/N support on both sides — the only specified subjects in the OT source are corpses.

docs.title: ECT Argument #5: Luke 16:19-31 — Rich Man and Lazarus
docs.text:
Steelman: Jesus names a specific person (Lazarus) — unique among parables — suggesting literal narrative. The rich man experiences conscious suffering in flame, with memory, speech, and sensation. If Jesus describes a real person in a real afterlife scenario, this teaches conscious post-mortem existence and suffering.

E/N/I Assessment: The ECT reading classifies as I-C (Compatible External inference). The passage's genre was classified as parabolic via I-B resolution (Strong) in etc7-09 — 15+ Plain items from 8 independent evidentiary lines against 1 Contextually Clear item (the naming of Lazarus). Tree 3 Gate 1 fails (allegorical characters in a parable). Gate 3 fails (parabolic genre).

Counter-Evidence:

At E-tier: The identical "certain rich man" (anthropos tis plousios) formula appears at Luke 12:16 with an explicit parabole label and at Luke 16:1 (universally recognized parable). Luke 15:3 provides a single parabole label covering the discourse unit. The passage uses basanos (G931) and odunao (G3600) — grief vocabulary — not basanizo (G928) or basanismos (G929) — eschatological torment vocabulary. Different word family, different register. The passage describes hades (G86, intermediate state), not the final hell/lake of fire — ECT scholars themselves acknowledge this.

Same author (Luke) records David is "both dead and buried" (Acts 2:29) and "not ascended into the heavens" (Acts 2:34). This is Luke's own theological position on the state of the dead. 7 didactic death-state passages from 6 authors describe the dead as unconscious: Ecc 9:5, Ps 146:4, Ps 6:5, Ps 115:17, Job 14:21, Isa 38:18-19, Ps 30:9. Paul's logic in 1 Cor 15:18 requires the dead not to be in conscious bliss.

The passage's climactic teaching point is the sufficiency of Moses and the prophets (vv.29,31), not afterlife geography.

Hierarchy Resolution: The parabolic genre classification (I-B Strong) means the passage cannot serve as E-tier evidence for either position. The ECT reading (I-C) adds the assumption that parabolic imagery teaches literal afterlife cosmology — a concept the text does not state.

docs.title: ECT Argument #6: Rev 6:9-11 — Souls Under the Altar
docs.text:
Steelman: These souls are conscious, speaking, and aware of time passing — proving the soul survives death in a conscious state. If souls are conscious between death and resurrection, they could also be conscious in hell. This passage provides the anthropological foundation that ECT requires: that the soul is inherently immortal and conscious after death.

E/N/I Assessment: The ECT reading classifies as I-C (Compatible External inference). Tree 3 Gate 1 fails — the souls are symbolic vision-figures in an apocalyptic scene ("I saw" — eidon), not literal humans. Gate 3 fails — apocalyptic genre, not didactic teaching.

Counter-Evidence:

At E-tier: The souls occupy the typological position of sacrificial blood poured at the base of the altar (Lev 4:7,18,25,30,34). Their "cry" follows the forensic personification pattern: Abel's blood cries (Gen 4:10), wages cry (Jas 5:4), the altar itself speaks (Rev 16:7). The sphazo (G4969) vocabulary chain links these slaughter victims to Abel (1 John 3:12) and the Lamb (Rev 5:6).

Rev 20:4-5 identifies the same group (five-link verbal parallel: souls, beheaded/slain, word of God, testimony, beast/mark) and locates their "living" (ezesan, G2198) at the first resurrection. Their conscious existence is placed at resurrection, not at death.

The "rest" (anapauo, G373) command parallels Rev 14:13 (blessed dead rest from labors) and Dan 12:13 (Daniel rests, then stands at the end). In all three, rest = the state of death before resurrection.

1 Tim 6:16 states God alone has immortality. Matt 10:28 states God can destroy the soul. Ezek 18:4 states the soul that sins dies. The ECT framework assumes inherent soul immortality — the biblical data contradicts this assumption.

Hierarchy Resolution: The ECT reading (I-C) requires treating apocalyptic vision as literal anthropological teaching — adding a framework the text does not state. No E/N items support ECT.

docs.title: ECT Argument #7: 2 Thess 1:9 — Everlasting Destruction
docs.text:
Steelman: "Everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord" means ongoing ruin or separation from God, not cessation of existence. "Destruction" (olethros) can mean an ongoing ruinous state, and "from the presence" (apo prosopou) means banishment from God's presence, not annihilation caused by it.

E/N/I Assessment: The ECT reading of 2 Thess 1:9 classifies as I-D (Counter-Evidence External inference). This passage is the one E-tier Cond. item among the 8 passages — all four Tree 3 gates pass (didactic epistle, human subjects, unambiguous grammar, consistent with other E-items). The ECT reading requires redefining olethros from its lexical meaning ("destruction") to "ongoing conscious ruin" — overriding what the word means.

Counter-Evidence:

At E-tier: olethros (G3639) means destruction/ruin in ALL 4 NT occurrences (1 Cor 5:5; 1 Thess 5:3; 2 Thess 1:9; 1 Tim 6:9). No lexicon defines olethros as torment. KJV renders uniformly as "destruction." Paul had basanizo (torment) available in his vocabulary and chose olethros (destruction). The word choice is deliberate.

The "apo prosopou tou kyriou" phrase ("from the presence of the Lord") echoes Isa 2:10,19,21 LXX, where the divine presence is the destructive agent — people hide FROM the destroying presence. They are not banished from a location; they flee the source of destruction. Psa 68:2 confirms: "as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God." The wax metaphor: wax melts and ceases to be wax when exposed to fire. It does not exist in a perpetual state of melting.

Hierarchy Resolution: The ECT reading (I-D) requires overriding the lexical meaning of olethros and reversing the directional meaning of apo prosopou. The I-D classification reflects the heaviest burden of proof in the evidence hierarchy.

docs.title: ECT Argument #8: Dan 12:2 — Everlasting Contempt
docs.text:
Steelman: "Everlasting life" (chayyei olam) and "everlasting contempt" (dera'on olam) use identical olam modification in parallel grammatical construction. If life is genuinely eternal, contempt must be genuinely eternal conscious experience. The parallelism demands equal duration and equal experiential nature.

E/N/I Assessment: The ECT reading classifies as I-B (Competing-Evidence inference). Prior study etc7-14 classified E15/E17 as Neutral — ambiguous between experienced shame and observed contempt.

Counter-Evidence:

At E-tier: dera'on (H1860) has only 2 OT occurrences: Dan 12:2 and Isa 66:24. In Isa 66:24, the objects of dera'on are peger (H6297) — corpses. Peger means dead body in ALL 24 OT uses. Dera'on describes what the transgressors become (objects of visceral revulsion), not what they experience — because the objects are dead bodies that cannot experience anything.

olam duration is governed by the nature-of-subject principle: olam spans from 3 days (Jonah 2:6) to genuinely eternal (Psa 90:2). Ended institutions labeled olam include circumcision, Levitical priesthood, and land promises. An olam promise was explicitly revoked (1 Sam 2:30). olam fire/smoke judgments historically ended (Isa 34:10 — animals dwell in ruins; Jer 17:27 — Jerusalem's gates not still burning). Life for those who receive immortality is genuinely eternal (subject = immortal being). Contempt for those who are dead is a permanent result (subject = corpse) — the state of being abhorrent continues permanently, but the corpse does not experience it.

Hierarchy Resolution: I-B resolved Strong toward Cond. — the only occurrence of dera'on with specified objects (Isa 66:24 = corpses) governs the occurrence without specified objects (Dan 12:2). Plain SIS application.

docs.title: Cross-Cutting Pattern: Vocabulary Differentiation
docs.text:
Across the 8 passages, a decisive vocabulary pattern emerges:

Torment vocabulary (basanizo G928 / basanismos G929) for human eschatological fate: Zero epistles. Zero Gospel teachings. Zero OT passages. All eschatological judgment uses are confined to Revelation's apocalyptic framework. The only Gospel occurrence of basanizo in an eschatological context (Matt 8:29) is demonic speech, not Jesus' teaching. Luke 16 uses basanos/odunao (grief vocabulary), not basanizo/basanismos. Matt 25:46 uses kolasis (punishment), not basanismos (torment).

Destruction/death vocabulary for human eschatological fate: Spans all genres and all major biblical authors — Jesus (apollymi — Matt 10:28, John 3:16; katakaio — Matt 13:30,40), Paul (thanatos — Rom 6:23; olethros — 2 Thess 1:9; apoleia — Phil 3:19), Peter (tephroo — 2 Pet 2:6), Hebrews author (esthio — Heb 10:27), Isaiah (chalal/suph — Isa 66:16-17), Malachi (epher — Mal 4:3), Ezekiel (muwth + nephesh — Ezek 18:4), Psalms (abad/kalah/ayin — Psa 37:10,20; 68:2).

Vocabulary differentiation at the lake of fire: In every passage where humans and non-human entities appear together at the lake of fire, different verbs are used for different subjects: Rev 19:20-21 (beast/false prophet cast alive into lake; humans slain — apektanthesan, G615). Rev 20:9-10 (humans devoured — katephagen, G2719; devil tormented — basanisthesontai, G928). Rev 20:14-15 (lake = second death — thanatos, G2288; humans cast into = receive death).

This vocabulary differentiation is a textual fact observable in the Greek — it does not require interpretation, framework, or theological position. The same author (John), writing in the same passage, uses different verbs for different subjects in consecutive verses.

docs.title: Cross-Cutting Pattern: Duration Vocabulary
docs.text:
The ECT duration argument depends on the claim that aionios/olam always means "endless." The evidence shows:

olam (H5769) spans from 3 days (Jonah 2:6) to genuinely eternal (Psa 90:2). It derives from alam (H5956, "to conceal") — time whose endpoint is hidden, not time without endpoint. 20+ ended institutions are labeled olam. An olam promise was explicitly revoked (1 Sam 2:30). Fire/smoke called olam historically ended (Isa 34:10 — animals dwell in ruins).

aionios (G166) has three past-time uses (Rom 16:25; 2 Tim 1:9; Tit 1:2) where the "eternal times" have ended. Tit 1:2 uses aionios twice in one verse with different temporal scopes — "eternal life" (zoes aioniou) and "before eternal times" (pro chronon aionion). The "eternal times" ended; we are past them. aidios (G126) exists as the strict "everduring" word — derived from aei ("always"), meaning continuous unbroken duration. The NT authors chose not to use aidios for eschatological punishment.

The Hebrews pattern (aionios + result-noun = permanent result of completed act) controls interpretation of Matt 25:46: eternal punishment = punished once, result permanent — not punished endlessly.

The "ages of ages" formula (eis tous aionas ton aionon) appears 21 times in the NT: 19 doxological (praise to God), 2 judgment uses (Rev 14:11 smoke, Rev 20:10 torment). Both judgment uses are in Revelation's apocalyptic framework for non-human/symbolic entities.

docs.title: Cross-Cutting Pattern: Conditional Immortality
docs.text:
The ECT framework requires the assumption that human souls are inherently immortal — if humans cannot cease to exist, the wicked must exist forever in some state, making ECT the default. The biblical evidence on immortality:

1 Tim 6:16: God alone (monos) has immortality (athanasia, G110). Only 3 NT occurrences of athanasia — applied to God (1 Tim 6:16) and to believers at resurrection (1 Cor 15:53-54). Never applied to inherent human nature.

Rom 2:7: Believers "seek for... immortality (aphtharsia, G861)." Seeking implies not possessing. 1 Cor 15:53-54: "This mortal (thnetos, G2349) must put on immortality (athanasia)." Humans are mortal; immortality is received at resurrection.

Matt 10:28: God is able to "destroy (apollymi, G622) both soul (psyche) and body in gehenna." If the soul can be destroyed, it is not inherently immortal.

Ezek 18:4: "The soul (nephesh) that sinneth, it shall die (muwth)." The soul is mortal.

The wicked are never said to receive immortality. If they do not receive it, they cannot exist forever.

docs.title: Word Studies
docs.text:
basanismos (G929) — 6 NT occurrences, ALL in Revelation. 4 of 6 time-bounded. Zero epistles, zero Gospel teachings, zero OT. Its exclusive confinement to Revelation's apocalyptic framework is the single most important vocabulary datum: if torment vocabulary for human eschatological fate existed in didactic genres, it would be E-tier ECT evidence. Its absence at the didactic level is decisive.

basanizo (G928) — 12 NT occurrences. The torment-for-ever formula (basanisthesontai eis tous aionas ton aionon) appears once — Rev 20:10 — applied only to non-human/symbolic entities.

kolasis (G2851) — 2 NT occurrences. Punishment/penalty from kolazo ("to curtail"). Jesus chose kolasis, not basanismos, in Matt 25:46.

olethros (G3639) — 4 NT occurrences, all Pauline. Destruction. Paul's chosen word for eschatological punishment (2 Thess 1:9). No lexicon defines it as torment.

apollymi (G622) — 102 NT occurrences. Destroy/perish. Jesus' word for what God does to the wicked (Matt 10:28). Core Gospel binary: perish vs. eternal life (John 3:16).

aionios (G166) — 71 NT occurrences. Duration determined by subject. Three past-time uses. Tit 1:2 dual-scope in same verse. Hebrews pattern: permanent result of completed act.

dera'on (H1860) — 2 OT occurrences. Contempt/abhorrence. In Isa 66:24, applied to corpses (peger). Describes what transgressors become, not what they experience.

peger (H6297) — 24 OT occurrences. Always means dead body/corpse. The subjects of Mark 9:48 / Isa 66:24 are corpses.

athanasia (G110) — 3 NT occurrences. Immortality. God alone has it (1 Tim 6:16). Believers receive it at resurrection (1 Cor 15:53-54). Never applied to inherent human nature.

docs.title: Rev 14:9-11: Human Subjects with Torment Language
docs.text:
This is the passage that applies torment vocabulary to human subjects (beast-worshippers) in an eschatological context. The text says basanisthesetai ("he shall be tormented") and "they have no rest day and night." The difficulty is real: torment vocabulary is applied to humans, not just to the devil/beast/false prophet.

The genre gate (apocalyptic) and the OT source of the smoke formula (Isa 34:10 — ended fire), the identical formula applied to Babylon's total destruction (Rev 19:3), and the identical "day and night" construction in Rev 4:8 (quality marker, not duration guarantee) address this difficulty. But the passage remains the ECT argument closest to E-tier status — prevented only by the apocalyptic genre gate.

docs.title: Matt 25:46: The Parallel Construction
docs.text:
The surface-level parallel (kolasin aionion // zoen aionion) is a genuine exegetical consideration. The natural reading of the same adjective modifying two parallel outcomes in identical grammatical construction is that both have the same temporal scope. The conditionalist must explain why the same adjective does not demand the same duration.

The answer involves: (1) the Hebrews aionios + result-noun pattern, (2) the Tit 1:2 dual-scope datum, (3) the kolasis vocabulary (punishment, not torment), and (4) the nature-of-subject principle. Both sides agree the righteous receive genuine eternal life. The question is whether aionios modifies the process of punishment (ongoing punishing) or the result (punishment inflicted, result permanent). The Hebrews pattern supports the latter.

docs.title: Rev 20:10: Extension to Humans
docs.text: The "same lake = same experience" inference has surface plausibility. If the devil is tormented in the lake and humans are thrown into the same lake, the inference that both experience the same thing is natural. The text's vocabulary differentiation (devoured vs. tormented in consecutive verses) addresses this, but the inference remains a consideration.

Must interpret apocalyptic imagery as didactic teaching about duration; must choose between the ended-fire reading (Isa 34:10) and the ongoing-torment reading; must ignore the identical formula applied to total destruction (Rev 19:3). #2 (choosing between readings), #3 (applying ECT framework to apocalyptic genre), #5 (systematizing) ECT I091 I2 Rev 20:10's torment formula extends to humans who are cast into the same lake of fire I-B E2: Devil/beast/false prophet are tormented for ever (Rev 20:10). The text uses different verbs for different subjects in the same passage. Must infer that "same destination = same experience" despite the text's explicit vocabulary differentiation between subjects. #1 (adding equivalence of experience the text does not state), #2 (choosing between "same experience" and "same category of judgment with different results"), #5 (systematizing) ECT I069 I3 Matt 25:46 teaches that eschatological punishment is endless conscious torment I-B E3: "Everlasting punishment" and "life eternal" use the same adjective in identical construction (Matt 25:46). Must choose between "same adjective = same duration" and "aionios modifies the result, not the process." Must choose between kolasis-as-ongoing-torment and kolasis-as-permanent-penalty. docs.title: I-B Resolution: I1 — Rev 14:11 Teaches Ongoing Conscious Torment
docs.text:
Step 1 — Tension: - FOR (ECT): E1 (Rev 14:10-11 — basanisthesetai, smoke of torment ascending, no rest day and night) - AGAINST (Cond.): E9 (wages of sin is death), E13 (wicked become ashes), E14 (perish vs. eternal life), E15 (Sodom turned to ashes as example), E7 (everlasting destruction — 2 Thess 1:9), E22/E23 (Isa 34:10 smoke formula for ended fire), E20 (identical formula for Babylon's total destruction), E21 (identical "day and night" construction in Rev 4:8)

Step 2 — Clarity Assessment:

Item Level Rationale E1 Ambiguous Apocalyptic genre; the identical smoke formula in Isa 34:10 describes an ended fire; the identical "day and night" phrase in Rev 4:8 is a quality marker E9 Plain Didactic epistle; directly states wages of sin = death; no interpretation needed E13 Plain Didactic prophecy; directly states wicked become ashes; complete destruction vocabulary E14 Plain Jesus' didactic teaching; perish vs. eternal life binary E15 Plain Didactic epistle; Sodom turned to ashes as example for ungodly E7 Plain Didactic epistle; everlasting destruction; all Tree 3 gates pass E22/E23 Contextually Clear OT prophecy with historical verification; requires knowing Edom's history E20 Contextually Clear Requires connecting Rev 19:3 formula to Rev 18 total-destruction documentation

Step 3 — Weight: 5 Plain items and 2 Contextually Clear items on the Cond. side govern 1 Ambiguous item on the ECT side.

Step 4 — SIS Application: The Plain didactic statements from multiple authors (Paul — Rom 6:23; Jesus — John 3:16; Malachi — Mal 4:1-3; Peter — 2 Pet 2:6; Paul — 2 Thess 1:9) determine the reading of the Ambiguous apocalyptic imagery in Rev 14:11. The clear interprets the unclear.

Step 5 — Resolution: Strong toward Cond. Plain statements from 5 authors in didactic genres govern 1 Ambiguous statement in apocalyptic genre.

Step 4 — SIS Application: The text's own vocabulary differentiation in consecutive verses determines the reading. The same author uses different verbs for different subjects — this is the text interpreting itself.

docs.text:
Step 1 — Tension: - FOR (ECT): E3 (everlasting punishment / life eternal with same adjective, identical construction, Matt 25:46) - AGAINST (Cond.): E7 (everlasting destruction, 2 Thess 1:9), E25 (Tit 1:2 dual-scope), E26 (Hebrews aionios + result-noun pattern), E9 (wages = death), E13 (ashes), E14 (perish vs. life)

Step 2 — Clarity Assessment:

Item Level Rationale E3 Ambiguous Parabolic genre; kolasis means punishment, not torment; both readings grammatically possible E7 Plain Didactic epistle; olethros = destruction; all gates pass E25 Plain Same adjective, manifestly different temporal scope, same verse — directly falsifies "same adjective = same duration" E26 Contextually Clear Requires recognizing the Hebrews pattern across multiple verses E9 Plain Wages = death, not torment E13 Plain Ashes, not ongoing torment

Step 3 — Weight: 4 Plain items and 1 Contextually Clear item govern 1 Ambiguous item.

Step 4 — SIS Application: The Plain didactic statement in 2 Thess 1:9 defines eschatological punishment as destruction. The Tit 1:2 datum directly falsifies the "same adjective = same duration" argument. These clear passages determine the reading of the Ambiguous parabolic statement.

docs.text:
Step 1 — Tension: - FOR (ECT): E8 (dera'on olam — everlasting contempt, parallel to chayyei olam, Dan 12:2) - AGAINST (Cond.): E29 (dera'on in Isa 66:24 describes reaction to peger = corpses), E28 (transgressors slain and consumed before viewing in Isa 66:24), olam duration is subject-determined (Jonah 2:6 = 3 days; 1 Sam 2:30 = revoked)

Step 2 — Clarity Assessment:

Item Level Rationale E8 Ambiguous Dera'on has only 2 OT occurrences; the word itself is ambiguous between experienced and observed E29 Plain Isa 66:24 specifies the objects as peger (corpses) — always dead body in 24/24 OT uses E28 Contextually Clear Requires reading Isa 66:16-17 before v.24 to establish the death-before-viewing sequence

Step 4 — SIS Application: The only occurrence of dera'on with specified objects (Isa 66:24 = corpses) governs the occurrence without specified objects (Dan 12:2). This is standard SIS: the clear passage interprets the unclear.

Full Tree 3/4 walkthroughs for each item were performed in the source studies by classifier subagents with actual parser tool output. The compiled results are documented in CLASSIFICATIONS.md in this study folder.

docs.title: What CAN Be Said
docs.text:
Scripture explicitly states or necessarily implies:

  • The wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23) — didactic epistle, E-tier
  • God alone has immortality (1 Tim 6:16) — didactic epistle, E-tier
  • God is able to destroy both soul and body in gehenna (Matt 10:28) — Jesus' teaching, E-tier
  • The soul that sins shall die (Ezek 18:4) — didactic prophecy, E-tier
  • The wicked become ashes (Mal 4:1-3) — didactic prophecy, E-tier
  • The alternative to eternal life is perishing (John 3:16) — Jesus' teaching, E-tier
  • Paul defines eschatological punishment as everlasting destruction (2 Thess 1:9) — didactic epistle, E-tier
  • Sodom was turned to ashes as an example for the ungodly (2 Pet 2:6) — didactic epistle, E-tier
  • The lake of fire is the second death (Rev 20:14) — self-interpreted via predicate nominative
  • Humans receive different verbs (devoured, slain, second death) than non-human entities (tormented) at the lake of fire (Rev 19-21) — textual observation
  • The "ages of ages" smoke formula in Isa 34:10 describes a fire that historically ended (Isa 34:11-17) — historical observation
  • Basanismos/basanizo for human eschatological fate appears in zero epistles, zero Gospel teachings, zero OT — vocabulary distribution
  • Destruction/death vocabulary for the wicked spans all genres and all major authors — vocabulary distribution

docs.title: What CANNOT Be Said
docs.text:
The following claims are not explicitly stated or necessarily implied by Scripture:

  • "The Bible explicitly teaches that the wicked experience eternal conscious torment" — no verse states this after passing all four Tree 3 gates. The ECT case exists entirely at the inference level.
  • "Rev 14:11 proves ECT" — the passage is apocalyptic (Gate 3 fail); the identical smoke formula in Isa 34:10 describes an ended fire.
  • "Rev 20:10 proves ECT for humans" — the three subjects are non-human/symbolic (Gate 1 fail); the text uses different verbs for humans.
  • "Matt 25:46 proves ECT" — kolasis means punishment (not torment); both readings are grammatically possible; the Hebrews pattern and Tit 1:2 datum address the parallel-duration argument.
  • "Luke 16 is a literal description of the afterlife" — genre classified as parabolic (Strong); even ECT scholars acknowledge it describes hades, not final hell.
  • "Rev 6:9-11 proves inherent soul immortality" — apocalyptic vision-figures following forensic personification pattern; living located at first resurrection (Rev 20:4-5).
  • "2 Thess 1:9 teaches ongoing ruin, not destruction" — this reading requires redefining olethros from its lexical meaning (I-D).
  • "The Bible explicitly teaches that the wicked are annihilated" — the word "annihilate" does not appear in Scripture. The Bible uses destruction, death, perishing, ashes, and cessation vocabulary. Annihilation is an I-A systematization of multiple E-items.
  • "Destruction vocabulary proves conditionalism" — the vocabulary distribution is Neutral (both sides accept it). The doctrinal conclusion is an I-A inference (Cond.) from that distribution.
  • "The soul is inherently immortal" — no biblical text states this. athanasia is applied to God (1 Tim 6:16) and to believers at resurrection (1 Cor 15:53-54), never to inherent human nature.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The 8 passages identified by ECT scholars as the strongest biblical case produce the following evidence pattern when classified mechanically using the Decision Trees:

Six of the 8 passages classify as Neutral at E-tier because of gate failures: Rev 14:9-11 (Gate 3 — apocalyptic genre), Rev 20:10 (Gate 1 — non-human subjects; Gate 3 — apocalyptic), Matt 25:46 (Gate 2 — both readings grammatically possible; Gate 3 — parabolic), Mark 9:43-48 (Gate 1 — subjects are corpses per OT source), Luke 16:19-31 (Gate 1 — allegorical character; Gate 3 — parabolic), Rev 6:9-11 (Gate 1 — symbolic vision-figures; Gate 3 — apocalyptic).

One passage classifies as Cond. at E-tier: 2 Thess 1:9. Paul wrote olethron aionion (everlasting destruction) in a didactic epistle. All four Tree 3 gates pass. Paul had basanizo (torment) available and chose olethros (destruction).

One passage classifies as Neutral at E-tier with ambiguity: Dan 12:2. Dera'on is ambiguous between experienced shame and observed contempt. The I-B resolution (the only occurrence with specified objects — corpses — governs) resolves Strong toward Cond.

Zero passages classify as ECT at E-tier. The ECT case for all 8 passages exists entirely at the inference level: I-B (4, all resolved Strong toward Cond.), I-C (3), I-D (2).

The vocabulary evidence confirms this pattern. Torment vocabulary (basanizo/basanismos) for human eschatological fate appears in zero epistles, zero Gospel teachings, zero OT passages — only in Revelation's apocalyptic framework or demonic speech. Destruction/death vocabulary spans all genres and all major biblical authors. At the lake of fire, the text itself differentiates: humans are devoured (Rev 20:9), slain (Rev 19:21), and receive the second death (Rev 20:14-15, 21:8). Non-human/symbolic entities are tormented (Rev 20:10). Different verbs, different subjects, consecutive verses, same author.

The evidence hierarchy (E > N > I) governs interpretation. With 9 E-tier Cond. items from didactic sources and 0 E-tier ECT items, the ECT position lacks evidence above the inference level. The conditionalist position has E-tier support from Jesus (Matt 10:28, John 3:16), Paul (Rom 6:23, 2 Thess 1:9, Phil 3:19), Peter (2 Pet 2:6), Ezekiel (18:4), and Malachi (4:1-3) — all in didactic genres, all passing Tree 3 gates.

docs.title: Primary Verses (28 — full analysis required)
docs.text:
8 ECT primary passages: The 8 passages being steelmanned and evaluated — retrieve with full chapter context - Rev 14:9-11 — ECT argument #1 — smoke of torment ascending forever and ever; primary ECT passage - Rev 20:10 — ECT argument #2 — tormented day and night forever and ever; devil/beast/false prophet - Mark 9:43-48 — ECT argument #4 — unquenchable fire, worm not dying; quotes Isa 66:24 - Luke 16:19-31 — ECT argument #5 — rich man and Lazarus; genre and vocabulary analysis - Rev 6:9-11 — ECT argument #6 — souls under the altar; apocalyptic vision-figures - 2 Thess 1:7-10 — ECT argument #7 — olethron aionion; Paul chose destruction not torment - Dan 12:2 — ECT argument #8 — dera'on olam; everlasting contempt; linked to Isa 66:24 corpses

Counter-evidence passages: Key conditionalist passages providing counter-evidence at E-tier - Rom 6:23 — Counter-evidence — wages of sin is death (thanatos), not torment - 1 Tim 6:16 — Counter-evidence — God alone has immortality (athanasia) - Matt 10:28 — Counter-evidence — destroy (apollymi) both soul and body in gehenna - Ezek 18:4 — Counter-evidence — the soul (nephesh) that sins shall die (muwth) - Mal 4:1-3 — Counter-evidence — wicked become stubble, burned to ashes (epher) - John 3:16 — Perish (apollymi) vs eternal life — core Gospel binary is destruction vs life - 2 Pet 2:6 — Counter-evidence — Sodom turned to ashes (tephroo), example for ungodly

OT fire-judgment paradigms: OT passages establishing the ended-fire pattern — retrieve with full chapter context - Ezek 28:18-19 — Satan-figure consumed by fire, becomes ashes, never shall be any more (ayin + olam)

Vocabulary differentiation passages: Passages showing the distinction between torment vocabulary (non-human/apocalyptic) and destruction vocabulary (human/didactic) - Rev 19:20-21 — Vocabulary differentiation — beast/false prophet cast in lake vs humans slain (apektanthesan) - Rev 20:9 — Same context — humans devoured (katephagen), different verb from tormented - Rev 20:14-15 — Lake of fire IS the second death — X=Y predicate nominative formula - Rev 21:8 — Second death defined for human sinners — lake of fire vocabulary - Rev 4:8 — Identical 'day and night' construction as Rev 14:11 — characterizes quality, not guaranteed duration

Duration/aionios pattern passages: Passages demonstrating aionios/olam semantic range and the nature-of-subject principle - Tit 1:2 — Aionios used twice with different temporal scopes in same verse — falsifies 'same adjective = same duration' - Heb 9:12 — Hebrews aionios + result-noun pattern — eternal redemption obtained once

Additional Primary Verses: - Rev 19:3 — Identical smoke formula applied to Babylon — controls interpretation of Rev 14:11 - Matt 25:41 — Fire prepared for the devil and his angels — primary non-human designation - Matt 25:46 — ECT argument #3 — kolasin aionion vs zoen aionion; punishment vs life - Isa 66:24 — Source text for Mark 9:43-48 — subjects are peger (corpses), not living beings - Isa 34:9-10 — OT source of ages-of-ages smoke formula — Edom fire historically ended - Isa 34:11-17 — Animals dwell in Edom's ruins — proves fire/smoke ended

docs.title: Focus Areas
docs.text:
1. Rev 14:9-11 — Smoke ascending forever: ECT or destruction imagery?: This is the ECT passage most laypeople cite. The steelman case: the plain language says 'torment ascendeth up for ever and ever' with 'no rest day and night.' READ $WORD_STUDIES/G929-basanismos.md for all 6 NT occurrences — note that 4 of 6 are time-bounded. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G372-anapausis.md for the 'no rest day and night' construction. Run greek_parser.py on Rev 14:9-11, Rev 19:3, Rev 4:8. The critical counter-evidence: the identical smoke formula in Isa 34:10 describes Edom's fire — which ended, with animals dwelling in the ruins (Isa 34:11-17). Rev 19:3 uses the same smoke formula for Babylon, whose destruction is documented as total and complete (Rev 18:8-23, fivefold 'found no more at all'). READ grammar reference $GRAMMAR_REF/passages/rev-14-8-11.md for the passage-level grammatical analysis. Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py --hybrid-ot on Rev 14:11 to find OT parallels. The research agent should retrieve full chapter context for Rev 14 and Isa 34. Verses: Rev 14:9-11, Rev 19:3, Isa 34:9-10, Isa 34:11-17, Rev 4:8, Rev 18:8-23 Strong's: G929, G372, G2586, G165

  2. Rev 20:10 — Tormented forever: Who are the subjects?: The strongest ECT reading: the ages-of-ages torment formula represents the ultimate eschatological punishment, and humans thrown into the same lake of fire share the same experience. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G928-basanizo.md and $WORD_STUDIES/G928-basanízō.md — note the 12 NT occurrences and their distribution. READ grammar reference $GRAMMAR_REF/passages/rev-20-7-15.md for passage-level analysis. Run greek_parser.py on Rev 20:9-15 to expose the vocabulary differentiation between subjects in consecutive verses. The critical datum: the torment-for-ever formula (basanisthesontai eis tous aionas ton aionon) appears ONCE in all of Scripture — applied only to devil/beast/false prophet, never to any human. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G2618-katakaio.md for the verb Jesus uses for human destruction. Compare Ezek 28:18-19 for the Satan-figure's own destruction described with cessation vocabulary. Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py --hybrid-ot on Rev 20:10. Verses: Rev 20:10, Rev 20:9, Rev 20:14-15, Rev 19:20-21, Rev 21:8, Ezek 28:18-19 Strong's: G928, G929, G2618, G2719

  3. Matt 25:46 — Everlasting punishment: Kolasis vs basanismos: The ECT steelman: 'everlasting punishment' and 'eternal life' use the same adjective (aionios) with the same grammatical construction, so the duration must be identical — if life is endless, punishment must be endless. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G2851-kolasis.md for the etymology (from kolazo, 'to curtail') and both NT occurrences. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G166-aionios.md for the full aionios semantic range. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G3639-olethros.md — Paul's explicit definition of eschatological punishment is destruction. Run greek_parser.py on Matt 25:41-46 and 2 Thess 1:9. The key counter-evidence: (1) kolasis means punishment/penalty, NOT torment — Jesus had basanismos available and chose a different word; (2) the Hebrews pattern shows aionios + result-noun = permanent result of completed act; (3) Tit 1:2 uses aionios twice in one verse with manifestly different temporal scopes. Retrieve full chapter context for Matt 25. Verses: Matt 25:41-46, 2 Thess 1:9, Heb 9:12, Heb 6:2, Heb 5:9, Tit 1:2 Strong's: G2851, G166, G3639, G2849

  4. Mark 9:43-48 — Unquenchable fire and undying worm: Isa 66:24 source analysis: The ECT steelman: Jesus warns of a place where 'the fire is not quenched' and 'the worm dieth not,' implying ongoing conscious suffering that never ends. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H6297-peger.md for all 24 OT occurrences — peger always means dead body/corpse, never a living person. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H8438-tôwlâʻ.md for the worm that acts on corpses. Run hebrew_parser.py on Isa 66:24 and retrieve Isa 66:16-17 which establishes the transgressors were 'slain of the LORD' and 'consumed together' BEFORE the viewing in v.24. Check 'unquenchable fire' in Jer 17:27 (Jerusalem's gates are not still burning) and Ezek 20:47. Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py --hybrid-ot on Mark 9:48. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G1067-geenna.md for the gehenna semantic range. Retrieve full chapter context for Isa 66 and Mark 9. Verses: Mark 9:43-48, Isa 66:24, Isa 66:16-17, Jer 17:27, Ezek 20:47 Strong's: H6297, H8438, G1067, G762

  5. Luke 16:19-31 — Rich man and Lazarus: Genre classification and vocabulary analysis: The ECT steelman: Jesus names a specific person (Lazarus) — unique among parables — suggesting literal narrative, and the rich man's conscious suffering in flame is presented as factual post-mortem reality. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G931-basanos.md for Luke 16's grief vocabulary. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G3600-odynao.md — this is NOT the same word family as Revelation's torment vocabulary. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G5490-chásma.md (chasma, hapax legomenon). Run greek_parser.py on Luke 16:19-31. The counter-evidence: (1) the identical 'certain rich man' formula appears at Luke 12:16 (explicit parable label) and 16:1 (universally recognized parable); (2) Luke 15:3 provides a single parabole label covering the discourse unit; (3) the climactic teaching point is sufficiency of Moses and prophets (vv.29,31), not afterlife geography; (4) same author (Luke) records David is dead and NOT ascended (Acts 2:29,34); (5) ECT scholars themselves acknowledge this describes hades (intermediate state), not final hell. Retrieve full chapter context for Luke 15-16. Verses: Luke 16:19-31, Luke 12:16, Luke 16:1, Luke 15:3, Acts 2:29, Acts 2:34 Strong's: G931, G3600, G5490, G86

  6. Rev 6:9-11 — Souls under the altar: Apocalyptic vision or anthropological teaching?: The ECT steelman: these souls are conscious, speaking, and aware of time passing — proving the soul survives death in a conscious state. If souls are conscious between death and resurrection, they could also be conscious in hell. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G5590-psyche.md for nephesh/psyche semantic range (does psyche require conscious entity?). READ $WORD_STUDIES/G4969-sphazo.md for the sphazō vocabulary chain. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G373-anapauo.md for the 'rest' command and its parallel in Rev 14:13 and Dan 12:13. The counter-evidence: (1) Tree 3 Gate 1 FAILS — symbolic vision-figures, not literal humans; (2) Gate 3 FAILS — apocalyptic genre, not didactic teaching; (3) the souls occupy the typological position of sacrificial blood poured at the base of the altar (Lev 4:7,18,25,30,34); (4) the 'cry' follows the forensic personification pattern where inanimate things cry; (5) Rev 20:4-5 identifies the same group and locates their 'living' at the first resurrection. Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py --hybrid-ot on Rev 6:9. Verses: Rev 6:9-11, Gen 4:10, Jas 5:4, Rev 20:4-5, Lev 4:7, Rev 14:13 Strong's: G5590, G4969, G373, G372

  7. 2 Thess 1:7-10 — Everlasting destruction: Paul's explicit definition of eschatological punishment: The ECT steelman: 'everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord' means ongoing ruin/separation from God, not cessation of existence. 'Destruction' can mean ongoing ruinous state, and 'from the presence' means banishment, not annihilation by the presence. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G3639-olethros.md — note that olethros means destruction/ruin in ALL 4 NT occurrences and no lexicon defines it as torment. Run greek_parser.py on 2 Thess 1:7-10. The critical evidence: Paul had basanizo (torment) available in his vocabulary and chose olethros (destruction) — the word choice is deliberate. The 'apo prosopou tou kyriou' phrase echoes Isa 2:10,19,21 LXX where the divine presence is the destructive AGENT (people hide FROM the destroying presence), not a location from which one is banished. Psa 68:2 confirms: 'as wax melteth before the fire, so let the wicked perish at the presence of God.' Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py --hybrid-ot on 2 Thess 1:9. Retrieve full chapter context for 2 Thess 1. Verses: 2 Thess 1:7-10, Isa 2:10, Isa 2:19, Isa 2:21, Psa 68:2 Strong's: G3639, G684, G622

  8. Dan 12:2 — Everlasting contempt: Conscious shame or observed revulsion at corpses?: The ECT steelman: 'everlasting life' and 'everlasting contempt' are grammatically parallel with identical olam modification, so if life is genuinely eternal, contempt must be genuinely eternal conscious experience. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H1860-draown.md for both occurrences and their semantic context. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H5769-owlam.md for the full olam semantic range (spans from 3 days to genuinely eternal). READ $WORD_STUDIES/H6297-peger.md — the objects of dera'on in Isa 66:24 are always dead bodies. Run hebrew_parser.py on Dan 12:2 and Isa 66:24. The critical datum: dera'on describes what the transgressors BECOME (objects of visceral revulsion), not what they EXPERIENCE — because in Isa 66:24 they are corpses. The nature-of-subject principle governs olam duration: life for those who receive immortality is genuinely eternal; contempt for those who are dead is a permanent result, not an ongoing experience. Run cross_testament_parallels_v2.py --hybrid-ot on Dan 12:2. Verses: Dan 12:2, Isa 66:24, Dan 12:13, Isa 66:16-17 Strong's: H1860, H5769, H6297, H5956

  9. Cross-cutting theme: Vocabulary differentiation — torment vs destruction vocabulary across genres: This is the cross-cutting analysis that ties all 8 passages together. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G928-basanizo.md and $WORD_STUDIES/G929-basanismos.md for torment vocabulary distribution. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G622-apollymi.md for destruction vocabulary. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G684-apoleia.md for perdition/destruction. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G2288-thanatos.md for death vocabulary. READ $WORD_STUDIES/WG-death.md for the death word group overview. The pattern from prior studies: basanizo/basanismos for human eschatological fate appears in zero epistles, zero Gospel teachings, zero OT passages — only in Revelation's apocalyptic framework or demonic speech (Matt 8:29). Meanwhile, destruction/death vocabulary spans Jesus, Paul, Peter, Hebrews author, Isaiah, Malachi, the Psalms — all genres, all major authors. Run search_strongs.py --verses on G928 and G929 to verify distribution. This vocabulary differentiation is the strongest single piece of evidence in the debate. Verses: Matt 10:28, John 3:16, Rom 6:23, Phil 3:19, Heb 10:27, 2 Pet 2:6, Mal 4:1-3 Strong's: G928, G929, G622, G684, G3639, G2288

  10. Cross-cutting theme: Duration vocabulary — aionios/olam semantic range and the nature-of-subject principle: The ECT steelman: 'everlasting' means everlasting. If the same adjective modifies both 'life' and 'punishment,' the duration must be identical. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H5769-owlam.md for the full olam study — note ended institutions labeled olam (circumcision, Levitical priesthood, Sabbath, land promises), explicitly revoked olam promises (1 Sam 2:30), and fire/smoke judgments called olam that historically ended (Isa 34:10, Jer 17:27). READ $WORD_STUDIES/G166-aionios.md for the 71 NT occurrences — three past-time uses (Rom 16:25, 2 Tim 1:9, Tit 1:2), Tit 1:2 dual-scope in same verse. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G126-aidios.md — this is the strict 'everduring' word, distinct from aionios. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G165-aion.md for the etymological root. READ $WORD_STUDIES/WG-forever.md for the word group overview. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H5956-alam.md for the root meaning 'to conceal.' The nature-of-subject principle: olam/aionios + inherently permanent subject = genuinely eternal; olam/aionios + finite/perishable subject = as long as the subject's nature permits. Run search_strongs.py --verses on G166 to verify distribution patterns. Verses: Tit 1:2, Heb 9:12, Heb 6:2, Heb 5:9, Jonah 2:6, 1 Sam 2:30, Jude 1:7 Strong's: G166, G126, G165, H5769, H5956

  11. Cross-cutting theme: Conditional immortality — Does the Bible teach inherent human immortality?: The ECT framework assumes immortal souls: if humans cannot cease to exist, then the wicked must exist forever in some state, making ECT the default. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G110-athanasia.md — only 3 NT occurrences, applied to God and to believers at resurrection, never to inherent human nature. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G861-aphtharsia.md and $WORD_STUDIES/G862-aphthartos.md for the incorruptibility word family. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G5590-psyche.md and $WORD_STUDIES/H5315-nephesh.md for the soul/nephesh semantic range — both are mortal. READ $WORD_STUDIES/WG-soul.md for the word group overview. READ $WORD_STUDIES/G2349-thnetos.md for the mortal/mortality vocabulary. The key texts: 1 Tim 6:16 (God alone has immortality), Ezek 18:4 (the soul that sins shall die), Matt 10:28 (God able to destroy soul and body), Rom 2:7 (seeking immortality — you don't seek what you already have), 1 Cor 15:53-54 (mortal must put on immortality — at resurrection). Run search_strongs.py --verses on G110. Verses: 1 Tim 6:16, Ezek 18:4, Matt 10:28, Rom 2:7, 1 Cor 15:53-54, Rom 6:23 Strong's: G110, G861, G862, G5590, H5315, G2349

  12. Cross-cutting theme: OT fire-judgment paradigms — Sodom, Edom, and the ended-fire pattern: The OT fire-judgment paradigm is critical for interpreting NT apocalyptic fire language. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H784-esh.md for fire vocabulary. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H665-epher.md for ashes vocabulary. READ $WORD_STUDIES/H6227-ashan.md and $WORD_STUDIES/H6225-ashan.md for smoke vocabulary. READ $WORD_STUDIES/WG-smoke.md for the smoke word group. Run hebrew_parser.py on Isa 34:9-10 and Gen 19:24. Key pattern: Sodom is described as destroyed by 'eternal fire' (Jude 1:7 — pyr aionion) yet Peter says Sodom was 'turned to ashes' (2 Pet 2:6 — tephroo, hapax legomenon) as an 'example' (hupodeigma) for the ungodly. Edom's 'smoke ascending up for ever' (Isa 34:10) uses the identical formula as Rev 14:11, yet animals dwell in the ruins (Isa 34:11-17). Retrieve full chapter context for Isa 34 and 2 Pet 2. docs.title: Synthesis Study Methodology
docs.text:
This is a SYNTHESIS study — do NOT re-derive what prior etc7 studies already established. Instead:

  1. READ prior study conclusions: The 00-references.md document compiles E/N/I classifications from 13 prior studies. Start from those established findings.

  2. Steelman each ECT argument: For each of the 8 passages, present the STRONGEST possible ECT reading before evaluating it. Cite actual ECT scholars (Peterson, Burk, Morgan, Block) where the prior studies reference their arguments.

  3. Evaluate at E/N/I tier: Apply Tree 3 classification to each ECT argument. The prior studies have already done this — verify and compile their results.

  4. Cross-reference counter-evidence: For each ECT argument, identify the specific E-tier and N-tier counter-evidence that governs interpretation.

  5. Map the overall pattern: The unique contribution of this synthesis is showing that ALL 8 passages follow the same pattern: ECT reading exists at inference level only, while conditionalist counter-evidence exists at E-tier across multiple genres and authors.

docs.title: The 8 Strongest Arguments for Eternal Torment — What Does the Bible Actually Say?
docs.text: Scholars who believe in eternal conscious torment (ECT) point to 8 key passages as their strongest biblical evidence. This study examined each one to determine what the text explicitly states versus what must be inferred.

docs.title: The Core Finding
docs.text: Of the 8 passages, none explicitly teach eternal conscious torment when read on their own terms. Six are neutral (the text can be read either way), one actually supports conditional destruction, and one is ambiguous but resolved by its Old Testament source. Meanwhile, at least 9 clear, straightforward passages from teaching portions of Scripture describe the fate of the wicked as death, destruction, and perishing.

docs.title: The 8 Passages Examined
docs.text:
Revelation 14:9-11 — "Smoke of their torment ascends forever." This is apocalyptic vision language. The same "smoke ascending forever" phrase comes from Isaiah 34:10 describing Edom's destruction — a fire that ended long ago (animals now live in the ruins). The identical formula describes Babylon's total destruction in Revelation 19:3.

Revelation 20:10 — "Tormented day and night forever." The subjects are the devil, the beast (a seven-headed symbolic creature), and the false prophet — not humans. When humans appear in the very next verses, different words are used: humans are "devoured" (v.9) and receive "the second death" (vv.14-15). Same author, consecutive verses, different verbs for different subjects.

Matthew 25:46 — "Everlasting punishment." Jesus used the word kolasis (penalty), not basanismos (torment). Paul defined this penalty in plain language: "everlasting destruction" (2 Thessalonians 1:9). The word "everlasting" modifies the result, not the process — just as "eternal redemption" (Hebrews 9:12) means redeemed once with a permanent result, not an ongoing act of redeeming.

Mark 9:43-48 — "The worm does not die, the fire is not quenched." Jesus was quoting Isaiah 66:24, where the subjects are explicitly corpses — dead bodies, not living people. "Unquenchable fire" in the Old Testament means fire that cannot be put out while burning (Jeremiah 17:27 — Jerusalem's gates are not still on fire).

Luke 16:19-31 — The Rich Man and Lazarus. This is a parable, using the same "a certain rich man" formula found in other recognized parables (Luke 12:16, 16:1). It describes hades (the intermediate state), not the final judgment. Even ECT scholars acknowledge this. The story's point is the sufficiency of Scripture (vv.29, 31), not afterlife geography.

Revelation 6:9-11 — Souls under the altar. These are symbolic vision-figures in an apocalyptic scene, occupying the position of sacrificial blood poured at the altar's base. Their "cry" follows the same pattern as Abel's blood crying out (Genesis 4:10) — a literary device, not proof of conscious disembodied existence.

2 Thessalonians 1:9 — "Everlasting destruction." This is the one passage among the eight that passes every test for clear, direct teaching — and it says destruction, not torment. Paul had the word for "torment" available and chose "destruction" instead.

Daniel 12:2 — "Everlasting contempt." The only other use of the Hebrew word dera'on is Isaiah 66:24, where it describes the reaction of onlookers viewing corpses. The contempt is what the dead become (objects of revulsion), not what they experience.

docs.title: The Vocabulary Pattern
docs.text: This may be the most telling evidence of all. Words for torment applied to human final judgment appear in zero letters, zero Gospel teachings, and zero Old Testament passages — only in Revelation's symbolic visions. Words for death, destruction, and perishing appear across every genre and every major biblical author: Jesus, Paul, Peter, Ezekiel, Malachi, and the Psalms.

docs.title: Key Verses
docs.text:
• Romans 6:23 — "The wages of sin is death."
  • 1 Timothy 6:16 — "God alone has immortality."
  • Matthew 10:28 — God "is able to destroy both soul and body in hell."
  • Ezekiel 18:4 — "The soul that sins, it shall die."
  • John 3:16 — "Should not perish, but have everlasting life."
  • Malachi 4:1-3 — The wicked "shall be ashes under the soles of your feet."
  • 2 Thessalonians 1:9 — "Punished with everlasting destruction."

docs.title: The Bottom Line
docs.text:
The case for eternal conscious torment depends entirely on inference — reading assumptions into apocalyptic imagery, parables, and ambiguous phrases. The case for conditional destruction rests on direct, plainly worded statements from teaching passages across the entire Bible. When clear passages and unclear passages point in different directions, the clear interprets the unclear.

docs.title: Cross-Testament Parallels
docs.text:
• Rev 14:11 → Isa 34:10 (ot, vocabulary + structural — identical smoke-ascending-forever formula; OT source for NT apocalyptic imagery. Edom's fire ended (animals dwell in ruins, Isa 34:11-17))
  • Rev 20:10 → Isa 34:10 (ot, vocabulary — 'forever' fire/smoke language; both use olam/aionios duration formula for fires that ended)
  • Rev 20:10 → Ezek 28:18-19 (ot, subject + thematic — same being (Satan-figure); OT describes with cessation vocabulary (ashes, never any more), Rev uses torment vocabulary. Competing portrayals of same entity's fate)
  • Mark 9:48 → Isa 66:24 (ot, direct quotation — Mark 9:48 quotes Isa 66:24. OT source identifies subjects as peger (corpses). Worm and fire act on dead bodies.)
  • 2 Thess 1:9 → Isa 2:10 (ot, vocabulary — 'apo prosopou' (from the presence/face) phrase. In Isa 2:10,19,21 LXX, the divine presence is the destructive agent. People flee FROM the destroying presence.)
  • 2 Thess 1:9 → Psa 68:2 (ot, thematic — 'wicked perish at the presence of God.' Divine presence as destructive agent, not banishment location.)
  • Rev 6:9 → Gen 4:10 (ot, forensic personification pattern — Abel's blood cries from the ground; souls cry from under the altar. Inanimate/dead things given voice to demand justice.)
  • Rev 6:9 → Lev 4:7 (ot, typological — sacrificial blood poured at base of altar; souls positioned under the altar. Altar-base = position of poured-out blood.)
  • Matt 25:46 → Dan 12:2 (ot, structural — dual-outcome judgment formula. Both use 'eternal' + contrasting outcomes. Dan 12:2 links to Isa 66:24 via dera'on.)
  • Rev 19:3 → Isa 34:10 (ot, vocabulary — identical smoke formula. Babylon's smoke ascends forever; Edom's smoke ascends forever. Both destructions were total.)
